न तत्र सूर्यः प्रविभातीह चन्द्रो
न नक्षत्राणि तपनो नोत विद्युत् ।
तद्भासेदमखिलं भाति नित्यं
तन्नित्यभासमचलं सद्विभाति ॥
2.10.m: There the sun does not shine, nor here the moon, / nor stars, nor fire, nor lightning; / by his light all this shines constantly; / that eternal light, immovable, exists shining.

2.10.s:
nityoditaṃ saṃvidā nirvikalpaṃ
śuddhaṃ bṛhantaṃ paramaṃ yadvibhāti /
atrāntaraṃ brahmavido 'tha nityaṃ
paśyanti tattvamacalaṃ yat sa īśaḥ //
2.10.d:
नित्योदितं संविदा निर्विकल्पं
शुद्धं बृहन्तं परमं यद्विभाति ।
अत्रान्तरं ब्रह्मविदो ऽथ नित्यं
पश्यन्ति तत्त्वमचलं यत् स ईशः ॥
2.10.m: Eternally risen, non-conceptual through consciousness, / pure, vast, supreme, which shines forth— / within this the knowers of Brahman constantly / behold the immovable reality, which is the Lord.

2.10.s:
nityānandamamṛtaṃ satyarūpaṃ
śuddhaṃ vadanti puruṣaṃ sarvavedāḥ /
tadevedamiti praṇaveneśitāraṃ
dhāyāyanti vedārthaviniścitārthāḥ //
2.10.d:
नित्यानन्दममृतं सत्यरूपं
शुद्धं वदन्ति पुरुषं सर्ववेदाः ।
तदेवेदमिति प्रणवेनेशितारं
धायायन्ति वेदार्थविनिश्चितार्थाः ॥
2.10.m: Eternally blissful, immortal, whose nature is truth, / pure, all the Vedas proclaim the Puruṣa; / thinking "That alone is this," by the Praṇava / those whose purpose is determined by the Vedic meaning meditate on the Ruler.

2.10.s:
na bhūmirāpo na mano na vahniḥ
prāṇo 'nilo gaganaṃ nota buddhiḥ /
na cetano 'nyat paramākāśamadhye
vibhāti devaḥ śiva eva kevalaḥ //
2.10.d:
न भूमिरापो न मनो न वह्निः
प्राणो ऽनिलो गगनं नोत बुद्धिः ।
न चेतनो ऽन्यत् परमाकाशमध्ये
विभाति देवः शिव एव केवलः ॥
2.10.m: Neither earth, nor waters, nor mind, nor fire, / nor breath, nor wind, nor ether, nor intellect; / nor any other conscious being in the midst of supreme space— / God alone, Śiva, shines.

2.10.s:
ityetaduktaṃ paramaṃ rahasyaṃ
jñānāmṛtaṃ sarvavedeṣu gūḍham /
jānāti yogī vijane 'tha deśe
yuñjīta yogaṃ prayato hyajasram //
itī śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge (īśvaragītāsu) daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.10.d:
इत्येतदुक्तं परमं रहस्यं
ज्ञानामृतं सर्ववेदेषु गूढम् ।
जानाति योगी विजने ऽथ देशे
युञ्जीत योगं प्रयतो ह्यजस्रम् ॥
इती श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे (ईश्वरगीतासु) दशमो ऽध्यायः
2.10.m:
Thus this supreme secret has been spoken, / the nectar of knowledge hidden in all the Vedas; / the yogin who knows it should, in a solitary place, / practice yoga constantly, with self-restraint.

Thus ends the tenth chapter in the latter section (in the Īśvaragītā) of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the holy Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.11.s:
īśvara uvāca
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yogaṃ paramadurlabham /
yenātmānaṃ prapaśyanti bhānumantamiveśvaram //
2.11.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योगं परमदुर्लभम् ।
येनात्मानं प्रपश्यन्ति भानुमन्तमिवेश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m:
The Lord said:
Hereafter I shall proclaim yoga, supreme and exceedingly difficult to attain, / by which they behold the Self, the Lord, like the shining sun.

2.11.s:
yogāgnirdahati kṣipramaśeṣaṃ pāpapañjaram /
prasannaṃ jāyate jñānaṃ sākṣānnirvāṇasiddhidam //
2.11.d:
योगाग्निर्दहति क्षिप्रमशेषं पापपञ्जरम् ।
प्रसन्नं जायते ज्ञानं साक्षान्निर्वाणसिद्धिदम् ॥
2.11.m: The fire of yoga swiftly burns the entire cage of sins; / serene knowledge arises, directly granting the perfection of extinction.

2.11.s:
yogātsaṃjāyate jñānaṃ jñānād yogaḥ pravartate /
yogajñānābhiyuktasya prasīdati maheśvaraḥ //
2.11.d:
योगात्संजायते ज्ञानं ज्ञानाद् योगः प्रवर्तते ।
योगज्ञानाभियुक्तस्य प्रसीदति महेश्वरः ॥
2.11.m: From yoga arises knowledge; from knowledge yoga proceeds; / toward one endowed with yoga and knowledge, the Great Lord is gracious.

2.11.s:
ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ nityameva vā /
ye yuñjantīha madyogaṃ te vijñeyā maheśvarāḥ //
2.11.d:
एककालं द्विकालं वा त्रिकालं नित्यमेव वा ।
ये युञ्जन्तीह मद्योगं ते विज्ञेया महेश्वराः ॥
2.11.m: Once a day, or twice, or thrice, or constantly, / those who here practice my yoga are to be known as great lords.

2.11.s:
yogastu dvividho jñeyo hyabhāvaḥ prathamo mataḥ /
aparastu mahāyogaḥ sarvayogottamottamaḥ //
2.11.d:
योगस्तु द्विविधो ज्ञेयो ह्यभावः प्रथमो मतः ।
अपरस्तु महायोगः सर्वयोगोत्तमोत्तमः ॥
2.11.m: Yoga, however, is to be known as two-fold: the yoga of non-existence is considered the first, / and the other is the Great Yoga, the highest among all yogas.

2.11.s:
śūnyaṃ sarvanirābhāsaṃ svarūpaṃ yatra cintyate /
abhāvayogaḥ sa prokto yenātmānaṃ prapaśyati //
2.11.d:
शून्यं सर्वनिराभासं स्वरूपं यत्र चिन्त्यते ।
अभावयोगः स प्रोक्तो येनात्मानं प्रपश्यति ॥
2.11.m: Where one's own nature is meditated upon as void, devoid of all appearance, / that is declared to be the yoga of non-existence, by which one beholds the Self.

2.11.s:
yatra paśyati cātmānaṃ nityānandaṃ nirañjanam /
mayaikyaṃ sa mahāyogo bhāṣitaḥ parameśvaraḥ //
2.11.d:
यत्र पश्यति चात्मानं नित्यानन्दं निरञ्जनम् ।
मयैक्यं स महायोगो भाषितः परमेश्वरः ॥
2.11.m: And where one beholds the Self as eternal bliss, stainless, / united with me—that is declared to be the Great Yoga, the Supreme Lord.

2.11.s:
ye cānye yogināṃ yogāḥ śrūyante granthavistare /
sarve te brahmayogasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
2.11.d:
ये चान्ये योगिनां योगाः श्रूयन्ते ग्रन्थविस्तरे ।
सर्वे ते ब्रह्मयोगस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
2.11.m: And whatever other yogas of yogins are heard in the extensive treatises, / all of them are not worth a sixteenth part of the yoga of Brahman.

2.11.s:
yatra sākṣāt prapaśyanti vimuktā viśvamīśvaram /
sarveṣāmeva yogānāṃ sa yogaḥ paramo mataḥ //
2.11.d:
यत्र साक्षात् प्रपश्यन्ति विमुक्ता विश्वमीश्वरम् ।
सर्वेषामेव योगानां स योगः परमो मतः ॥
2.11.m: Where the liberated directly behold the universe as the Lord, / of all yogas that yoga is considered supreme.

2.11.s:
sahasraśo 'tha śataśo ye ceśvarabahiṣkṛtāḥ /
na te paśyanti māmekaṃ yogino yatamānasāḥ //
2.11.d:
सहस्रशो ऽथ शतशो ये चेश्वरबहिष्कृताः ।
न ते पश्यन्ति मामेकं योगिनो यतमानसाः ॥
2.11.m: By hundreds and thousands, those who are excluded from the Lord, / even as yogins with controlled minds, do not behold me, the One.

2.11.s:
prāṇāyāmastathā dhyānaṃ pratyāhāro 'tha dhāraṇā /
samādhiśca muniśreṣṭhā yamo niyama āsanam //
2.11.d:
प्राणायामस्तथा ध्यानं प्रत्याहारो ऽथ धारणा ।
समाधिश्च मुनिश्रेष्ठा यमो नियम आसनम् ॥
2.11.m: Breath control, as well as meditation, sensory withdrawal, and concentration, / and absorption, O best of sages, restraint, observance, posture—

2.11.s:
mayyekacittatāyogo vṛttyantaranirodhataḥ /
tatsādhanānyaṣṭadhā tu yuṣmākaṃ kathitāni tu //
2.11.d:
मय्येकचित्ततायोगो वृत्त्यन्तरनिरोधतः ।
तत्साधनान्यष्टधा तु युष्माकं कथितानि तु ॥
2.11.m: Yoga is single-mindedness upon me through the cessation of other mental activities; / its eightfold means have indeed been spoken to you.

2.11.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryāparigrahau /
yamāḥ saṃkṣepataḥ proktāścittaśuddhipradā nṛṇām //
2.11.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहौ ।
यमाः संक्षेपतः प्रोक्ताश्चित्तशुद्धिप्रदा नृणाम् ॥
2.11.m: Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possession: / these are briefly declared to be the restraints, granting purity of mind to mortals.

2.11.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā sarvabhūteṣu sarvadā /
akleśajananaṃ proktaṃ tvahiṃsā paramarṣibhiḥ //
2.11.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा सर्वभूतेषु सर्वदा ।
अक्लेशजननं प्रोक्तं त्वहिंसा परमर्षिभिः ॥
2.11.m: By action, thought, or speech toward all beings at all times, / causing no affliction is declared by the supreme rṣis to be non-violence.

2.11.s:
ahiṃsāyāḥ paro dharmo nāstyahiṃsā paraṃ sukham /
vidhinā yā bhaveddhiṃsā tvahiṃsaiva prakīrtitā //
2.11.d:
अहिंसायाः परो धर्मो नास्त्यहिंसा परं सुखम् ।
विधिना या भवेद्धिंसा त्वहिंसैव प्रकीर्तिता ॥
2.11.m: There is no duty higher than non-violence; non-violence is the supreme happiness; / violence which is performed according to injunction is celebrated as non-violence alone.

2.11.s:
satyena sarvamāpnoti satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam /
yathārthakathanācāraḥ satyaṃ proktaṃ dvijātibhiḥ //
2.11.d:
सत्येन सर्वमाप्नोति सत्ये सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
यथार्थकथनाचारः सत्यं प्रोक्तं द्विजातिभिः ॥
2.11.m: By truth one attains everything; in truth everything is established; / conduct involving speaking reality is declared by the twice-born to be truth.

2.11.s:
paradravyāpaharaṇaṃ cauryād vātha balena vā /
steyaṃ tasyānācaraṇādasteyaṃ dharmasādhanam //
2.11.d:
परद्रव्यापहरणं चौर्याद् वाथ बलेन वा ।
स्तेयं तस्यानाचरणादस्तेयं धर्मसाधनम् ॥
2.11.m:
The taking of another’s property by theft or by force
is stealing; from abstaining from it comes non-stealing, an instrument of dharma.

2.11.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā /
sarvatra maithunatyāgaṃ brahmacaryaṃ pracakṣate //
2.11.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा ।
सर्वत्र मैथुनत्यागं ब्रह्मचर्यं प्रचक्षते ॥
2.11.m:
The renunciation of sexual intercourse in every circumstance, at all times,
and in all places—in action, thought, and speech—is called celibacy.

2.11.s:
dravyāṇāmapyanādānamāpadyapi yathecchayā /
aparigraha ityāhustaṃ prayatnena pālayet //
2.11.d:
द्रव्याणामप्यनादानमापद्यपि यथेच्छया ।
अपरिग्रह इत्याहुस्तं प्रयत्नेन पालयेत् ॥
2.11.m:
Non-acceptance of material goods at will, even in times of distress,
is called non-possession; one should observe it with effort.

2.11.s:
tapaḥ svādhyāyasaṃtoṣāḥ śaucamīśvarapūjanam /
samāsānniyamāḥ proktā yogasiddhipradāyinaḥ //
2.11.d:
तपः स्वाध्यायसंतोषाः शौचमीश्वरपूजनम् ।
समासान्नियमाः प्रोक्ता योगसिद्धिप्रदायिनः ॥
2.11.m:
Austerity, recitation of sacred texts, contentment, purity, and worship of God:
briefly, these are declared to be the observances that bestow success in yoga.

2.11.s:
upavāsaparākādikṛcchracāndrāyaṇādibhiḥ /
śarīraśoṣaṇaṃ prāhustāpasāstapa uttamam //
2.11.d:
उपवासपराकादिकृच्छ्रचान्द्रायणादिभिः ।
शरीरशोषणं प्राहुस्तापसास्तप उत्तमम् ॥
2.11.m:
The emaciation of the body through fasts, parāka, kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, and the like
is declared by ascetics to be the supreme austerity.

2.11.s:
vedāntaśatarudrīyapraṇavādijapaṃ budhāḥ /
sattvaśuddhikaraṃ puṃsāṃ svādhyāyaṃ paricakṣate //
2.11.d:
वेदान्तशतरुद्रीयप्रणवादिजपं बुधाः ।
सत्त्वशुद्धिकरं पुंसां स्वाध्यायं परिचक्षते ॥
2.11.m:
The repetition of the Vedānta, the Śatarudrīya, the Praṇava, and the like,
which effects the purification of the mind for persons, the wise call sacred recitation.

2.11.s:
svādhyāyasya trayo bhedā vācikopāṃśumānasāḥ /
uttarottaravaiśiṣṭyaṃ prāhurvedārthavedinaḥ //
2.11.d:
स्वाध्यायस्य त्रयो भेदा वाचिकोपांशुमानसाः ।
उत्तरोत्तरवैशिष्ट्यं प्राहुर्वेदार्थवेदिनः ॥
2.11.m:
There are three varieties of sacred recitation: vocal, whispered, and mental;
those who know the meaning of the Vedas declare each successive one to be superior.

2.11.s:
yaḥ śabdabodhajananaḥ pareṣāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ sphuṭam /
svādhyāyo vācikaḥ prokta upāṃśoratha lakṣaṇam //
2.11.d:
यः शब्दबोधजननः परेषां शृण्वतां स्फुटम् ।
स्वाध्यायो वाचिकः प्रोक्त उपांशोरथ लक्षणम् ॥
2.11.m:
That which clearly produces apprehension of the sound in others who are listening
is declared to be vocal recitation. Now, the definition of whispered recitation:

2.11.s:
oṣṭhayoḥ spandamātreṇa parasyāśabdabodhakaḥ /
upāṃśureṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ sāhasro vācikājjapaḥ //
2.11.d:
ओष्ठयोः स्पन्दमात्रेण परस्याशब्दबोधकः ।
उपांशुरेष निर्दिष्टः साहस्रो वाचिकाज्जपः ॥
2.11.m:
By mere movement of the lips, without conveying the sound to another,
this is defined as whispered, a repetition a thousandfold [superior] to the vocal.

2.11.s:
yatpadākṣarasaṅgatyā parispandanavarjitam /
cintanaṃ sarvaśabdānāṃ mānasaṃ taṃ japaṃ viduḥ //
2.11.d:
यत्पदाक्षरसङ्गत्या परिस्पन्दनवर्जितम् ।
चिन्तनं सर्वशब्दानां मानसं तं जपं विदुः ॥
2.11.m:
The contemplation of all the words through the sequence of words and syllables,
devoid of any movement [of the lips], they know to be mental repetition.

2.11.s:
yadṛcchālābhato nityamalaṃ puṃso bhavediti /
yā dhīstāmṛṣayaḥ prāhuḥ saṃtoṣaṃ sukhalakṣaṇam //
2.11.d:
यदृच्छालाभतो नित्यमलं पुंसो भवेदिति ।
या धीस्तामृषयः प्राहुः संतोषं सुखलक्षणम् ॥
2.11.m:
That thought by which a man is always content with whatever comes by chance,
saying 'it is enough'—the sages call that contentment, whose mark is happiness.

2.11.s:
bāhyamābhyantaraṃ śaucaṃ dvidhā proktaṃ dvijottamāḥ /
mṛjjalābhyāṃ smṛtaṃ bāhyaṃ manaḥśuddhirathāntaram //
2.11.d:
बाह्यमाभ्यन्तरं शौचं द्विधा प्रोक्तं द्विजोत्तमाः ।
मृज्जलाभ्यां स्मृतं बाह्यं मनःशुद्धिरथान्तरम् ॥
2.11.m:
Purity is declared to be of two kinds, external and internal, O best of the twice-born;
external is remembered as achieved by earth and water, and internal is purity of mind.

2.11.s:
stutismaraṇapūjābhirvāṅmanaḥkāyakarmabhiḥ /
suniścalā śive bhaktiretadīśvarapūjanam //
2.11.d:
स्तुतिस्मरणपूजाभिर्वाङ्मनःकायकर्मभिः ।
सुनिश्चला शिवे भक्तिरेतदीश्वरपूजनम् ॥
2.11.m:
Unwavering devotion to Śiva through praise, remembrance, and worship,
by actions of speech, mind, and body—this is worship of God.

2.11.s:
yamāḥ saniyamāḥ proktāḥ prāṇāyāmaṃ nibodhata /
prāṇaḥ svadehajo vāyurāyāmastannirodhanam //
2.11.d:
यमाः सनियमाः प्रोक्ताः प्राणायामं निबोधत ।
प्राणः स्वदेहजो वायुरायामस्तन्निरोधनम् ॥
2.11.m:
The restraints along with the observances have been declared; learn now of breath control.
Prāṇa is the wind born in one's own body, and āyāma is its restraint.

2.11.s:
uttamādhamamadhyatvāt tridhāyaṃ pratipāditaḥ /
sa eva dvividhaḥ proktaḥ sagarbho 'garbha eva ca //
2.11.d:
उत्तमाधममध्यत्वात् त्रिधायं प्रतिपादितः ।
स एव द्विविधः प्रोक्तः सगर्भो ऽगर्भ एव च ॥
2.11.m:
It is taught to be threefold, being low, middling, and superior;
it is also declared to be of two kinds: with seed and without seed.

2.11.s:
mātrādvādaśako mandaścaturviṃśatimātrikaḥ /
madhyamaḥ prāṇasaṃrodhaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśanmātrikottamaḥ //
2.11.d:
मात्राद्वादशको मन्दश्चतुर्विंशतिमात्रिकः ।
मध्यमः प्राणसंरोधः षट्त्रिंशन्मात्रिकोत्तमः ॥
2.11.m:
A restraint of breath of twelve units of time is mild; of twenty-four units
is middling; and of thirty-six units is superior.

2.11.s:
prasvedakampanotthānajanakatvaṃ yathākramam /
mandamadhyamamukhyānāmānandāduttamottamaḥ //
2.11.d:
प्रस्वेदकम्पनोत्थानजनकत्वं यथाक्रमम् ।
मन्दमध्यममुख्यानामानन्दादुत्तमोत्तमः ॥
2.11.m:
Generating perspiration, trembling, and levitation, respectively,
for the mild, middling, and chief [levels]; through bliss, it is the highest of the high.

2.11.s:
sagarbhamāhuḥ sajapamagarbhaṃ vijapaṃ budhāḥ /
etad vai yogināmuktaṃ prāṇāyāmasya lakṣaṇam //
2.11.d:
सगर्भमाहुः सजपमगर्भं विजपं बुधाः ।
एतद् वै योगिनामुक्तं प्राणायामस्य लक्षणम् ॥
2.11.m:
The wise call that with seed accompanied by repetition, and without seed devoid of repetition;
this indeed is declared to be the characteristic of breath control for yogins.

2.11.s:
savyāhṛtiṃ sapraṇavāṃ gāyatrīṃ śirasā saha /
trirjapedāyataprāṇaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa ucyate //
2.11.d:
सव्याहृतिं सप्रणवां गायत्रीं शिरसा सह ।
त्रिर्जपेदायतप्राणः प्राणायामः स उच्यते ॥
2.11.m:
Holding the breath, one should recite thrice the Gāyatrī with the sacred utterances,
with the Praṇava, and together with its head; that is called breath control.

2.11.s:
recakaḥ pūrakaścaiva prāṇāyāmo 'tha kumbhakaḥ /
procyate sarvaśāstreṣu yogibhiryatamānasaiḥ //
2.11.d:
रेचकः पूरकश्चैव प्राणायामो ऽथ कुम्भकः ।
प्रोच्यते सर्वशास्त्रेषु योगिभिर्यतमानसैः ॥
2.11.m:
Exhalation, inhalation, and retention of breath
are declared in all scriptures by yogins of controlled minds.

2.11.s:
recako 'jastraniśvāsāt pūrakastannirodhataḥ /
sāmyena saṃsthitiryā sā kumbhakaḥ parigīyate //
2.11.d:
रेचको ऽजस्त्रनिश्वासात् पूरकस्तन्निरोधतः ।
साम्येन संस्थितिर्या सा कुम्भकः परिगीयते ॥
2.11.m:
Exhalation is from continuous breathing out; inhalation is from checking that;
that steady state which is balanced is celebrated as retention.

2.11.s:
indriyāṇāṃ vicaratāṃ viṣayeṣu svabhāvataḥ /
nigrahaḥ procyate sadbhiḥ pratyāhārastu sattamāḥ //
2.11.d:
इन्द्रियाणां विचरतां विषयेषु स्वभावतः ।
निग्रहः प्रोच्यते सद्भिः प्रत्याहारस्तु सत्तमाः ॥
2.11.m:
The restraint of the sense organs wandering naturally among sense objects
is declared by the virtuous to be withdrawal, O best of beings.

2.11.s:
hṛtpuṇḍarīke nābhyāṃ vā mūrdhni parvatamastake /
evamādiṣu deśeṣu dhāraṇā cittabandhanam //
2.11.d:
हृत्पुण्डरीके नाभ्यां वा मूर्ध्नि पर्वतमस्तके ।
एवमादिषु देशेषु धारणा चित्तबन्धनम् ॥
2.11.m:
In the lotus of the heart, or at the navel, on the crown of the head, or on a mountain peak—
fixing the mind in such places is concentration.

2.11.s:
deśāvasthitimālambya buddheryā vṛttisaṃtatiḥ /
vṛttyantarairasaṃsṛṣṭā taddhyānaṃ sūrayo viduḥ //
2.11.d:
देशावस्थितिमालम्ब्य बुद्धेर्या वृत्तिसंततिः ।
वृत्त्यन्तरैरसंसृष्टा तद्ध्यानं सूरयो विदुः ॥
2.11.m:
The continuous flow of the intellect resting upon that place,
unmixed with any other thoughts—the wise know that to be meditation.

2.11.s:
ekākāraḥ samādhiḥ syād deśālambanavarjitaḥ /
pratyayo hyarthamātreṇa yogasādhanamuttamam //
2.11.d:
एकाकारः समाधिः स्याद् देशालम्बनवर्जितः ।
प्रत्ययो ह्यर्थमात्रेण योगसाधनमुत्तमम् ॥
2.11.m:
Absorption is of a single form, devoid of reliance on a physical place,
a cognition consisting solely of the object, the supreme means of yoga.

2.11.s:
dhāraṇā dvādaśāyāmā dhyānaṃ dvādaśadhāraṇāḥ /
dhyānaṃ dvādaśakaṃ yāvat samādhirabhidhīyate //
2.11.d:
धारणा द्वादशायामा ध्यानं द्वादशधारणाः ।
ध्यानं द्वादशकं यावत् समाधिरभिधीयते ॥
2.11.m:
A concentration lasts twelve breath controls; a meditation lasts twelve concentrations;
and so long as twelve meditations last, it is designated absorption.

2.11.s:
āsanaṃ svastikaṃ proktaṃ padmamardhāsanaṃ tathā /
sādhanānāṃ ca sarveṣāmetatsādhanamuttamam //
2.11.d:
आसनं स्वस्तिकं प्रोक्तं पद्ममर्धासनं तथा ।
साधनानां च सर्वेषामेतत्साधनमुत्तमम् ॥
2.11.m:
The posture is declared to be the svastika, the lotus, and also the half-seat;
and among all means, this is the supreme means.

2.11.s:
ūrvorupari viprendrāḥ kṛtvā pādatale ubhe /
samāsītātmanaḥ padmametadāsanamuttamam //
2.11.d:
ऊर्वोरुपरि विप्रेन्द्राः कृत्वा पादतले उभे ।
समासीतात्मनः पद्ममेतदासनमुत्तमम् ॥
2.11.m:
Placing both soles of the feet upon the thighs, O chief sages,
one should sit calmly within oneself; this is the lotus posture, the supreme seat.

2.11.s:
ekaṃ pādamathaikasmin vinyasyoruṇi sattamāḥ /
āsītārdhāsanamidaṃ yogasādhanamuttamam //
2.11.d:
एकं पादमथैकस्मिन् विन्यस्योरुणि सत्तमाः ।
आसीतार्धासनमिदं योगसाधनमुत्तमम् ॥
2.11.m:
Placing one foot upon one thigh, O best of men,
one should sit; this is the half-seat, the supreme instrument of yoga.

2.11.s:
ubhe kṛtvā pādatale jānūrvorantareṇa hi /
samāsītātmanaḥ proktamāsanaṃ svastikaṃ param //
2.11.d:
उभे कृत्वा पादतले जानूर्वोरन्तरेण हि ।
समासीतात्मनः प्रोक्तमासनं स्वस्तिकं परम् ॥
2.11.m:
Placing both soles of the feet between the knees and the thighs,
one should sit composed; this is declared to be the svastika, the supreme posture.

2.11.s:
adeśakāle yogasya darśanaṃ hi na vidyate /
agnyabhyāse jale vāpi śuṣkaparṇacaye tathā //
2.11.d:
अदेशकाले योगस्य दर्शनं हि न विद्यते ।
अग्न्यभ्यासे जले वापि शुष्कपर्णचये तथा ॥
2.11.m:
In an improper place and time, vision of yoga is not attained:
near a fire, in water, or upon a heap of dry leaves;

2.11.s:
jantuvyāpte śmaśāne ca jīrṇagoṣṭhe catuṣpathe /
saśabde sabhaye vāpi caityavalmīkasaṃcaye //
2.11.d:
जन्तुव्याप्ते श्मशाने च जीर्णगोष्ठे चतुष्पथे ।
सशब्दे सभये वापि चैत्यवल्मीकसंचये ॥
2.11.m:
in a place infested with vermin, a cremation ground, a ruined cow-pen, a crossroad,
in a noisy or frightening place, at a sacred monument, or on an anthill;

2.11.s:
aśubhe durjanākrānte maśakādisamanvite /
nācared dehabādhe vā daurmanasyādisaṃbhave //
2.11.d:
अशुभे दुर्जनाक्रान्ते मशकादिसमन्विते ।
नाचरेद् देहबाधे वा दौर्मनस्यादिसंभवे ॥
2.11.m:
in an unwholesome place, one overrun by wicked people, or full of mosquitoes and the like;
nor should one practice when afflicted in body or when depression and such arise.

2.11.s:
sugupte suśubhe deśe guhāyāṃ parvatasya tu /
nadyāstīre puṇyadeśe devatāyatane tathā //
2.11.d:
सुगुप्ते सुशुभे देशे गुहायां पर्वतस्य तु ।
नद्यास्तीरे पुण्यदेशे देवतायतने तथा ॥
2.11.m:
In a well-secluded, auspicious place, in a mountain cave,
on a riverbank, in a sacred region, or in a temple of a deity;

2.11.s:
gṛhe vā suśubhe ramye vijane jantuvarjite /
yuñjīta yogī satatamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ //
2.11.d:
गृहे वा सुशुभे रम्ये विजने जन्तुवर्जिते ।
युञ्जीत योगी सततमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
2.11.m:
or in an auspicious, delightful, solitary house free of vermin,
the yogin, devoted to me, should constantly yoke himself.

2.11.s:
namaskṛtya tu yogīndrān saśiṣyāṃśca vināyakam /
guruṃ caivātha māṃ yogī yuñjīta susamāhitaḥ //
2.11.d:
नमस्कृत्य तु योगीन्द्रान् सशिष्यांश्च विनायकम् ।
गुरुं चैवाथ मां योगी युञ्जीत सुसमाहितः ॥
2.11.m:
Having bowed to the lords of yoga, their disciples, Vināyaka,
the guru, and then to me, the yogin should concentrate, well collected.

2.11.s:
āsanaṃ svastikaṃ baddhvā padmamardhamathāpi vā /
nāsikāgre samāṃ dṛṣṭimīṣadunmīlitekṣaṇaḥ //
2.11.d:
आसनं स्वस्तिकं बद्ध्वा पद्ममर्धमथापि वा ।
नासिकाग्रे समां दृष्टिमीषदुन्मीलितेक्षणः ॥
2.11.m:
Having assumed the svastika posture, or the lotus, or the half-seat,
fixing the gaze evenly on the tip of the nose, with eyes slightly open,

2.11.s:
kṛtvātha nirbhayaḥ śāntastyaktvā māyāmayaṃ jagat /
svātmanyavasthitaṃ devaṃ cintayet parameśvaram //
2.11.d:
कृत्वाथ निर्भयः शान्तस्त्यक्त्वा मायामयं जगत् ।
स्वात्मन्यवस्थितं देवं चिन्तयेत् परमेश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m:
fearless and calm, having abandoned the world made of illusory power,
he should contemplate the Lord, the Supreme God abiding in his own self.

2.11.s:
śikhāgre dvādaśāṅgulye kalpayitvātha paṅkajam /
dharmakandasamudbhūtaṃ jñānanālaṃ suśobhanam //
2.11.d:
शिखाग्रे द्वादशाङ्गुल्ये कल्पयित्वाथ पङ्कजम् ।
धर्मकन्दसमुद्भूतं ज्ञाननालं सुशोभनम् ॥
2.11.m:
Visualizing a lotus twelve finger-breadths above the tuft of hair on the head,
springing from the bulb of dharma, with the stalk of knowledge, exceedingly beautiful,

2.11.s:
aiśvaryāṣṭadalaṃ śvetaṃ paraṃ vairāgyakarṇikam /
cintayet paramaṃ kośaṃ karṇikāyāṃ hiraṇmayam //
2.11.d:
ऐश्वर्याष्टदलं श्वेतं परं वैराग्यकर्णिकम् ।
चिन्तयेत् परमं कोशं कर्णिकायां हिरण्मयम् ॥
2.11.m:
with eight white petals of sovereign powers and supreme detachment for its pericarp,
he should contemplate upon that pericarp the supreme golden sheath,

2.11.s:
sarvaśaktimayaṃ sākṣād yaṃ prāhurdivyamavyayam /
oṅkāravācyamavyaktaṃ raśmijālasamākulam //
2.11.d:
सर्वशक्तिमयं साक्षाद् यं प्राहुर्दिव्यमव्ययम् ।
ओङ्कारवाच्यमव्यक्तं रश्मिजालसमाकुलम् ॥
2.11.m:
consisting of all powers, visible, which they call divine and imperishable,
expressed by the syllable Oṃ, unmanifest, filled with a web of rays.

2.11.s:
cintayet tatra vimalaṃ paraṃ jyotiryadakṣaram /
tasmin jyotiṣi vinyasyasvātmānaṃ tadabhedataḥ //
2.11.d:
चिन्तयेत् तत्र विमलं परं ज्योतिर्यदक्षरम् ।
तस्मिन् ज्योतिषि विन्यस्यस्वात्मानं तदभेदतः ॥
2.11.m:
He should contemplate there the spotless, supreme light which is imperishable;
fixing his own self in that light, non-different from it,

2.11.s:
dhyāyītākāśamadhyasthamīśaṃ paramakāraṇam /
tadātmā sarvago bhūtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet //
2.11.d:
ध्यायीताकाशमध्यस्थमीशं परमकारणम् ।
तदात्मा सर्वगो भूत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
2.11.m:
he should meditate upon the Lord, the ultimate cause, residing in the middle of space.
Having become that self, all-pervading, he should not think of anything at all.

2.11.s:
etad guhyatamaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyānāntaramathocyate /
cintayitvā tu pūrvoktaṃ hṛdaye padmamuttamam //
2.11.d:
एतद् गुह्यतमं ध्यानं ध्यानान्तरमथोच्यते ।
चिन्तयित्वा तु पूर्वोक्तं हृदये पद्ममुत्तमम् ॥
2.11.m:
This is the most secret meditation; now another meditation is described:
having contemplated the previously mentioned supreme lotus in the heart,

2.11.s:
ātmānamatha kartāraṃ tatrānalasamatviṣam /
madhye vahniśikhākāraṃ puruṣaṃ pañcaviṃśakam //
2.11.d:
आत्मानमथ कर्तारं तत्रानलसमत्विषम् ।
मध्ये वह्निशिखाकारं पुरुषं पञ्चविंशकम् ॥
2.11.m:
one should contemplate there the self, the agent, equal in brilliance to fire,
shaped like a flame of fire in the center, the twenty-fifth principle, the individual soul;

2.11.s:
cintayet paramātmānaṃ tanmadhye gaganaṃ param /
oṅkarabodhitaṃ tattvaṃ śāśvataṃ śivamacyutam //
2.11.d:
चिन्तयेत् परमात्मानं तन्मध्ये गगनं परम् ।
ओङ्करबोधितं तत्त्वं शाश्वतं शिवमच्युतम् ॥
2.11.m:
and in its center, the Supreme Self, the supreme space,
the reality revealed by the syllable Oṃ, eternal, Śiva, the unchanging one,

2.11.s:
avyaktaṃ prakṛtau līnaṃ paraṃ jyotiranuttamam /
tadantaḥ paramaṃ tattvamātmādhāraṃ nirañjanam //
2.11.d:
अव्यक्तं प्रकृतौ लीनं परं ज्योतिरनुत्तमम् ।
तदन्तः परमं तत्त्वमात्माधारं निरञ्जनम् ॥
2.11.m:
unmanifest, dissolved in primordial matter, the supreme, unexcelled light;
within it, the supreme principle, the support of the self, taintless.

2.11.s:
dhyāyīta tanmayo nityamekarūpaṃ maheśvaram /
viśodhya sarvatattvāni praṇavenāthavā punaḥ //
2.11.d:
ध्यायीत तन्मयो नित्यमेकरूपं महेश्वरम् ।
विशोध्य सर्वतत्त्वानि प्रणवेनाथवा पुनः ॥
2.11.m:
Absorbed in that, he should constantly meditate upon Maheśvara of uniform nature;
or, again, having purified all principles by means of the Praṇava,

2.11.s:
saṃsthāpya mayi cātmānaṃ nirmale parame pade /
plāvayitvātmano dehaṃ tenaiva jñānavāriṇā //
2.11.d:
संस्थाप्य मयि चात्मानं निर्मले परमे पदे ।
प्लावयित्वात्मनो देहं तेनैव ज्ञानवारिणा ॥
2.11.m: And fixing the self in Me, the stainless, supreme state, / and flooding one's body with that very water of knowledge,

2.11.s:
madātmā manmayo bhasma gṛhītvā hyagnihotrajam /
tenoddhṛtya tu sarvāṅgamagnirityādimantrataḥ /
cintayet svātmanīśānaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ svarūpiṇam //
2.11.d:
मदात्मा मन्मयो भस्म गृहीत्वा ह्यग्निहोत्रजम् ।
तेनोद्धृत्य तु सर्वाङ्गमग्निरित्यादिमन्त्रतः ।
चिन्तयेत् स्वात्मनीशानं परं ज्योतिः स्वरूपिणम् ॥
2.11.m: having one's self in Me, absorbed in Me, taking ashes born of the agnihotra, / and smearing all one's limbs with it with the mantra beginning with 'Agni…', / one should meditate within one's own self on the Lord, who is the supreme light in essence.

2.11.s:
eṣa pāśupato yogaḥ paśupāśavimuktaye /
sarvavedāntasāro 'yamatyāśramamiti śrutiḥ //
2.11.d:
एष पाशुपतो योगः पशुपाशविमुक्तये ।
सर्ववेदान्तसारो ऽयमत्याश्रममिति श्रुतिः ॥
2.11.m: This is the Pāśupata yoga for the release from the fetters of individual souls; / this is the essence of all Vedānta; Vedic revelation declares it to transcend the stages of life.

2.11.s:
etat parataraṃ guhyaṃ matsāyujyopapādakam /
dvijātīnāṃ tu kathitaṃ bhaktānāṃ brahmacāriṇām //
2.11.d:
एतत् परतरं गुह्यं मत्सायुज्योपपादकम् ।
द्विजातीनां तु कथितं भक्तानां ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
2.11.m: This supreme secret, which brings about complete union with Me, / has been declared for the twice-born who are devoted and observe celibacy.

2.11.s:
brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca kṣamā śaucaṃ tapo damaḥ /
saṃtoṣaḥ satyamāstikyaṃ vratāṅgāni viśeṣataḥ //
2.11.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च क्षमा शौचं तपो दमः ।
संतोषः सत्यमास्तिक्यं व्रताङ्गानि विशेषतः ॥
2.11.m: Celibacy, non-violence, patience, purity, austerity, self-control, / contentment, truthfulness, and faith—these are especially the limbs of the observance.

2.11.s:
ekenāpyatha hīnena vratamasya tu lupyate /
tasmādātmaguṇopeto madvrataṃ voḍhumarhati //
2.11.d:
एकेनाप्यथ हीनेन व्रतमस्य तु लुप्यते ।
तस्मादात्मगुणोपेतो मद्व्रतं वोढुमर्हति ॥
2.11.m: Even if one of these is missing, his observance is broken; / therefore, endowed with the virtues of the self, he is fit to maintain My observance.

2.11.s:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ /
bahavo 'nena yogena pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ //
2.11.d:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः ।
बहवो ऽनेन योगेन पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
2.11.m: Freed from passion, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, / purified by this yoga, many have attained My state of being.

2.11.s:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham /
jñānayogena māṃ tasmād yajeta parameśvaram //
2.11.d:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
ज्ञानयोगेन मां तस्माद् यजेत परमेश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m: In whatever way they surrender to Me, in that very way I reward them; / therefore, through the yoga of knowledge, one should worship Me, the Supreme Lord.

2.11.s:
athavā bhaktiyogena vairāgyeṇa pareṇa tu /
cetasā bodhayuktena pūjayenmāṃ sadā śuciḥ //
2.11.d:
अथवा भक्तियोगेन वैराग्येण परेण तु ।
चेतसा बोधयुक्तेन पूजयेन्मां सदा शुचिः ॥
2.11.m: Or through the yoga of devotion, with supreme dispassion / and a mind endowed with awakening, one, being always pure, should worship Me.

2.11.s:
sarvakarmāṇi saṃnyasya bhikṣāśī niṣparigrahaḥ /
prāpnoti mama sāyujyaṃ guhyametanmayoditam //
2.11.d:
सर्वकर्माणि संन्यस्य भिक्षाशी निष्परिग्रहः ।
प्राप्नोति मम सायुज्यं गुह्यमेतन्मयोदितम् ॥
2.11.m: Renouncing all actions, eating begged food, devoid of possessions, / he attains complete union with Me: this secret has been spoken by Me.

2.11.s:
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca /
nirmamo nirahaṅkāro yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ //
2.11.d:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
2.11.m: Free from hatred toward all beings, friendly, and compassionate, / devoid of possessiveness, devoid of egotism—my devotee who is such is dear to Me.

2.11.s:
saṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ /
mayyarpitamano buddhiryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ //
2.11.d:
संतुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।
मय्यर्पितमनो बुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
2.11.m: Always contented, a yogin, self-controlled, of firm resolve, / with mind and intellect dedicated to Me—my devotee who is such is dear to Me.

2.11.s:
yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ /
harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa hi me priyaḥ //
2.11.d:
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स हि मे प्रियः ॥
2.11.m: He from whom the world shrinks not, and who shrinks not from the world, / freed from joy, intolerance, fear, and agitation—he indeed is dear to Me.

2.11.s:
anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ /
sarvārambhaparityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ //
2.11.d:
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी भक्तिमान् यः स मे प्रियः ॥
2.11.m: Expectant of nothing, pure, capable, unconcerned, free from anguish, / abandoning all undertakings—he who is devoted is dear to Me.

2.11.s:
tulyanindāstutirmaunī saṃtuṣṭo yena kenacit /
aniketaḥ sthiramatirmadbhakto māmupaiṣyati //
2.11.d:
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी संतुष्टो येन केनचित् ।
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्मद्भक्तो मामुपैष्यति ॥
2.11.m: To whom blame and praise are equal, silent, contented with whatever comes, / without a fixed abode, of steady mind—My devotee shall come to Me.

2.11.s:
sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo matparāyaṇaḥ /
matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ paramaṃ padam //
2.11.d:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मत्परायणः ।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं परमं पदम् ॥
2.11.m: Even while constantly performing all actions, intent on Me, / by My grace he attains the eternal, supreme abode.

2.11.s:
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ /
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajet //
2.11.d:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा मामेकं शरणं व्रजेत् ॥
2.11.m: Mentally renouncing all actions unto Me, intent on Me, / becoming free from desire and devoid of possessiveness, he should take refuge in Me alone.

2.11.s:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ /
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto 'pi naiva tena nibadhyate //
2.11.d:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तो ऽपि नैव तेन निबध्यते ॥
2.11.m: Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, ever-satisfied, without dependencies, / even though fully engaged in action, he is not bound by it.

2.11.s:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ /
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti tatpadam //
2.11.d:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति तत्पदम् ॥
2.11.m: Free from desire, with mind and self restrained, having abandoned all possessions, / performing action merely with the body, he attains that state.

2.11.s:
yadṛcchālābhatuṣṭasya dvandvātītasya caiva hi /
kurvato matprasādārthaṃ karma saṃsāranāśanam //
2.11.d:
यदृच्छालाभतुष्टस्य द्वन्द्वातीतस्य चैव हि ।
कुर्वतो मत्प्रसादार्थं कर्म संसारनाशनम् ॥
2.11.m: For one contented with whatever comes by chance, transcending dualities, / performing action for the sake of My grace, action destroys cyclic existence.

2.11.s:
manmanā mannamaskāro madyājī matparāyaṇaḥ /
māmupaiṣyati yogīśaṃ jñātvā māṃ parameśvaram //
2.11.d:
मन्मना मन्नमस्कारो मद्याजी मत्परायणः ।
मामुपैष्यति योगीशं ज्ञात्वा मां परमेश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m: Fixing his mind on Me, bowing to Me, worshipping Me, intent on Me, / knowing Me as the Supreme Lord, he will come to Me, the Lord of Yogins.

2.11.s:
madbuddhayo māṃ satataṃ bodhayantaḥ parasparam /
kathayantaśca māṃ nityaṃ mama sāyujyamāpnuyuḥ //
2.11.d:
मद्बुद्धयो मां सततं बोधयन्तः परस्परम् ।
कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं मम सायुज्यमाप्नुयुः ॥
2.11.m: With their intellects fixed on Me, continually instructing one another about Me, / and ever conversing about Me, they shall attain complete union with Me.

2.11.s:
evaṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ māyeyaṃ karmasānvagam /
nāśayāmi tamaḥ kṛtsnaṃ jñānadīpena bhāsvatā //
2.11.d:
एवं नित्याभियुक्तानां मायेयं कर्मसान्वगम् ।
नाशयामि तमः कृत्स्नं ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥
2.11.m: For those thus constantly disciplined, I destroy entirely this darkness / born of illusory creative power, which follows action, by means of the shining lamp of knowledge.

2.11.s:
madbuddhayo māṃ satataṃ pūjayantīha ye janāḥ /
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham //
2.11.d:
मद्बुद्धयो मां सततं पूजयन्तीह ये जनाः ।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
2.11.m: Those people who, with minds fixed on Me, constantly worship Me here— / to those ever disciplined, I bring acquisition and preservation.

2.11.s:
ye 'nye ca kāmabhogārthaṃ yajante hyanyadevatāḥ /
teṣāṃ tadantaṃ vijñeyaṃ devatānugataṃ phalam //
2.11.d:
ये ऽन्ये च कामभोगार्थं यजन्ते ह्यन्यदेवताः ।
तेषां तदन्तं विज्ञेयं देवतानुगतं फलम् ॥
2.11.m: And those others who, for the sake of desired pleasures, worship other deities— / their fruit, following that deity, is known to have an end.

2.11.s:
ye cānyadevatābhaktāḥ pūjayantīha devatāḥ /
madbhāvanāsamāyuktā mucyante te 'pi bhāvataḥ //
2.11.d:
ये चान्यदेवताभक्ताः पूजयन्तीह देवताः ।
मद्भावनासमायुक्ता मुच्यन्ते ते ऽपि भावतः ॥
2.11.m: And those who, devoted to other deities, worship deities here, / yet are endowed with contemplation of Me—they too are liberated through their devotion.

2.11.s:
tasmādanīśvarānanyāṃstyaktvā devānaśeṣataḥ /
māmeva saṃśrayedīśaṃ sa yāti paramaṃ padam //
2.11.d:
तस्मादनीश्वरानन्यांस्त्यक्त्वा देवानशेषतः ।
मामेव संश्रयेदीशं स याति परमं पदम् ॥
2.11.m: Therefore, having abandoned all other non-sovereign gods without remainder, / one should resort only to Me, the Lord; he goes to the supreme state.

2.11.s:
tyaktvā putrādiṣu snehaṃ niḥ śoko niṣparigrahaḥ /
yajeccāmaraṇālliṅge viraktaḥ parameśvaram //
2.11.d:
त्यक्त्वा पुत्रादिषु स्नेहं निः शोको निष्परिग्रहः ।
यजेच्चामरणाल्लिङ्गे विरक्तः परमेश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m: Renouncing affection for sons and the rest, free from grief, devoid of possessions, / dispassionate, one should worship the Supreme Lord in the liṅga until death.

2.11.s:
ye 'rcayanti sadā liṅgaṃ tyaktvā bhogānaśeṣataḥ /
ekena janmanā teṣāṃ dadāmi paramaiśvaram //
2.11.d:
ये ऽर्चयन्ति सदा लिङ्गं त्यक्त्वा भोगानशेषतः ।
एकेन जन्मना तेषां ददामि परमैश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m: Those who constantly worship the liṅga, having abandoned pleasures completely— / within a single birth I grant them supreme lordship.

2.11.s:
parānandātmakaṃ liṅgaṃ kevalaṃ sannirañjanam /
jñānātmakaṃ sarvagataṃ yogināṃ hṛdi saṃsthitam //
2.11.d:
परानन्दात्मकं लिङ्गं केवलं सन्निरञ्जनम् ।
ज्ञानात्मकं सर्वगतं योगिनां हृदि संस्थितम् ॥
2.11.m: The liṅga consists of supreme bliss, absolute, existent, immaculate, / consisting of knowledge, omnipresent, established in the heart of yogins.

2.11.s:
ye cānye niyatā bhaktā bhāvayitvā vidhānataḥ /
yatra kvacana talliṅgamarcayanti maheśvaram //
2.11.d:
ये चान्ये नियता भक्ता भावयित्वा विधानतः ।
यत्र क्वचन तल्लिङ्गमर्चयन्ति महेश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m: And whatever other disciplined devotees, contemplating in accordance with the rule, / worship the Great Lord anywhere in that liṅga,

2.11.s:
jale vā vahnimadhye vāvyomni sūrye 'thavānyataḥ /
ratnādau bhāvayitveśamarcayelliṅgamaiśvaram //
2.11.d:
जले वा वह्निमध्ये वाव्योम्नि सूर्ये ऽथवान्यतः ।
रत्नादौ भावयित्वेशमर्चयेल्लिङ्गमैश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m: whether in water, or in fire, in space, in the sun, or elsewhere, / in jewels and the like, meditating on the Lord, one should worship the divine liṅga.

2.11.s:
sarvaṃ liṅgamayaṃ hyetat sarvaṃ liṅge pratiṣṭhitam /
tasmālliṅge 'rcayedīśaṃ yatra kvacana śāśvatam //
2.11.d:
सर्वं लिङ्गमयं ह्येतत् सर्वं लिङ्गे प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
तस्माल्लिङ्गे ऽर्चयेदीशं यत्र क्वचन शाश्वतम् ॥
2.11.m: For all this consists of the liṅga; all is established in the liṅga; / therefore one should worship the eternal Lord in the liṅga anywhere.

2.11.s:
agnau kriyāvatāmapsu vyomni sūrye manīṣiṇām /
kāṣṭhādiṣveva mūrkhāṇāṃ hṛdi liṅgantuyoginām //
2.11.d:
अग्नौ क्रियावतामप्सु व्योम्नि सूर्ये मनीषिणाम् ।
काष्ठादिष्वेव मूर्खाणां हृदि लिङ्गन्तुयोगिनाम् ॥
2.11.m: The liṅga is in fire for ritualists, in water, space, and the sun for the wise, / in wood and stones only for fools, but in the heart for yogins.

2.11.s:
yadyanutpannavijñāno viraktaḥ prītisaṃyutaḥ /
yāvajjīvaṃ japed yuktaḥ praṇavaṃ brahmaṇo vapuḥ //
2.11.d:
यद्यनुत्पन्नविज्ञानो विरक्तः प्रीतिसंयुतः ।
यावज्जीवं जपेद् युक्तः प्रणवं ब्रह्मणो वपुः ॥
2.11.m: If discernment has not arisen, one, dispassionate and endowed with devotion, / should continually recite the praṇava, the body of Brahman, as long as he lives.

2.11.s:
athavā śatarudrīyaṃ japedāmaraṇād dvijaḥ /
ekākī yatacittātmā sa yāti paramaṃ padam //
2.11.d:
अथवा शतरुद्रीयं जपेदामरणाद् द्विजः ।
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा स याति परमं पदम् ॥
2.11.m: Or a twice-born, solitary, with mind and self restrained, / should recite the Śatarudrīya until death; he goes to the supreme state.

2.11.s:
vased vāmaraṇād vipro vārāṇasyāṃ samāhitaḥ /
so 'pīśvaraprasādena yāti tat paramaṃ padam //
2.11.d:
वसेद् वामरणाद् विप्रो वाराणस्यां समाहितः ।
सो ऽपीश्वरप्रसादेन याति तत् परमं पदम् ॥
2.11.m: Or a brāhmaṇa, composed in mind, may reside in Vārāṇasī until death; / he too, through the grace of the Lord, goes to that supreme state.

2.11.s:
tatrotkramaṇakāle hi sarveṣāmeva dehinām /
dadāti tat paraṃ jñānaṃ yena mucyeta bandhanāt //
2.11.d:
तत्रोत्क्रमणकाले हि सर्वेषामेव देहिनाम् ।
ददाति तत् परं ज्ञानं येन मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥
2.11.m: For there, at the time of departure, to all embodied beings indeed / He imparts that supreme knowledge by which one is liberated from bondage.

2.11.s:
varṇāśramavidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ kurvāṇo matparāyaṇaḥ /
tenaiva janmanā jñānaṃ labdhvā yāti śivaṃ padam //
2.11.d:
वर्णाश्रमविधिं कृत्स्नं कुर्वाणो मत्परायणः ।
तेनैव जन्मना ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा याति शिवं पदम् ॥
2.11.m: Performing the entire rule of caste and life-stage, intent on Me, / having attained knowledge in that very birth, he goes to the auspicious state.

2.11.s:
ye 'pi tatra vasantīha nīcā vā pāpayonayaḥ /
sarve taranti saṃsāramīśvarānugrahād dvijāḥ //
2.11.d:
ये ऽपि तत्र वसन्तीह नीचा वा पापयोनयः ।
सर्वे तरन्ति संसारमीश्वरानुग्रहाद् द्विजाः ॥
2.11.m: Even those of low status or sinful births who dwell there, / all cross over cyclic existence by the grace of the Lord, O twice-born.

2.11.s:
kintu vighnā bhaviṣyanti pāpopahatacetasām /
dharmaṃ samāśrayet tasmānmuktaye niyataṃ dvijāḥ //
2.11.d:
किन्तु विघ्ना भविष्यन्ति पापोपहतचेतसाम् ।
धर्मं समाश्रयेत् तस्मान्मुक्तये नियतं द्विजाः ॥
2.11.m: However, there will be obstacles for those whose minds are ruined by sin; / therefore, O twice-born, one must strictly resort to duty for liberation.

2.11.s:
etad rahasyaṃ vedānāṃ na deyaṃ yasya kasya cit /
dhārmikāyaiva dātavyaṃ bhaktāya brahmacāriṇe //
2.11.d:
एतद् रहस्यं वेदानां न देयं यस्य कस्य चित् ।
धार्मिकायैव दातव्यं भक्ताय ब्रह्मचारिणे ॥
2.11.m: This secret of the Vedas must not be given to just anyone; / it should be given only to the righteous, to a devotee observing celibacy.

2.11.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ityetaduktvā bhagavānātmayogamanuttamam /
vyājahāra samāsīnaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam //
2.11.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्येतदुक्त्वा भगवानात्मयोगमनुत्तमम् ।
व्याजहार समासीनं नारायणमनामयम् ॥
2.11.m: Vyāsa said: / Having spoken this unexcelled yoga of the self, the Lord / addressed the unimpaired Nārāyaṇa, who was seated nearby:

2.11.s:
mayaitad bhāṣitaṃ jñānaṃ hitārthaṃ brahmavādinām /
dātavyaṃ śāntacittebhyaḥ śiṣyebhyo bhavatā śivam //
2.11.d:
मयैतद् भाषितं ज्ञानं हितार्थं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ।
दातव्यं शान्तचित्तेभ्यः शिष्येभ्यो भवता शिवम् ॥
2.11.m: "This auspicious knowledge has been spoken by Me for the welfare of the expounders of the Veda; / it should be given by you to pupils whose minds are tranquil."

2.11.s:
uktvaivamatha yogīndrānabravīd bhagavānajaḥ /
hitāya sarvabhaktānāṃ dvijātīnāṃ dvijottamāḥ //
2.11.d:
उक्त्वैवमथ योगीन्द्रानब्रवीद् भगवानजः ।
हिताय सर्वभक्तानां द्विजातीनां द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
2.11.m: Having spoken thus, the unborn Lord then spoke to the lords among yogins / for the welfare of all twice-born devotees, O best of the twice-born:

2.11.s:
bhavanto 'pi hi majjñānaṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ vidhipūrvakam /
upadekṣyanti bhaktānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vacanānmama //
2.11.d:
भवन्तो ऽपि हि मज्ज्ञानं शिष्याणां विधिपूर्वकम् ।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति भक्तानां सर्वेषां वचनान्मम ॥
2.11.m: "You too, according to rule, shall instruct your disciples, / all those who are devoted, in My knowledge at My command.

2.11.s:
ayaṃ nārāyaṇo yo 'hamīśvaro nātra saṃśayaḥ /
nāntaraṃ ye prapaśyanti teṣāṃ deyamidaṃ param //
2.11.d:
अयं नारायणो यो ऽहमीश्वरो नात्र संशयः ।
नान्तरं ये प्रपश्यन्ति तेषां देयमिदं परम् ॥
2.11.m: This Nārāyaṇa is who I, the Lord, am; there is no doubt in this; / to those who see no difference between us, this supreme [teaching] is to be given."

2.11.s:
mamaiṣā paramā mūrtirnārāyaṇasamāhvayā /
sarvabhūtātmabhūtasthā śāntā cākṣarasaṃjñitā //
2.11.d:
ममैषा परमा मूर्तिर्नारायणसमाह्वया ।
सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्था शान्ता चाक्षरसंज्ञिता ॥
2.11.m: This is my supreme form, named Nārāyaṇa, / residing within the Self of all beings, tranquil, and called the Imperishable.

2.11.s:
ye tvanyathā prapaśyanti loke bhedadṛśo janāḥ /
na te māṃ saṃprapaśyanti jāyante ca punaḥ punaḥ //
2.11.d:
ये त्वन्यथा प्रपश्यन्ति लोके भेददृशो जनाः ।
न ते मां संप्रपश्यन्ति जायन्ते च पुनः पुनः ॥
2.11.m: Those people in the world who see otherwise, perceiving difference, / do not perceive me, and they are born again and again.

2.11.s:
ye tvimaṃ viṣṇumavyaktaṃ māṃ vā devaṃ maheśvaram /
ekībhāvena paśyanti na teṣāṃ punarudbhavaḥ //
2.11.d:
ये त्विमं विष्णुमव्यक्तं मां वा देवं महेश्वरम् ।
एकीभावेन पश्यन्ति न तेषां पुनरुद्भवः ॥
2.11.m: Those who see this unmanifest Viṣṇu and me, the god Maheśvara, / in unity, do not experience rebirth.

2.11.s:
tasmādanādinidhanaṃ viṣṇumātmānamavyayam /
māmeva saṃprapaśyadhvaṃ pūjayadhvaṃ tathaiva hi //
2.11.d:
तस्मादनादिनिधनं विष्णुमात्मानमव्ययम् ।
मामेव संप्रपश्यध्वं पूजयध्वं तथैव हि ॥
2.11.m: Therefore, behold Viṣṇu, the imperishable Self without beginning or end, / as myself alone, and worship [him] in the very same way.

2.11.s:
ye 'nyathā māṃ prapaśyanti matvemaṃ devatāntaram /
te yānti narakān ghorān nāhaṃ teṣuvyavasthitaḥ //
2.11.d:
ये ऽन्यथा मां प्रपश्यन्ति मत्वेमं देवतान्तरम् ।
ते यान्ति नरकान् घोरान् नाहं तेषुव्यवस्थितः ॥
2.11.m: Those who see me differently, thinking him to be another deity, / go to terrible hells; I am not established in them.

2.11.s:
mūrkhaṃ vā paṇḍitaṃ vāpi brāhmaṇaṃ vā madāśrayam /
mocayāmi śvapākaṃ vā na nārāyaṇanindakam //
2.11.d:
मूर्खं वा पण्डितं वापि ब्राह्मणं वा मदाश्रयम् ।
मोचयामि श्वपाकं वा न नारायणनिन्दकम् ॥
2.11.m: Whether a fool, a learned man, a brāhmaṇa, or an outcaste who takes refuge in me, / I liberate him; but not one who reviles Nārāyaṇa.

2.11.s:
tasmādeṣa mahāyogī madbhaktaiḥ puruṣottamaḥ /
arcanīyo namaskāryo matprītijananāya hi //
2.11.d:
तस्मादेष महायोगी मद्भक्तैः पुरुषोत्तमः ।
अर्चनीयो नमस्कार्यो मत्प्रीतिजननाय हि ॥
2.11.m: Therefore this great yogin, the Supreme Spirit, should be worshipped / and saluted by my devotees to generate my delight.

2.11.s:
evamuktvā samāliṅgya vāsudevaṃ pinākadhṛk /
antarhito 'bhavat teṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva paśyatām //
2.11.d:
एवमुक्त्वा समालिङ्ग्य वासुदेवं पिनाकधृक् ।
अन्तर्हितो ऽभवत् तेषां सर्वेषामेव पश्यताम् ॥
2.11.m: Having spoken thus and embraced Vāsudeva, the wielder of the Pināka / vanished before the eyes of them all.

2.11.s:
nārāyaṇo 'pi bhagavāṃstāpasaṃ veṣamuttamam /
jagrāha yoginaḥ sarvāṃstyaktvā vai paramaṃ vapuḥ //
2.11.d:
नारायणो ऽपि भगवांस्तापसं वेषमुत्तमम् ।
जग्राह योगिनः सर्वांस्त्यक्त्वा वै परमं वपुः ॥
2.11.m: Lord Nārāyaṇa too, relinquishing that supreme form, / assumed an excellent ascetic attire before all the yogins.

2.11.s:
jñātaṃ bhavadbhiramalaṃ prasādāt parameṣṭhinaḥ /
sākṣādeva maheśasya jñānaṃ saṃsāranāśanam //
2.11.d:
ज्ञातं भवद्भिरमलं प्रसादात् परमेष्ठिनः ।
साक्षादेव महेशस्य ज्ञानं संसारनाशनम् ॥
2.11.m: “You have known, through the grace of the Supreme Lord, / the taintless knowledge of Maheśa directly, which destroys worldly existence.

2.11.s:
gacchadhvaṃ vijvarāḥ sarve vijñānaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ /
pravartayadhvaṃ śiṣyebhyo dhārmikebhyo munīśvarāḥ //
2.11.d:
गच्छध्वं विज्वराः सर्वे विज्ञानं परमेष्ठिनः ।
प्रवर्तयध्वं शिष्येभ्यो धार्मिकेभ्यो मुनीश्वराः ॥
2.11.m: Go, all of you, free from affliction, and impart the wisdom / of the Supreme Lord to your righteous disciples, O best of sages.

2.11.s:
idaṃ bhaktāya śāntāya dhārmikāyāhitāgnaye /
vijñānamaiśvaraṃ deyaṃ brāhmaṇāya viśeṣataḥ //
2.11.d:
इदं भक्ताय शान्ताय धार्मिकायाहिताग्नये ।
विज्ञानमैश्वरं देयं ब्राह्मणाय विशेषतः ॥
2.11.m: This divine wisdom should be given to a devotee who is tranquil, / righteous, and keeps the sacred fires, especially to a brāhmaṇa.”

2.11.s:
evamuktvā sa viśvātmā yogināṃ yogavittamaḥ /
nārāyaṇo mahāyogī jagāmādarśanaṃ svayam //
2.11.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स विश्वात्मा योगिनां योगवित्तमः ।
नारायणो महायोगी जगामादर्शनं स्वयम् ॥
2.11.m: Having spoken thus, that Self of the universe, the best knower of yoga among yogins, / the great yogin Nārāyaṇa, vanished of his own accord.

2.11.s:
te 'pi devādideveśaṃ namaskṛtya maheśvaram /
nārāyaṇaṃ ca bhūtādiṃ svāni sthānāni bhejire //
2.11.d:
ते ऽपि देवादिदेवेशं नमस्कृत्य महेश्वरम् ।
नारायणं च भूतादिं स्वानि स्थानानि भेजिरे ॥
2.11.m: They too, having bowed to Maheśvara, the lord of the first of the gods, / and to Nārāyaṇa, the origin of beings, departed to their respective abodes.

2.11.s:
sanatkumāro bhagavān saṃvartāya mahāmuniḥ /
dattavānaiśvaraṃ jñānaṃ so 'pi satyavratāya tu //
2.11.d:
सनत्कुमारो भगवान् संवर्ताय महामुनिः ।
दत्तवानैश्वरं ज्ञानं सो ऽपि सत्यव्रताय तु ॥
2.11.m: The venerable Sanatkumāra, the great sage, imparted / this divine knowledge to Saṃvarta, and he in turn to Satyavrata.

2.11.s:
sanandano 'pi yogīndraḥ pulahāya maharṣaye /
pradadau gautamāyātha pulaho 'pi prajāpatiḥ //
2.11.d:
सनन्दनो ऽपि योगीन्द्रः पुलहाय महर्षये ।
प्रददौ गौतमायाथ पुलहो ऽपि प्रजापतिः ॥
2.11.m: Sanandana, the lord of yogins, also gave [it] to the great sage Pulaha, / and Pulaha, the progenitor of creatures, gave it to Gautama.

2.11.s:
aṅgirā vedaviduṣe bharadvājāya dattavān /
jaigīṣavyāya kapilastathā pañcaśikhāya ca //
2.11.d:
अङ्गिरा वेदविदुषे भरद्वाजाय दत्तवान् ।
जैगीषव्याय कपिलस्तथा पञ्चशिखाय च ॥
2.11.m: Aṅgiras gave [it] to Bharadvāja, who was learned in the Vedas; / Kapila gave [it] to Jaigīṣavya, and likewise to Pañcaśikha.

2.11.s:
parāśaro 'pi sanakāt pitā me sarvatattvadṛk /
lebhetatparamaṃ jñānaṃ tasmād vālmīkirāptavān //
2.11.d:
पराशरो ऽपि सनकात् पिता मे सर्वतत्त्वदृक् ।
लेभेतत्परमं ज्ञानं तस्माद् वाल्मीकिराप्तवान् ॥
2.11.m: My father Parāśara, who sees the truth of everything, obtained / that supreme knowledge from Sanaka; from him Vālmīki received it.

2.11.s:
mamovāca purā devaḥ satīdehabhavāṅgajaḥ /
vāmadevo mahāyogī rudraḥ kila pinākadhṛk //
2.11.d:
ममोवाच पुरा देवः सतीदेहभवाङ्गजः ।
वामदेवो महायोगी रुद्रः किल पिनाकधृक् ॥
2.11.m: To me the god spoke in ancient times, the son born from the body of Satī, / Vāmadeva, the great yogin, Rudra indeed, the wielder of the Pināka.

2.11.s:
nārāyaṇo 'pi bhagavān devakītanayo hariḥ /
arjunāya svayaṃ sākṣāt dattavānidamuttamam //
2.11.d:
नारायणो ऽपि भगवान् देवकीतनयो हरिः ।
अर्जुनाय स्वयं साक्षात् दत्तवानिदमुत्तमम् ॥
2.11.m: Lord Nārāyaṇa too, Hari, the son of Devakī, / directly gave this excellent [teaching] himself to Arjuna.

2.11.s:
yadahaṃ labdhavān rudrād vāmadevādanuttamam /
viśeṣād giriśe bhaktistasmādārabhya me 'bhavat //
2.11.d:
यदहं लब्धवान् रुद्राद् वामदेवादनुत्तमम् ।
विशेषाद् गिरिशे भक्तिस्तस्मादारभ्य मे ऽभवत् ॥
2.11.m: Since that unsurpassable [knowledge] which I obtained from Rudra Vāmadeva, / my special devotion to the mountain-dweller arose.

2.11.s:
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ rudraṃ prapanno 'haṃ viśeṣataḥ /
bhūteśaṃ giraśaṃ sthāṇuṃ devadevaṃ triśūlinam //
2.11.d:
शरण्यं शरणं रुद्रं प्रपन्नो ऽहं विशेषतः ।
भूतेशं गिरशं स्थाणुं देवदेवं त्रिशूलिनम् ॥
2.11.m: I took refuge particularly in Rudra, worthy of refuge, / the lord of beings, the mountain-dweller, the immutable, the god of gods, the trident-bearer.

2.11.s:
bhavanto 'pi hi taṃ devaṃ śaṃbhuṃ govṛṣavāhanam /
prapadyadhvaṃ sapatnīkāḥ saputrāḥ śaraṇaṃ śivam //
2.11.d:
भवन्तो ऽपि हि तं देवं शंभुं गोवृषवाहनम् ।
प्रपद्यध्वं सपत्नीकाः सपुत्राः शरणं शिवम् ॥
2.11.m: You too, along with your wives and sons, take refuge in that god Śaṃbhu, / whose mount is the bull, [who is] Śiva.

2.11.s:
vartadhvaṃ tatprasādena karmayogena śaṅkaram /
pūjayadhvaṃ mahādevaṃ gopatiṃ bhūtibhūṣaṇam //
2.11.d:
वर्तध्वं तत्प्रसादेन कर्मयोगेन शङ्करम् ।
पूजयध्वं महादेवं गोपतिं भूतिभूषणम् ॥
2.11.m: Live by his grace through the yoga of action; worship Śaṅkara, / the Mahādeva, the lord of cattle, adorned with sacred ashes.

2.11.s:
evamukte 'tha munayaḥ śaunakādyā maheśvaram /
praṇemuḥ śāśvataṃ sthāṇuṃ vyāsaṃ satyavatīsutam //
2.11.d:
एवमुक्ते ऽथ मुनयः शौनकाद्या महेश्वरम् ।
प्रणेमुः शाश्वतं स्थाणुं व्यासं सत्यवतीसुतम् ॥
2.11.m: When this was said, the sages headed by Śaunaka bowed to Maheśvara, / the eternal, the immutable, [and to] Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī.

2.11.s:
abruvan hṛṣṭamanasaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ prabhum /
sākṣādeva hṛṣīkeśaṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram //
2.11.d:
अब्रुवन् हृष्टमनसः कृष्णद्वैपायनं प्रभुम् ।
साक्षादेव हृषीकेशं सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् ॥
2.11.m: With delighted minds they spoke to the lord Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, / who was directly Hṛṣīkeśa, the supreme lord of all worlds:

2.11.s:
bhavatprasādādacalā śaraṇye govṛṣadhvaje /
idānīṃ jāyate bhaktiryā devairapi durlabhā //
2.11.d:
भवत्प्रसादादचला शरण्ये गोवृषध्वजे ।
इदानीं जायते भक्तिर्या देवैरपि दुर्लभा ॥
2.11.m: “By your grace, an unshakeable devotion toward the bull-bannered one, the refuge, / has now arisen—a devotion hard to attain even for the gods.

2.11.s:
kathayasva muniśreṣṭha karmayogamanuttamam /
yenāsau bhagavānīśaḥ samārādhyo mumukṣubhiḥ //
2.11.d:
कथयस्व मुनिश्रेष्ठ कर्मयोगमनुत्तमम् ।
येनासौ भगवानीशः समाराध्यो मुमुक्षुभिः ॥
2.11.m: Declare, O best of sages, the unsurpassable yoga of action / by which that Lord, the ruler, is to be worshipped by seekers of liberation.

2.11.s:
tvatsaṃnidhāveṣa sūtaḥ śṛṇotu bhagavadvacaḥ /
tadvadākhilalokānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dharmasaṃgraham //
2.11.d:
त्वत्संनिधावेष सूतः शृणोतु भगवद्वचः ।
तद्वदाखिललोकानां रक्षणं धर्मसंग्रहम् ॥
2.11.m: In your presence let this Sūta hear the words of the Lord; / speak likewise the summary of righteousness that protects all worlds,

2.11.s:
yaduktaṃ devadevena viṣṇunā kūrmarūpiṇā /
pṛṣṭena munibhiḥ pūrvaṃ śakreṇāmṛtamanthane //
2.11.d:
यदुक्तं देवदेवेन विष्णुना कूर्मरूपिणा ।
पृष्टेन मुनिभिः पूर्वं शक्रेणामृतमन्थने ॥
2.11.m: as spoken by the god of gods, Viṣṇu embodied as a tortoise, / when questioned formerly by the sages and Śakra during the churning of the nectar.”

2.11.s:
śrutvā satyavatīsūnuḥ karmayogaṃ sanātanam /
munīnāṃ bhāṣitaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ provāca susamāhitaḥ //
2.11.d:
श्रुत्वा सत्यवतीसूनुः कर्मयोगं सनातनम् ।
मुनीनां भाषितं कृष्णः प्रोवाच सुसमाहितः ॥
2.11.m: Having heard the sages' words regarding the eternal yoga of action, / Kṛṣṇa, the son of Satyavatī, spoke with a deeply collected mind:

2.11.s:
ya imaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ saṃvādaṃ kṛttivāsasaḥ /
sanatkumārapramukhaiḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
2.11.d:
य इमं पठते नित्यं संवादं कृत्तिवाससः ।
सनत्कुमारप्रमुखैः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
2.11.m: “Whoever constantly recites this dialogue of the hide-clad one / with Sanatkumāra and the rest is freed from all sins.

2.11.s:
śrāvayed vā dvijān śuddhān brahmacaryaparāyaṇān /
yo vā vicārayedarthaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
2.11.d:
श्रावयेद् वा द्विजान् शुद्धान् ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणान् ।
यो वा विचारयेदर्थं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.11.m: Or whoever causes pure twice-born men dedicated to celibacy to hear it, / or whoever reflects on its meaning, goes to the supreme state.

2.11.s:
yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnityaṃ bhaktiyukto dṛḍhavrataḥ /
sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaloke mahīyate //
2.11.d:
यश्चैतच्छृणुयान्नित्यं भक्तियुक्तो दृढव्रतः ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
2.11.m: And whoever hears this constantly, endowed with devotion and firm in vows, / is released from all sins and honored in the realm of Brahmā.

2.11.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena paṭhitavyo manīṣibhiḥ /
śrotavyaścātha mantavyo viśeṣād brāhmaṇaiḥ sadā //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge (īśvaragītāsu) ekādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.11.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन पठितव्यो मनीषिभिः ।
श्रोतव्यश्चाथ मन्तव्यो विशेषाद् ब्राह्मणैः सदा ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे (ईश्वरगीतासु) एकादशो ऽध्यायः
2.11.m:
Therefore it should be recited with every effort by wise men, / and should always be heard and reflected upon, especially by brāhmaṇas.”

Thus ends the eleventh chapter in the latter section (in the Īśvaragītā) in the compilation of six thousand verses of the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.12.s:
vyāsa uvāca
śṛṇudhvamṛṣayaḥ sarve vakṣyamāṇaṃ sanātanam /
karmayogaṃ brāhmaṇānāmātyantikaphalapradam //
2.12.d:
व्यास उवाच
शृणुध्वमृषयः सर्वे वक्ष्यमाणं सनातनम् ।
कर्मयोगं ब्राह्मणानामात्यन्तिकफलप्रदम् ॥
2.12.m: Vyāsa said: / “Listen, all you ṛṣis, to the eternal yoga of action / about to be spoken, which yields the ultimate fruit for brāhmaṇas.

2.12.s:
āmnāyasiddhamakhilaṃ brihmaṇānupradarśitam /
ṛṣīṇāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ pūrvaṃ manurāha prajāpatiḥ //
2.12.d:
आम्नायसिद्धमखिलं ब्रिह्मणानुप्रदर्शितम् ।
ऋषीणां शृण्वतां पूर्वं मनुराह प्रजापतिः ॥
2.12.m: Established entirely in Vedic tradition and revealed by Brahmā, / Manu, the progenitor of creatures, formerly declared it to the listening ṛṣis.

2.12.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyamṛṣisaṅghairniṣevitam /
samāhitadhiyo yūyaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama //
2.12.d:
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यमृषिसङ्घैर्निषेवितम् ।
समाहितधियो यूयं शृणुध्वं गदतो मम ॥
2.12.m: It removes all sins, is meritorious, and is practiced by multitudes of ṛṣis. / Listen with concentrated minds as I speak.

2.12.s:
kṛtopanayano vedānadhīyīta dvijottamāḥ /
garbhāṣṭame 'ṣṭame vābde svasūtroktavidhānataḥ //
2.12.d:
कृतोपनयनो वेदानधीयीत द्विजोत्तमाः ।
गर्भाष्टमे ऽष्टमे वाब्दे स्वसूत्रोक्तविधानतः ॥
2.12.m: Having undergone the sacred-thread initiation, O best of twice-borns, one should study the Vedas / in the eighth year from conception, or in the eighth year [of age], according to the rule declared in one's own sūtra.

2.12.s:
daṇḍī ca mekhalī sūtrī kṛṣṇājinadharo muniḥ /
bhikṣāhāro guruhito vīkṣamāṇo gururmukham //
2.12.d:
दण्डी च मेखली सूत्री कृष्णाजिनधरो मुनिः ।
भिक्षाहारो गुरुहितो वीक्षमाणो गुरुर्मुखम् ॥
2.12.m: Carrying a staff, wearing a girdle, a sacred cord, and wearing a black antelope skin, being a silent sage, / subsisting on alms, devoted to the teacher's welfare, gazing upon the teacher's face.

2.12.s:
kārpāsamupavītārthaṃ nirmitaṃ brahmaṇā purā /
brāhmaṇānāṃ trivit sūtraṃ kauśaṃ vā vastrameva vā //
2.12.d:
कार्पासमुपवीतार्थं निर्मितं ब्रह्मणा पुरा ।
ब्राह्मणानां त्रिवित् सूत्रं कौशं वा वस्त्रमेव वा ॥
2.12.m: Cotton for the sacred thread was fashioned of old by Brahmā; / for brāhmaṇas it is a three-ply cord, or [made of] kuśa grass, or a cloth.

2.12.s:
sadopavītī caiva syāt sadā baddhaśikho dvijaḥ /
anyathā yat kṛtaṃ karma tad bhavatyayathākṛtam //
2.12.d:
सदोपवीती चैव स्यात् सदा बद्धशिखो द्विजः ।
अन्यथा यत् कृतं कर्म तद् भवत्ययथाकृतम् ॥
2.12.m: A twice-born man must always wear the sacred thread and always have his topknot tied; / otherwise, whatever rite is performed becomes as though not performed.

2.12.s:
vasedavikṛtaṃ vāsaḥ kārpāsaṃ vā kaṣāyakam /
tadeva paridhānīyaṃ śuklamacchidramuttamam //
2.12.d:
वसेदविकृतं वासः कार्पासं वा कषायकम् ।
तदेव परिधानीयं शुक्लमच्छिद्रमुत्तमम् ॥
2.12.m: One should wear an unaltered garment, made of cotton or dyed reddish-brown; / that same garment to be worn should be white, without holes, and excellent.

2.12.s:
uttaraṃ tu samākhyātaṃ vāsaḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ śubham /
abhāve gavyamajinaṃ rauravaṃ vā vidhīyate //
2.12.d:
उत्तरं तु समाख्यातं वासः कृष्णाजिनं शुभम् ।
अभावे गव्यमजिनं रौरवं वा विधीयते ॥
2.12.m: An auspicious black antelope skin is declared as the upper garment; / in its absence, a bovine hide or a ruru-deer skin is prescribed.

2.12.s:
uddhṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ savye bāhau samarpitam /
upavītaṃ bhavennityaṃ nivītaṃ kaṇṭhasajjane //
2.12.d:
उद्धृत्य दक्षिणं बाहुं सव्ये बाहौ समर्पितम् ।
उपवीतं भवेन्नित्यं निवीतं कण्ठसज्जने ॥
2.12.m: When the right arm is raised and it rests on the left arm, / it is always the upavīta; when hanging around the neck, it is the nivīta.

2.12.s:
savyaṃ bāhuṃ samuddhṛtya dakṣiṇe tu dhṛtaṃ dvijāḥ /
prācīnāvītamityuktaṃ pitrye karmaṇi yojayet //
2.12.d:
सव्यं बाहुं समुद्धृत्य दक्षिणे तु धृतं द्विजाः ।
प्राचीनावीतमित्युक्तं पित्र्ये कर्मणि योजयेत् ॥
2.12.m: When the left arm is raised and it is worn over the right, O twice-borns, / it is called the prācīnāvīta; one should employ it in rites for ancestors.

2.12.s:
agnyagāre gavāṃ goṣṭhe home japye tathaiva ca /
svādhyāye bhojane nityaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca sannidhau //
2.12.d:
अग्न्यगारे गवां गोष्ठे होमे जप्ये तथैव च ।
स्वाध्याये भोजने नित्यं ब्राह्मणानां च सन्निधौ ॥
2.12.m: In the fire-sanctuary, in the cowpen, during oblation and recitation, / in daily private Vedic recitation, at meals, and in the presence of brāhmaṇas,”

2.12.s:
upāsane gurūṇāṃ ca saṃdhyayoḥ sādhusaṃgame /
upavītī bhavennityaṃ vidhireṣa sanātanaḥ //
2.12.d:
उपासने गुरूणां च संध्ययोः साधुसंगमे ।
उपवीती भवेन्नित्यं विधिरेष सनातनः ॥
2.12.m: And while attending upon elders, during the morning and evening twilights, and in the assembly of the virtuous, / he should always wear the sacred thread over the left shoulder: this is the eternal rule.

2.12.s:
mauñjī trivṛt samā ślakṣaṇā kāryā viprasya mekhalā /
muñjābhāve kuśenāhurgranthinaikena vā tribhiḥ //
2.12.d:
मौञ्जी त्रिवृत् समा श्लक्षणा कार्या विप्रस्य मेखला ।
मुञ्जाभावे कुशेनाहुर्ग्रन्थिनैकेन वा त्रिभिः ॥
2.12.m: A Brahmin's girdle should be made of triple-twisted muñja grass, even and smooth; / in the absence of muñja, they say [it may be made] of kuśa grass, with one knot or with three.

2.12.s:
dhārayed bailvapālāśau daṇḍau keśāntakau dvijaḥ /
yajñārhavṛkṣajaṃ vātha saumyamavraṇameva ca //
2.12.d:
धारयेद् बैल्वपालाशौ दण्डौ केशान्तकौ द्विजः ।
यज्ञार्हवृक्षजं वाथ सौम्यमव्रणमेव च ॥
2.12.m: A twice-born man should carry a staff of bilva or palāśa reaching to the hair of the head, / or made of a tree fit for sacrifice, pleasing and unblemished.

2.12.s:
sāyaṃ prātardvijaḥ saṃdhyāmupāsīta samāhitaḥ /
kāmāllobhād bhayānmohāt tyaktena patito bhavet //
2.12.d:
सायं प्रातर्द्विजः संध्यामुपासीत समाहितः ।
कामाल्लोभाद् भयान्मोहात् त्यक्तेन पतितो भवेत् ॥
2.12.m: Evening and morning, a twice-born man, composed in mind, should attend the twilight devotion; / if abandoned out of desire, greed, fear, or delusion, he becomes fallen.

2.12.s:
agnikāryaṃ tataḥ kuryāt sāyaṃ prātaḥ prasannadhīḥ /
snātvā saṃtarpayed devānṛṣīn pitṛgaṇāṃstathā //
2.12.d:
अग्निकार्यं ततः कुर्यात् सायं प्रातः प्रसन्नधीः ।
स्नात्वा संतर्पयेद् देवानृषीन् पितृगणांस्तथा ॥
2.12.m: Then with a serene mind he should perform the fire-sacrifice evening and morning; / having bathed, he should offer libations to the gods, the sages, and the ancestral spirits.

2.12.s:
devatābhyarcanaṃ kuryāt puṣpaiḥ patreṇa vāmbubhiḥ /
abhivādanaśīlaḥ syānnityaṃ vṛddheṣu dharmataḥ //
2.12.d:
देवताभ्यर्चनं कुर्यात् पुष्पैः पत्रेण वाम्बुभिः ।
अभिवादनशीलः स्यान्नित्यं वृद्धेषु धर्मतः ॥
2.12.m: He should perform the worship of the deities with flowers, leaves, or waters; / he should always be inclined to salute his elders according to dharma:

2.12.s:
asāvahaṃ bho nāmeti samyak praṇatipūrvakam /
āyurārogyasiddhyarthaṃ tandrādiparivarjitaḥ //
2.12.d:
असावहं भो नामेति सम्यक् प्रणतिपूर्वकम् ।
आयुरारोग्यसिद्ध्यर्थं तन्द्रादिपरिवर्जितः ॥
2.12.m: [Saying,] 'I am so-and-so by name, venerable sir,' preceded by proper prostration, / for the sake of attaining long life and health, free from lethargy and the like.

2.12.s:
āyuṣṇān bhava saumyeti vācyo vipro 'bhivādane /
akāraścāsya nāmno 'nte vācyaḥ pūrvākṣaraḥ plutaḥ //
2.12.d:
आयुष्णान् भव सौम्येति वाच्यो विप्रो ऽभिवादने ।
अकारश्चास्य नाम्नो ऽन्ते वाच्यः पूर्वाक्षरः प्लुतः ॥
2.12.m: Upon salutation, a Brahmin should be addressed, 'May you be long-lived, gentle one,' / and the letter 'a' at the end of his name should be pronounced, with the preceding vowel prolated.

2.12.s:
na kuryād yo 'bhivādasya dvijaḥ pratyabhivādanam /
nābhivādyaḥ sa viduṣā yathā śūdrastathaiva saḥ //
2.12.d:
न कुर्याद् यो ऽभिवादस्य द्विजः प्रत्यभिवादनम् ।
नाभिवाद्यः स विदुषा यथा शूद्रस्तथैव सः ॥
2.12.m: A twice-born man who does not return a salutation / should not be saluted by a learned man; he is just like a Śūdra.

2.12.s:
vyatyastapāṇinā kāryamupasaṃgrahaṇaṃ guroḥ /
savyena savyaḥ spraṣṭavyo dakṣiṇena tu dakṣiṇaḥ //
2.12.d:
व्यत्यस्तपाणिना कार्यमुपसंग्रहणं गुरोः ।
सव्येन सव्यः स्प्रष्टव्यो दक्षिणेन तु दक्षिणः ॥
2.12.m: Clasping of the teacher's feet must be done with crossed hands: / the left foot is to be touched with the left hand, and the right with the right.

2.12.s:
laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ cāpi tathādhyātmikameva vā /
ādadīta yato jñānaṃ taṃ pūrvamabhivādayet //
2.12.d:
लौकिकं वैदिकं चापि तथाध्यात्मिकमेव वा ।
आददीत यतो ज्ञानं तं पूर्वमभिवादयेत् ॥
2.12.m: From whomever he receives knowledge—whether worldly, Vedic, / or indeed spiritual—he should salute him first.

2.12.s:
nodakaṃ dhārayed bhaikṣaṃ puṣpāṇi samidhastathā /
evaṃvidhāni cānyāni na daivādyeṣu karmasu //
2.12.d:
नोदकं धारयेद् भैक्षं पुष्पाणि समिधस्तथा ।
एवंविधानि चान्यानि न दैवाद्येषु कर्मसु ॥
2.12.m: He should not carry water, alms-food, flowers, or sacrificial fuel, / nor other things of this kind, during rites dedicated to the gods and ancestors.

2.12.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchet kṣatrabandhumanāmayam /
vaiśyaṃ kṣemaṃ samāgamya śūdramārogyameva tu //
2.12.d:
ब्राह्मणं कुशलं पृच्छेत् क्षत्रबन्धुमनामयम् ।
वैश्यं क्षेमं समागम्य शूद्रमारोग्यमेव तु ॥
2.12.m: Meeting [them], he should inquire after the well-being of a Brahmin, the freedom from disease of a Kṣatriya, / the prosperity of a Vaiśya, and the good health of a Śūdra.

2.12.s:
upādhyāyaḥ pitā jyeṣṭho bhrātā caiva mahīpatiḥ /
mātulaḥ śvaśurastrātā mātāmahapitāmahau /
varṇajyeṣṭhaḥ pitṛvyaśca puṃso 'tra guravaḥ smṛtāḥ //
2.12.d:
उपाध्यायः पिता ज्येष्ठो भ्राता चैव महीपतिः ।
मातुलः श्वशुरस्त्राता मातामहपितामहौ ।
वर्णज्येष्ठः पितृव्यश्च पुंसो ऽत्र गुरवः स्मृताः ॥
2.12.m: A preceptor, a father, an elder brother, a king, / a maternal uncle, a father-in-law, a protector, maternal and paternal grandfathers, / an elder by caste, and a paternal uncle are here remembered as a man's male elders.

2.12.s:
mātā mātāmahī gurvo piturmātuśca sodarāḥ /
śvaśrūḥ pitāmahījyeṣṭhā dhātrī ca guravaḥ striyaḥ //
2.12.d:
माता मातामही गुर्वो पितुर्मातुश्च सोदराः ।
श्वश्रूः पितामहीज्येष्ठा धात्री च गुरवः स्त्रियः ॥
2.12.m: A mother, a maternal grandmother, a teacher's wife, the sisters of father and mother, / a mother-in-law, a paternal grandmother, an elder sister, and a nurse are the female elders.

2.12.s:
ityukto guruvargo 'yaṃ mātṛtaḥ pitṛto dvijāḥ /
anuvartanameteṣāṃ manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ //
2.12.d:
इत्युक्तो गुरुवर्गो ऽयं मातृतः पितृतो द्विजाः ।
अनुवर्तनमेतेषां मनोवाक्कायकर्मभिः ॥
2.12.m: This group of elders from the mother's and father's sides has thus been spoken, O twice-born ones; / following after them in thought, word, body, and deed [is required].

2.12.s:
guruṃ dṛṣṭvā samuttiṣṭhedabhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ /
naitairupaviśet sārdhaṃ vivadennātmakāraṇāt //
2.12.d:
गुरुं दृष्ट्वा समुत्तिष्ठेदभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः ।
नैतैरुपविशेत् सार्धं विवदेन्नात्मकारणात् ॥
2.12.m: Seeing an elder, he should stand up, salute, with folded hands; / he should not sit together with these, nor argue for his own sake.

2.12.s:
jīvitārthamapi dveṣād gurubhirnaiva bhāṣaṇam /
udito 'pi guṇairanyairgurudveṣī patatyadhaḥ //
2.12.d:
जीवितार्थमपि द्वेषाद् गुरुभिर्नैव भाषणम् ।
उदितो ऽपि गुणैरन्यैर्गुरुद्वेषी पतत्यधः ॥
2.12.m: Even for the sake of one's life, there should be no speaking with elders out of hatred; / even if distinguished by other virtues, one who hates an elder falls low.

2.12.s:
gurūṇāmapi sarveṣāṃ pūjyāḥ pañca viśeṣataḥ /
teṣāmādyāstrayaḥ śreṣṭhāsteṣāṃ mātā supūjitā //
2.12.d:
गुरूणामपि सर्वेषां पूज्याः पञ्च विशेषतः ।
तेषामाद्यास्त्रयः श्रेष्ठास्तेषां माता सुपूजिता ॥
2.12.m: Even among all elders, five are especially worthy of worship; / of these, the first three are pre-eminent, and among them the mother is most honoured.

2.12.s:
yo bhāvayati yā sūte yena vidyopadiśyate /
jyeṣṭho bhrātā ca bhartā ca pañcaite guravaḥ smṛtāḥ //
2.12.d:
यो भावयति या सूते येन विद्योपदिश्यते ।
ज्येष्ठो भ्राता च भर्ता च पञ्चैते गुरवः स्मृताः ॥
2.12.m: He who nurtures, she who gives birth, he by whom knowledge is imparted, / an elder brother, and a master—these five are remembered as elders.

2.12.s:
ātmanaḥ sarvayatnena prāṇatyāgena vā punaḥ /
pūjanīyā viśeṣeṇa pañcaite bhūtimicchatā //
2.12.d:
आत्मनः सर्वयत्नेन प्राणत्यागेन वा पुनः ।
पूजनीया विशेषेण पञ्चैते भूतिमिच्छता ॥
2.12.m: With all one's effort, or even at the cost of one's life, / these five must be especially worshipped by one who desires prosperity.

2.12.s:
yāvat pitā ca mātā ca dvāvetau nirvikāriṇau /
tāvat sarvaṃ parityajya putraḥ syāt tatparāyaṇaḥ //
2.12.d:
यावत् पिता च माता च द्वावेतौ निर्विकारिणौ ।
तावत् सर्वं परित्यज्य पुत्रः स्यात् तत्परायणः ॥
2.12.m: As long as father and mother, both of them, are free from affliction, / so long, abandoning all else, a son should be devoted to them.

2.12.s:
pitā mātā ca suprītau syātāṃ putraguṇairyadi /
sa putraḥ sakalaṃ dharmamāpnuyāt tena karmaṇā //
2.12.d:
पिता माता च सुप्रीतौ स्यातां पुत्रगुणैर्यदि ।
स पुत्रः सकलं धर्ममाप्नुयात् तेन कर्मणा ॥
2.12.m: If father and mother are thoroughly pleased with their son's virtues, / that son attains all dharma through that deed.

2.12.s:
nāsti mātṛsamaṃ daivaṃ nāsti pitṛsamo guruḥ /
tayoḥ pratyupakāro 'pi na kathañcana vidyate //
2.12.d:
नास्ति मातृसमं दैवं नास्ति पितृसमो गुरुः ।
तयोः प्रत्युपकारो ऽपि न कथञ्चन विद्यते ॥
2.12.m: There is no deity equal to a mother; there is no elder equal to a father; / indeed, there is no way to repay them.

2.12.s:
tayornityaṃ priyaṃ kuryāt karmaṇā manasā girā /
na tābhyāmananujñāto dharmamanyaṃ samācaret //
2.12.d:
तयोर्नित्यं प्रियं कुर्यात् कर्मणा मनसा गिरा ।
न ताभ्यामननुज्ञातो धर्ममन्यं समाचरेत् ॥
2.12.m: He should always do what is dear to them by deed, mind, and speech; / without their permission, he should not practice any other religious duty,

2.12.s:
varjayitvā muktiphalaṃ nityaṃ naimittikaṃ tathā /
dharmasāraḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ pretyānantaphalapradaḥ //
2.12.d:
वर्जयित्वा मुक्तिफलं नित्यं नैमित्तिकं तथा ।
धर्मसारः समुद्दिष्टः प्रेत्यानन्तफलप्रदः ॥
2.12.m: Excepting that which yields liberation, as well as the regular and occasional duties; / [devotion to them] is declared the essence of dharma, yielding endless fruit after death.

2.12.s:
samyagārādhya vaktāraṃ visṛṣṭastadanujñayā /
śiṣyo vidyāphalaṃ bhuṅkte pretya cāpadyate divi //
2.12.d:
सम्यगाराध्य वक्तारं विसृष्टस्तदनुज्ञया ।
शिष्यो विद्याफलं भुङ्क्ते प्रेत्य चापद्यते दिवि ॥
2.12.m: Having properly served the instructor and dismissed with his permission, / a student enjoys the fruit of his learning and after death reaches heaven.

2.12.s:
yo bhrātaraṃ pitṛsamaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ mūrkho 'vamanyate /
tena doṣeṇa sa pretya nirayaṃ ghoramṛcchati //
2.12.d:
यो भ्रातरं पितृसमं ज्येष्ठं मूर्खो ऽवमन्यते ।
तेन दोषेण स प्रेत्य निरयं घोरमृच्छति ॥
2.12.m: A fool who dishonours an elder brother who is like a father, / on account of that fault goes to a terrible hell after death.

2.12.s:
puṃsā vartmaniviṣṭena pūjyo bhartā tu sarvadā /
yāti dātari loke 'smin upakārāddhi gauravam //
2.12.d:
पुंसा वर्त्मनिविष्टेन पूज्यो भर्ता तु सर्वदा ।
याति दातरि लोके ऽस्मिन् उपकाराद्धि गौरवम् ॥
2.12.m: By a man set on his course, a master is always to be worshipped; / for in this world respect goes to a benefactor on account of assistance.

2.12.s:
yenarā bhartṛpiṇḍārthaṃ svān prāṇān saṃtyajanti hi /
teṣāmathākṣayāṃllokān provāca bhagavān manuḥ //
2.12.d:
येनरा भर्तृपिण्डार्थं स्वान् प्राणान् संत्यजन्ति हि ।
तेषामथाक्षयांल्लोकान् प्रोवाच भगवान् मनुः ॥
2.12.m: The men who indeed abandon their own lives for the sustenance of their master— / for them the blessed Manu declared imperishable worlds.

2.12.s:
mātulāṃśca pitṛvyāṃśca śvaśurānṛtvijo gurūn /
asāvahamiti brūyuḥ pratyutthāya yavīyasaḥ //
2.12.d:
मातुलांश्च पितृव्यांश्च श्वशुरानृत्विजो गुरून् ।
असावहमिति ब्रूयुः प्रत्युत्थाय यवीयसः ॥
2.12.m: To maternal uncles, paternal uncles, fathers-in-law, officiating priests, and preceptors, / younger men, having risen to meet them, should say, 'I am so-and-so.'

2.12.s:
avācyo dīkṣito nāmnā yavīyānapi yo bhavet /
bhobhavatpūrvakaṃ tvenamabhibhāṣeta dharmavit //
2.12.d:
अवाच्यो दीक्षितो नाम्ना यवीयानपि यो भवेत् ।
भोभवत्पूर्वकं त्वेनमभिभाषेत धर्मवित् ॥
2.12.m: An initiated person should not be addressed by name even if he is younger; / one who knows dharma should address him beginning with 'bhoḥ' or 'bhavat'.

2.12.s:
abhivādyāśca pūjyaśca śirasā vandya eva ca /
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyādyaiśca śrīkāmaiḥ sādaraṃ sadā //
2.12.d:
अभिवाद्याश्च पूज्यश्च शिरसा वन्द्य एव च ।
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियाद्यैश्च श्रीकामैः सादरं सदा ॥
2.12.m: A Brahmin is to be saluted, worshipped, and bowed to with the head / with respect at all times by Kṣatriyas and others desiring prosperity.

2.12.s:
nābhivādyāstu vipreṇa kṣatriyādyāḥ kathañcana /
jñānakarmaguṇopetā yadyapyete bahuśrutāḥ //
2.12.d:
नाभिवाद्यास्तु विप्रेण क्षत्रियाद्याः कथञ्चन ।
ज्ञानकर्मगुणोपेता यद्यप्येते बहुश्रुताः ॥
2.12.m: Kṣatriyas and others must never be saluted by a Brahmin, / even if they are endowed with the virtues of knowledge and ritual acts, and are deeply learned.

2.12.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ svasti kuryāditi sthitiḥ /
savarṇeṣu savarṇānāṃ kāryamevābhivādanam //
2.12.d:
ब्राह्मणः सर्ववर्णानां स्वस्ति कुर्यादिति स्थितिः ।
सवर्णेषु सवर्णानां कार्यमेवाभिवादनम् ॥
2.12.m: The settled rule is that a Brahmin should say 'svasti' to all castes; / among equals in caste, salutation must indeed be performed.

2.12.s:
gururagnirdvijātīnāṃ varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo guruḥ /
patireko guruḥ strīṇāṃ sarvatrābhyāgato guruḥ //
2.12.d:
गुरुरग्निर्द्विजातीनां वर्णानां ब्राह्मणो गुरुः ।
पतिरेको गुरुः स्त्रीणां सर्वत्राभ्यागतो गुरुः ॥
2.12.m: Fire is the elder of the twice-born; the Brahmin is the elder of the castes; / the husband is the sole elder of women; a guest is an elder everywhere.

2.12.s:
vidyā karma vayo bandhurvittaṃ bhavati pañcamam /
mānyasthānāni pañcāhuḥ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ gurūttarāt //
2.12.d:
विद्या कर्म वयो बन्धुर्वित्तं भवति पञ्चमम् ।
मान्यस्थानानि पञ्चाहुः पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरूत्तरात् ॥
2.12.m: Learning, ritual action, age, kin, and wealth is the fifth: / they say these are the five grounds of respect, each earlier one weightier than the later.

2.12.s:
pañcānāṃ triṣu varṇeṣu bhūyāṃsi balavanti ca /
yatra syuḥ so 'tra mānārhaḥ śūdro 'pi daśamīṃ gataḥ //
2.12.d:
पञ्चानां त्रिषु वर्णेषु भूयांसि बलवन्ति च ।
यत्र स्युः सो ऽत्र मानार्हः शूद्रो ऽपि दशमीं गतः ॥
2.12.m: Among the three castes, in whomever more and stronger of these five are present, / he is worthy of respect here; even a Śūdra is so, when he has reached the tenth [decade of life].

2.12.s:
panthā deyo brāhmaṇāya striyai rājñe hyacakṣuṣe /
vṛddhāya bhārabugnāya rogiṇe durbalāya ca //
2.12.d:
पन्था देयो ब्राह्मणाय स्त्रियै राज्ञे ह्यचक्षुषे ।
वृद्धाय भारबुग्नाय रोगिणे दुर्बलाय च ॥
2.12.m: The path should be yielded to a Brahmin, to a woman, to a king, to the blind, / to an old man, to one bowed under a load, to a sick man, and to the weak.

2.12.s:
bhikṣāmāhṛtya śiṣṭānāṃ gṛhebhyaḥ prayato 'nvaham /
nivedya gurave 'śnīyād vāgyatastadanujñayā //
2.12.d:
भिक्षामाहृत्य शिष्टानां गृहेभ्यः प्रयतो ऽन्वहम् ।
निवेद्य गुरवे ऽश्नीयाद् वाग्यतस्तदनुज्ञया ॥
2.12.m: Having collected alms from the houses of virtuous people, restrained every day, / having presented it to his teacher, he should eat with restrained speech with his permission.

2.12.s:
bhavatpūrvaṃ cared bhaikṣyamupanīto dvijottamaḥ /
bhavanmadhyaṃ tu rājanyo vaiśyastu bhavaduttaram //
2.12.d:
भवत्पूर्वं चरेद् भैक्ष्यमुपनीतो द्विजोत्तमः ।
भवन्मध्यं तु राजन्यो वैश्यस्तु भवदुत्तरम् ॥
2.12.m: An initiated excellent twice-born should beg for alms with 'bhavat' first; / a Kṣatriya with 'bhavat' in the middle, but a Vaiśya with 'bhavat' at the end.

2.12.s:
mātaraṃ vā svasāraṃ vā māturvā bhaginīṃ nijām /
bhikṣeta bhikṣāṃ prathamaṃ yā cainaṃ na vimānayet //
2.12.d:
मातरं वा स्वसारं वा मातुर्वा भगिनीं निजाम् ।
भिक्षेत भिक्षां प्रथमं या चैनं न विमानयेत् ॥
2.12.m: He should first beg alms of his mother, or sister, / or his own mother's sister, or of one who would not dishonour him.

2.12.s:
sajātīyagṛheṣveva sārvavarṇikameva vā /
bhaikṣyasya caraṇaṃ proktaṃ patitādiṣu varjitam //
2.12.d:
सजातीयगृहेष्वेव सार्ववर्णिकमेव वा ।
भैक्ष्यस्य चरणं प्रोक्तं पतितादिषु वर्जितम् ॥
2.12.m: The gathering of alms is prescribed in the houses of one's own caste / or among all castes, excluding those who are fallen and the like.

2.12.s:
vedayajñairahīnānāṃ praśastānāṃ svakarmasu /
brahmacaryāhared bhaikṣaṃ gṛhebhyaḥ prayato 'nvaham //
2.12.d:
वेदयज्ञैरहीनानां प्रशस्तानां स्वकर्मसु ।
ब्रह्मचर्याहरेद् भैक्षं गृहेभ्यः प्रयतो ऽन्वहम् ॥
2.12.m: Restrained every day, the student should bring alms from the houses / of those who are not deficient in the Vedas and sacrifices, and are praised in their own duties.

2.12.s:
guroḥ kule na bhikṣeta na jñātikulabandhuṣu /
alābhe tvanyagehānāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ vivarjayet //
2.12.d:
गुरोः कुले न भिक्षेत न ज्ञातिकुलबन्धुषु ।
अलाभे त्वन्यगेहानां पूर्वं पूर्वं विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.12.m: He should not beg in the household of his guru, nor among the families of kinsmen and relatives; / but in the absence of other homes, he should avoid each prior one [in reverse order].

2.12.s:
sarvaṃ vā vicared grāmaṃ pūrvoktānāmasaṃbhave /
niyamya prayato vācaṃ diśastvanavalokayan //
2.12.d:
सर्वं वा विचरेद् ग्रामं पूर्वोक्तानामसंभवे ।
नियम्य प्रयतो वाचं दिशस्त्वनवलोकयन् ॥
2.12.m: Or, if the aforementioned are unavailable, he may traverse the whole village, / restrained, holding his speech, and not looking about at the quarters.

2.12.s:
samāhṛtya tu tad bhaikṣaṃ yāvadarthamamāyayā /
bhuñjīta prayato nityaṃ vāgyato 'nanyamānasaḥ //
2.12.d:
समाहृत्य तु तद् भैक्षं यावदर्थममायया ।
भुञ्जीत प्रयतो नित्यं वाग्यतो ऽनन्यमानसः ॥
2.12.m: Having collected that alms-food according to his need, without deceit, / he should always eat it, purified, controlling his speech, with his mind focused on nothing else.

2.12.s:
bhaikṣyeṇa vartayennityaṃ naikānnādī bhaved vratī /
bhaikṣyeṇa vratino vṛttirupavāsasamā smṛtā //
2.12.d:
भैक्ष्येण वर्तयेन्नित्यं नैकान्नादी भवेद् व्रती ।
भैक्ष्येण व्रतिनो वृत्तिरुपवाससमा स्मृता ॥
2.12.m: He should always subsist on alms-food; one observing vows should not eat from a single donor's house. / The livelihood of one observing vows through alms-food is considered equal to fasting.

2.12.s:
pūjayedaśanaṃ nityamadyāccaitadakutsayan /
dṛṣṭvā hṛṣyet prasīdecca pratinandecca sarvaśaḥ //
2.12.d:
पूजयेदशनं नित्यमद्याच्चैतदकुत्सयन् ।
दृष्ट्वा हृष्येत् प्रसीदेच्च प्रतिनन्देच्च सर्वशः ॥
2.12.m: He should always revere food and eat it without reviling [it]; / seeing it, he should rejoice, be pleased, and welcome it in every way.

2.12.s:
anārogyamanāyuṣyamasvargyaṃ cātibhojanam /
apuṇyaṃ lokavidviṣṭaṃ tasmāt tatparivarjayet //
2.12.d:
अनारोग्यमनायुष्यमस्वर्ग्यं चातिभोजनम् ।
अपुण्यं लोकविद्विष्टं तस्मात् तत्परिवर्जयेत् ॥
2.12.m: Overeating brings ill health, shortens life, and bars heaven; / it is unmeritorious and despised by the world; therefore, one should avoid it.

2.12.s:
prāṅmukho 'nnāni bhuñjīta sūryābhimukha eva vā /
nādyādudaṅmukho nityaṃ vidhireṣa sanātanaḥ //
2.12.d:
प्राङ्मुखो ऽन्नानि भुञ्जीत सूर्याभिमुख एव वा ।
नाद्यादुदङ्मुखो नित्यं विधिरेष सनातनः ॥
2.12.m:
One should eat meals facing east, or facing the sun;
one must never eat facing north: this is the eternal rule.

2.12.s:
prakṣālya pāṇipādau ca bhuñjāno dvirupaspṛśet /
śucau deśe samāsīno bhuktvā ca dvirupaspṛśet //
itī śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.12.d:
प्रक्षाल्य पाणिपादौ च भुञ्जानो द्विरुपस्पृशेत् ।
शुचौ देशे समासीनो भुक्त्वा च द्विरुपस्पृशेत् ॥
इती श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे द्वादशो ऽध्यायः

2.13.s:
vyāsa uvāca
bhuktvā pītvā ca suptvā ca snātvā rathyopasarpaṇe /
oṣṭhāvalamokau spṛṣṭvā vāso viparidhāya ca //
2.13.d:
व्यास उवाच
भुक्त्वा पीत्वा च सुप्त्वा च स्नात्वा रथ्योपसर्पणे ।
ओष्ठावलमोकौ स्पृष्ट्वा वासो विपरिधाय च ॥

2.13.s:
retomūtrapurīṣāṇāmutsarge 'yuktabhāṣaṇe /
ṣṭhīvitvādhyayanārambhe kāsaśvāsāgame tathā //
2.13.d:
रेतोमूत्रपुरीषाणामुत्सर्गे ऽयुक्तभाषणे ।
ष्ठीवित्वाध्ययनारम्भे कासश्वासागमे तथा ॥
2.13.m:
at the discharge of semen, urine, or feces; upon improper speech;
after spitting; at the start of Vedic recitation; and at the onset of coughing or sighing;

2.13.s:
catvaraṃ vā śmaśānaṃ vā samākramya dvijottamaḥ /
saṃdhyayorubhayostadvadācānto 'pyācamet punaḥ //
2.13.d:
चत्वरं वा श्मशानं वा समाक्रम्य द्विजोत्तमः ।
संध्ययोरुभयोस्तद्वदाचान्तो ऽप्याचमेत् पुनः ॥
2.13.m:
or having stepped into a crossroads or a cremation ground, the best of the twice-born,
and likewise at both twilights, even if already rinsed, should rinse his mouth again.

2.13.s:
caṇḍālamlecchasaṃbhāṣe strīśūdrocchiṣṭabhāṣaṇe /
ucchiṣṭaṃ puruṣaṃ spṛṣṭvā bhojyaṃ cāpi tathāvidham /
ācāmedaśrupāte vā lohitasya tathaiva ca //
2.13.d:
चण्डालम्लेच्छसंभाषे स्त्रीशूद्रोच्छिष्टभाषणे ।
उच्छिष्टं पुरुषं स्पृष्ट्वा भोज्यं चापि तथाविधम् ।
आचामेदश्रुपाते वा लोहितस्य तथैव च ॥

2.13.s:
bhojane saṃdhyayoḥ snātvā pītvā mūtrapurīṣayoḥ /
ācānto 'pyācamet suptvā sakṛtsakṛdathānyataḥ //
2.13.d:
भोजने संध्ययोः स्नात्वा पीत्वा मूत्रपुरीषयोः ।
आचान्तो ऽप्याचमेत् सुप्त्वा सकृत्सकृदथान्यतः ॥
2.13.m:
At meals, at the two twilights, after bathing, after drinking, after voiding urine and feces,
and after sleeping, even if already rinsed, he should rinse; elsewhere, once each.

2.13.s:
agnergavāmathālambhe spṛṣṭvā prayatameva vā /
strīṇāmathātmanaḥ sparśe nīvīṃ vā paridhāya ca //
2.13.d:
अग्नेर्गवामथालम्भे स्पृष्ट्वा प्रयतमेव वा ।
स्त्रीणामथात्मनः स्पर्शे नीवीं वा परिधाय च ॥
2.13.m:
Upon touching fire or cows, or touching what is pure,
or upon touching women or oneself, or after tying one's lower garment;

2.13.s:
upaspṛśejjalaṃ vārdraṃ tṛṇaṃ vā bhūmimeva vā /
keśānāṃ cātmanaḥ sparśe vāsaso 'kṣālitasya ca //
2.13.d:
उपस्पृशेज्जलं वार्द्रं तृणं वा भूमिमेव वा ।
केशानां चात्मनः स्पर्शे वाससो ऽक्षालितस्य च ॥
2.13.m:
one should touch water, damp grass, or the earth;
and upon touching one's own hair, or an unwashed garment.

2.13.s:
anuṣṇābhiraphenābiraduṣṭābhiśca dharmataḥ /
śaucepsuḥ sarvadācāmedāsīnaḥ prāgudaṅmukhaḥ //
2.13.d:
अनुष्णाभिरफेनाबिरदुष्टाभिश्च धर्मतः ।
शौचेप्सुः सर्वदाचामेदासीनः प्रागुदङ्मुखः ॥
2.13.m:
With water that is not hot, free of foam, and unpolluted according to duty,
one desiring purity should always rinse while seated, facing east or north.

2.13.s:
śiraḥ prāvṛtya kaṇṭhaṃ vā muktakacchasikho 'pi vā /
akṛtvā pādayoḥ śaucamācānto 'pyaśucirbhavet //
2.13.d:
शिरः प्रावृत्य कण्ठं वा मुक्तकच्छसिखो ऽपि वा ।
अकृत्वा पादयोः शौचमाचान्तो ऽप्यशुचिर्भवेत् ॥
2.13.m:
Covering his head or neck, or with untied tuck or topknot,
or without having washed his feet, even if he rinses he remains impure.

2.13.s:
sopānatko jalastho vā noṣṇīṣī vācamed budhaḥ /
na caiva varṣadhārābhirna tiṣṭhan noddhṛtodakaiḥ //
2.13.d:
सोपानत्को जलस्थो वा नोष्णीषी वाचमेद् बुधः ।
न चैव वर्षधाराभिर्न तिष्ठन् नोद्धृतोदकैः ॥
2.13.m:
Wearing shoes, standing in water, or wearing a turban, a wise man must not rinse;
