nor with streams of rain, nor standing, nor with raised water;

2.13.s:
naikahastārpitajalairvinā sūtreṇa vā punaḥ /
na pādukāsanastho vā bahirjānurathāpi vā //
2.13.d:
नैकहस्तार्पितजलैर्विना सूत्रेण वा पुनः ।
न पादुकासनस्थो वा बहिर्जानुरथापि वा ॥
2.13.m:
nor with water offered from a single hand, nor without the sacred thread;
nor seated on wooden sandals, nor with his knees outside [his arms];

2.13.s:
na jalpan na hasan prekṣan śayānaḥ prahva eva ca /
nāvīkṣitābhiḥ phenādyairupetābhirathāpi vā //
2.13.d:
न जल्पन् न हसन् प्रेक्षन् शयानः प्रह्व एव च ।
नावीक्षिताभिः फेनाद्यैरुपेताभिरथापि वा ॥
2.13.m:
neither chattering, laughing, looking about, lying down, nor bent over;
nor with uninspected water, or water accompanied by foam and the like;

2.13.s:
śūdrāśucikaronmuktairna kṣārābhistathaiva ca /
na caivāṅgulibhiḥ śabdaṃ na kurvan nānyamānasaḥ //
2.13.d:
शूद्राशुचिकरोन्मुक्तैर्न क्षाराभिस्तथैव च ।
न चैवाङ्गुलिभिः शब्दं न कुर्वन् नान्यमानसः ॥
2.13.m:
nor with water released from the hand of a Śūdra or an impure person, nor with alkaline water;
making no sound with the fingers, and not distracted in mind;

2.13.s:
na varṇarasaduṣṭābhirna caiva pradarodakaiḥ /
na pāṇikṣubhitābhirvā na bahiṣkakṣa eva vā //
2.13.d:
न वर्णरसदुष्टाभिर्न चैव प्रदरोदकैः ।
न पाणिक्षुभिताभिर्वा न बहिष्कक्ष एव वा ॥
2.13.m:
nor with water spoiled in color or taste, nor with water from a chasm;
nor with water agitated by the hand, nor outside the hem of one's garment.

2.13.s:
hṛdgābhiḥ pūyate vipraḥ kaṇṭhyābhiḥ kṣatriyaḥ śuciḥ /
prāśitābhistathāvaiśyaḥ strīśūdrau sparśato 'ntataḥ //
2.13.d:
हृद्गाभिः पूयते विप्रः कण्ठ्याभिः क्षत्रियः शुचिः ।
प्राशिताभिस्तथावैश्यः स्त्रीशूद्रौ स्पर्शतो ऽन्ततः ॥
2.13.m:
A Brāhmaṇa is purified by water reaching the heart; a Kṣatriya is purified by water reaching the throat;
a Vaiśya by water tasted; a woman and a Śūdra by the mere touch at the end.

2.13.s:
aṅguṣṭhamūlāntarato rekhāyāṃ brāhmamucyate /
antarāṅguṣṭhadeśinyo pitṝṇāṃ tīrthamuttamam //
2.13.d:
अङ्गुष्ठमूलान्तरतो रेखायां ब्राह्ममुच्यते ।
अन्तराङ्गुष्ठदेशिन्यो पितॄणां तीर्थमुत्तमम् ॥
2.13.m:
Inside the base of the thumb, at the line, is called the Brāhma-tīrtha;
between the thumb and the forefinger is the excellent tīrtha of the ancestors;

2.13.s:
kaniṣṭhāmūlataḥ paścāt prājāpatyaṃ pracakṣate /
aṅgulyagre smṛtaṃ daivaṃ tadevārṣaṃ prakīrtitam //
2.13.d:
कनिष्ठामूलतः पश्चात् प्राजापत्यं प्रचक्षते ।
अङ्गुल्यग्रे स्मृतं दैवं तदेवार्षं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
2.13.m:
behind the base of the little finger, they proclaim the Prājāpatya;
at the tip of the fingers is recorded the Daiva, and that same is proclaimed the Ārṣa;

2.13.s:
mūle vā daivamārṣaṃ syādāgneyaṃ madhyataḥ smṛtaṃ /
tadeva saumikaṃ tīrthametajjñātvā na muhyati //
2.13.d:
मूले वा दैवमार्षं स्यादाग्नेयं मध्यतः स्मृतं ।
तदेव सौमिकं तीर्थमेतज्ज्ञात्वा न मुह्यति ॥
2.13.m:
or at the base it is Daiva and Ārṣa, and in the middle Āgneya is remembered;
that same is the Saumika tīrtha; knowing this, one is not confused.

2.13.s:
brāhmeṇaiva tu tīrthena dvijo nityamupaspṛśet /
kāyena vātha daivena tu pitryeṇa vai dvijāḥ //
2.13.d:
ब्राह्मेणैव तु तीर्थेन द्विजो नित्यमुपस्पृशेत् ।
कायेन वाथ दैवेन तु पित्र्येण वै द्विजाः ॥
2.13.m:
A twice-born should always rinse with the Brāhma tīrtha,
or with the Kāya, or with the Daiva, but twice-born [use] the Pitrya [for the ancestors].

2.13.s:
triḥ prāśnīyādapaḥ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prayatastataḥ /
saṃmṛjyāṅguṣṭhamūlena mukhaṃ vai samupaspṛśet //
2.13.d:
त्रिः प्राश्नीयादपः पूर्वं ब्राह्मणः प्रयतस्ततः ।
संमृज्याङ्गुष्ठमूलेन मुखं वै समुपस्पृशेत् ॥
2.13.m:
First, a Brāhmaṇa, being purified, should sip water three times;
then, wiping with the base of the thumb, he should touch his mouth.

2.13.s:
aṅguṣṭhānāmikābhyāṃ tu spṛśennetradvayaṃ tataḥ /
tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayogena spṛśennāsāpṛṭadvayam //
2.13.d:
अङ्गुष्ठानामिकाभ्यां तु स्पृशेन्नेत्रद्वयं ततः ।
तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठयोगेन स्पृशेन्नासापृटद्वयम् ॥
2.13.m:
With the thumb and ring finger he should then touch the two eyes;
with the joining of the forefinger and thumb he should touch the two nostrils.

2.13.s:
kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhayogena śravaṇe samupaspṛśet /
sarvāsāmatha yogena hṛdayaṃ tu talena vā /
saṃspṛśed vā śirastadvadaṅguṣṭhenāthavā dvayam //
2.13.d:
कनिष्ठाङ्गुष्ठयोगेन श्रवणे समुपस्पृशेत् ।
सर्वासामथ योगेन हृदयं तु तलेन वा ।
संस्पृशेद् वा शिरस्तद्वदङ्गुष्ठेनाथवा द्वयम् ॥

2.13.s:
triḥ prāśnīyād yadambhastu suprītāstena devatāḥ /
brahmā viṣṇurmaheśaśca bhavantītyanuśuśrumaḥ //
2.13.d:
त्रिः प्राश्नीयाद् यदम्भस्तु सुप्रीतास्तेन देवताः ।
ब्रह्मा विष्णुर्महेशश्च भवन्तीत्यनुशुश्रुमः ॥
2.13.m:
When he sips water three times, by that the deities are well pleased:
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa become so—thus we have heard.

2.13.s:
gaṅgā ca yamunā caiva prīyete parimārjanāt /
saṃspṛṣṭayorlocanayoḥ prīyete śaśibhāskarau //
2.13.d:
गङ्गा च यमुना चैव प्रीयेते परिमार्जनात् ।
संस्पृष्टयोर्लोचनयोः प्रीयेते शशिभास्करौ ॥
2.13.m:
Gaṅgā and Yamunā are pleased by the wiping;
when the eyes are touched, the moon and the sun are pleased.

2.13.s:
nāsatyadastrau prīyete spṛṣṭe nāsāpuṭadvaye /
karṇayoḥ spṛṣṭayostadvat prīyete cānilānalau //
2.13.d:
नासत्यदस्त्रौ प्रीयेते स्पृष्टे नासापुटद्वये ।
कर्णयोः स्पृष्टयोस्तद्वत् प्रीयेते चानिलानलौ ॥
2.13.m:
Nāsatya and Dasra are pleased when the two nostrils are touched;
likewise when the ears are touched, wind and fire are pleased.

2.13.s:
saṃspṛṣṭe hṛdaye cāsya prīyante sarvadevatāḥ /
mūrdhni saṃsparśanādekaḥ prītaḥ sa puruṣo bhavet //
2.13.d:
संस्पृष्टे हृदये चास्य प्रीयन्ते सर्वदेवताः ।
मूर्ध्नि संस्पर्शनादेकः प्रीतः स पुरुषो भवेत् ॥
2.13.m:
When his heart is touched, all the deities are pleased;
from touching the crown of the head, that one Spirit becomes pleased.

2.13.s:
nocchiṣṭaṃ kurvate mukhyā vipruṣo 'ṅgaṃ nayanti yāḥ /
dantavad dantalagneṣu jihvāsparśe 'śucirbhavet //
2.13.d:
नोच्छिष्टं कुर्वते मुख्या विप्रुषो ऽङ्गं नयन्ति याः ।
दन्तवद् दन्तलग्नेषु जिह्वास्पर्शे ऽशुचिर्भवेत् ॥
2.13.m:
Drops from the mouth that fall on the body do not make one ritually defiled;
particles stuck between the teeth are like teeth; touching them with the tongue makes one impure.

2.13.s:
spṛśānti bindavaḥ pādau ya ācāmayataḥ parān /
bhūmigaiste samā jñeyā na tairaprayato bhavet //
2.13.d:
स्पृशान्ति बिन्दवः पादौ य आचामयतः परान् ।
भूमिगैस्ते समा ज्ञेया न तैरप्रयतो भवेत् ॥
2.13.m:
Drops that touch the feet of one who is causing others to rinse
are to be considered equal to those fallen on the ground; one does not become impure by them.

2.13.s:
maduparke ca some ca tāmbūlasya ca bhakṣaṇe /
phalamūle cekṣudaṇḍe na doṣaṃ prāha ve manuḥ //
2.13.d:
मदुपर्के च सोमे च ताम्बूलस्य च भक्षणे ।
फलमूले चेक्षुदण्डे न दोषं प्राह वे मनुः ॥
2.13.m:
In the honey-mixture, in soma, in eating betel,
in fruits, roots, and sugarcane, Manu declared no fault.

2.13.s:
pracaraṃścānnapāneṣu dravyahasto bhavennaraḥ /
bhūmau nikṣipya tad dravyamācamyābhyukṣayet tu tat //
2.13.d:
प्रचरंश्चान्नपानेषु द्रव्यहस्तो भवेन्नरः ।
भूमौ निक्षिप्य तद् द्रव्यमाचम्याभ्युक्षयेत् तु तत् ॥
2.13.m:
A man moving about among food and drinks with an item in hand:
having placed that item on the ground, and having rinsed, he should sprinkle it.

2.13.s:
taijasaṃ vai samādāya yadyucchiṣṭo bhaved dvijaḥ /
bhūmau nikṣipya tad dravyamācamyābhyukṣayet tu tat //
2.13.d:
तैजसं वै समादाय यद्युच्छिष्टो भवेद् द्विजः ।
भूमौ निक्षिप्य तद् द्रव्यमाचम्याभ्युक्षयेत् तु तत् ॥
2.13.m:
If a twice-born, holding a metallic vessel, becomes ritually defiled,
having placed that item on the ground, and having rinsed, he should sprinkle it.

2.13.s:
yadyamatraṃ samādāya bhaveduccheṣaṇānvitaḥ /
anidhāyaiva tad dravyamācāntaḥ śucitāmiyāt /
vastrādiṣu vikalpaḥ syāt tatsaṃspṛṣṭvācamediha //
2.13.d:
यद्यमत्रं समादाय भवेदुच्छेषणान्वितः ।
अनिधायैव तद् द्रव्यमाचान्तः शुचितामियात् ।
वस्त्रादिषु विकल्पः स्यात् तत्संस्पृष्ट्वाचमेदिह ॥

2.13.s:
araṇye 'nudake rātrau cauravyāghrākule pathi /
kṛtvā mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā dravyahasto na duṣyati //
2.13.d:
अरण्ये ऽनुदके रात्रौ चौरव्याघ्राकुले पथि ।
कृत्वा मूत्रं पुरीषं वा द्रव्यहस्तो न दुष्यति ॥
2.13.m:
In the wilderness, where there is no water, at night, on a road beset with thieves and tigers,
having discharged urine or feces with an item in hand, he does not incur fault.

2.13.s:
nidhāya dakṣiṇe karṇe brahmasūtramudaṅmukhaḥ /
ahni kuryācchakṛnmūtraṃ rātrau ced dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ //
2.13.d:
निधाय दक्षिणे कर्णे ब्रह्मसूत्रमुदङ्मुखः ।
अह्नि कुर्याच्छकृन्मूत्रं रात्रौ चेद् दक्षिणामुखः ॥
2.13.m:
Placing the sacred thread on his right ear, facing north
he should discharge feces and urine by day; if by night, facing south.

2.13.s:
antardhāya mahīṃ kāṣṭhaiḥ patrairloṣṭhatṛṇena vā /
prāvṛtya ca śiraḥ kuryād viṇmūtrasya visarjanam //
2.13.d:
अन्तर्धाय महीं काष्ठैः पत्रैर्लोष्ठतृणेन वा ।
प्रावृत्य च शिरः कुर्याद् विण्मूत्रस्य विसर्जनम् ॥
2.13.m:
Covering the ground with pieces of wood, leaves, a clod of earth, or grass,
and having covered his head, he should perform the discharge of feces and urine.

2.13.s:
chāyākūpanadīgoṣṭhacaityāmbhaḥ pathi bhasmasu /
agnau caiva śmaśāne ca viṇmūtre na samācaret //
2.13.d:
छायाकूपनदीगोष्ठचैत्याम्भः पथि भस्मसु ।
अग्नौ चैव श्मशाने च विण्मूत्रे न समाचरेत् ॥
2.13.m:
In the shade, in a well, in a river, in a cow-pen, near a sacred tree or monument, in water, on a path, in ashes,
in fire, and in a cremation ground, he should not void feces or urine.

2.13.s:
na gomaye na kṛṣṭe vā mahāvṛkṣe na śāḍvale /
na tiṣṭhan vā na nirvāsā na ca parvatamastake //
2.13.d:
न गोमये न कृष्टे वा महावृक्षे न शाड्वले ।
न तिष्ठन् वा न निर्वासा न च पर्वतमस्तके ॥
2.13.m:
Neither on cow dung, nor on plowed ground, nor near a great tree, nor on grass,
nor standing, nor naked, nor on a mountain summit;

2.13.s:
na jīrṇadevāyatane na valmīke kadācana /
na sasattveṣu garteṣu na gacchan vā samācaret //
2.13.d:
न जीर्णदेवायतने न वल्मीके कदाचन ।
न ससत्त्वेषु गर्तेषु न गच्छन् वा समाचरेत् ॥
2.13.m:
never in a dilapidated temple, nor on an anthill,
nor into holes containing living creatures, nor walking should he void;

2.13.s:
tuṣāṅgārakapāleṣu rājamārge tathaiva ca /
na kṣetre na vile vāpi na tīrthe na catuṣpathe //
2.13.d:
तुषाङ्गारकपालेषु राजमार्गे तथैव च ।
न क्षेत्रे न विले वापि न तीर्थे न चतुष्पथे ॥
2.13.m:
on chaff, charcoal, potsherds, and likewise on the king's highway,
not in a field, nor in a pit, nor at a sacred bathing-place, nor at a crossroads;

2.13.s:
nodyānodasamīpe vā noṣare na parāśucau /
na sopānatpāduko vā chatrī vā nāntarikṣake //
2.13.d:
नोद्यानोदसमीपे वा नोषरे न पराशुचौ ।
न सोपानत्पादुको वा छत्री वा नान्तरिक्षके ॥
2.13.m:
nor near a garden or water, nor on barren soil, nor on another's impurity,
neither wearing shoes nor sandals, nor holding an umbrella, nor in the air;

2.13.s:
na caivābhimukhe strīṇāṃ gurubrāhmaṇayorgavām /
na devadevālayayorapāmapi kadācana //
2.13.d:
न चैवाभिमुखे स्त्रीणां गुरुब्राह्मणयोर्गवाम् ।
न देवदेवालययोरपामपि कदाचन ॥
2.13.m:
nor facing women, elders, Brāhmaṇas, or cows,
nor never facing a deity or a temple, nor water;

2.13.s:
na jyotīṃṣi nirīkṣanvānasaṃdhyābhimukho 'pivā /
pratyādityaṃ pratyanalaṃ pratisomaṃ tathaiva ca //
2.13.d:
न ज्योतींषि निरीक्षन्वानसंध्याभिमुखो ऽपिवा ।
प्रत्यादित्यं प्रत्यनलं प्रतिसोमं तथैव च ॥
2.13.m:
nor gazing at the luminaries, nor facing the twilight,
nor facing the sun, nor fire, and likewise not facing the moon.

2.13.s:
āhṛtya mṛttikāṃ kūlāllepagandhāpakarṣaṇam /
kuryādatandritaḥ śaucaṃ viśuddhairuddhṛtodakaiḥ //
2.13.d:
आहृत्य मृत्तिकां कूलाल्लेपगन्धापकर्षणम् ।
कुर्यादतन्द्रितः शौचं विशुद्धैरुद्धृतोदकैः ॥
2.13.m: Having fetched earth from a riverbank to remove smear and odor, / he should attentively perform purification with clean water drawn [from a reservoir].

2.13.s:
nāharenmṛttikāṃ vipraḥ pāṃśulānna ca kardamāt /
na mārgānnoṣarād deśācchaucaśiṣṭāṃ parasya ca //
2.13.d:
नाहरेन्मृत्तिकां विप्रः पांशुलान्न च कर्दमात् ।
न मार्गान्नोषराद् देशाच्छौचशिष्टां परस्य च ॥
2.13.m: A brahmin should not take earth from dusty soil or from mud, / nor from a road, nor from a saline region, nor the residue left by another after purification,

2.13.s:
na devāyatanāt kūpād grāmānna ca jalāt tathā /
upaspṛśet tato nityaṃ pūrvoktena vidhānataḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.13.d:
न देवायतनात् कूपाद् ग्रामान्न च जलात् तथा ।
उपस्पृशेत् ततो नित्यं पूर्वोक्तेन विधानतः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे त्रयोदशो ऽध्यायः
2.13.m:
nor from a temple, a well, a village, or likewise from [under] the water. / Then he should always sip water according to the rule previously stated.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.14.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evaṃ daṇḍādibhiryuktaḥ śaucācārasamanvitaḥ /
āhūto 'dhyayanaṃ kuryād vīkṣamāṇo gurormukham //
2.14.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवं दण्डादिभिर्युक्तः शौचाचारसमन्वितः ।
आहूतो ऽध्ययनं कुर्याद् वीक्षमाणो गुरोर्मुखम् ॥
2.14.m: Vyāsa said: / Thus equipped with the staff and [other requisites], endowed with purity of conduct, / he should study when summoned, looking at his guru's face.

2.14.s:
nityamudyatapāṇiḥ syāt sādhvācāraḥ susaṃyataḥ /
āsyatāmiti coktaḥ sannāsītābhimukhaṃ guroḥ //
2.14.d:
नित्यमुद्यतपाणिः स्यात् साध्वाचारः सुसंयतः ।
आस्यतामिति चोक्तः सन्नासीताभिमुखं गुरोः ॥
2.14.m: He should always have his hands raised [in respect], be of good conduct and well-restrained; / and when told, 'Be seated,' he should sit facing his guru.

2.14.s:
pratiśravaṇasaṃbhāṣe śayāno na samācaret /
nāsīno na ca bhuñjāno na tiṣṭhanna parāṅmukhaḥ //
2.14.d:
प्रतिश्रवणसंभाषे शयानो न समाचरेत् ।
नासीनो न च भुञ्जानो न तिष्ठन्न पराङ्मुखः ॥
2.14.m: He should not answer or converse while lying down, / nor while sitting, nor while eating, nor while standing, nor facing away.

2.14.s:
nīcaṃ śayyāsanaṃ cāsya sarvadā gurusannidhau /
gurostu cakṣurviṣaye na yatheṣṭāsano bhavet //
2.14.d:
नीचं शय्यासनं चास्य सर्वदा गुरुसन्निधौ ।
गुरोस्तु चक्षुर्विषये न यथेष्टासनो भवेत् ॥
2.14.m: His bed and seat should always be lower in the presence of his guru; / and within the sight of the guru, he should not sit as he pleases.

2.14.s:
nodāharedasya nāma parokṣamapi kevalam /
na caivāsyānukurvota gatibhāṣaṇaceṣṭitam //
2.14.d:
नोदाहरेदस्य नाम परोक्षमपि केवलम् ।
न चैवास्यानुकुर्वोत गतिभाषणचेष्टितम् ॥
2.14.m: He should not utter his [guru's] name alone, even when out of sight, / nor should he mimic his gait, speech, or gestures.

2.14.s:
guroryatra parīvādo nindā cāpi pravartate /
karṇaiṃ tatra pidhātavyau gantavyaṃ vā tato 'nyataḥ //
2.14.d:
गुरोर्यत्र परीवादो निन्दा चापि प्रवर्तते ।
कर्णैं तत्र पिधातव्यौ गन्तव्यं वा ततो ऽन्यतः ॥
2.14.m: Where censure or slander of the guru takes place, / he must cover both ears, or go away from there elsewhere.

2.14.s:
dūrastho nārcayedenaṃ na kruddho nāntike striyāḥ /
na caivāsyottaraṃ brūyāt sthito nāsīta sannidhau //
2.14.d:
दूरस्थो नार्चयेदेनं न क्रुद्धो नान्तिके स्त्रियाः ।
न चैवास्योत्तरं ब्रूयात् स्थितो नासीत सन्निधौ ॥
2.14.m: Standing far off, he should not honor him, nor when angry, nor near a woman; / he must never answer him back, nor remain seated when he is standing nearby.

2.14.s:
udakumbhaṃ kuśān puṣpaṃ samidho 'syāharet sadā /
mārjanaṃ lepanaṃ nityamaṅgānāṃ vai samācaret //
2.14.d:
उदकुम्भं कुशान् पुष्पं समिधो ऽस्याहरेत् सदा ।
मार्जनं लेपनं नित्यमङ्गानां वै समाचरेत् ॥
2.14.m: He should always bring him a water-jar, kuśa grass, flowers, and sacrificial wood; / he should always rub and massage his limbs.

2.14.s:
nāsya nirmālyaśayanaṃ pādukopānahāvapi /
ākramedāsanaṃ cāsya chāyādīn vā kadācana //
2.14.d:
नास्य निर्माल्यशयनं पादुकोपानहावपि ।
आक्रमेदासनं चास्य छायादीन् वा कदाचन ॥
2.14.m: He should never step upon his leftover offerings, bed, sandals, or shoes, / nor upon his seat, his shadow, and the like.

2.14.s:
sādhayed dantakāṣṭhādīn labdhaṃ cāsmai nivedayet /
anāpṛcchya na gantavyaṃ bhavet priyahite rataḥ //
2.14.d:
साधयेद् दन्तकाष्ठादीन् लब्धं चास्मै निवेदयेत् ।
अनापृच्छ्य न गन्तव्यं भवेत् प्रियहिते रतः ॥
2.14.m: He should prepare [his] tooth-cleaning sticks and other items, and offer him what he obtains; / he should not depart without asking permission, and should be devoted to what is pleasing and beneficial [to him].

2.14.s:
na pādau sārayedasya saṃnidhāne kadācana /
jṛmbhitaṃ hasitaṃ caiva kaṇṭhaprāvaraṇaṃ tathā /
varjayet sannidhau nityamavasphocanameva ca //
2.14.d:
न पादौ सारयेदस्य संनिधाने कदाचन ।
जृम्भितं हसितं चैव कण्ठप्रावरणं तथा ।
वर्जयेत् सन्निधौ नित्यमवस्फोचनमेव च ॥
2.14.m: He should never stretch out his feet in his presence; / yawning, laughing, and wrapping his throat, / as well as cracking his fingers, he should always avoid in his presence.

2.14.s:
yathākālamadhīyīta yāvanna vimanā guruḥ /
āsītādho guroḥ kūrce phalake vā samāhitaḥ //
2.14.d:
यथाकालमधीयीत यावन्न विमना गुरुः ।
आसीताधो गुरोः कूर्चे फलके वा समाहितः ॥
2.14.m: He should study at the proper time, so long as the guru is not dispirited; / he should sit lower than the guru on a grass mat or a wooden plank, composed in mind.

2.14.s:
āsane śayane yāne naiva tiṣṭhet kadācana /
dhāvantamanudhāveta gacchantamanugacchati //
2.14.d:
आसने शयने याने नैव तिष्ठेत् कदाचन ।
धावन्तमनुधावेत गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति ॥
2.14.m: He should never remain on a seat, a couch, or a vehicle [while the guru walks]; / he should run after him if he runs, and follow him as he walks.

2.14.s:
go 'śvoṣṭrayānaprāsādaprastareṣu kaṭeṣu ca /
āsīta guruṇā sārdhaṃ śilāphalakanauṣu ca //
2.14.d:
गो ऽश्वोष्ट्रयानप्रासादप्रस्तरेषु कटेषु च ।
आसीत गुरुणा सार्धं शिलाफलकनौषु च ॥
2.14.m: He may sit together with the guru in carriages drawn by oxen, horses, or camels, in palaces, / on rock slabs, on woven mats, on stone slabs, wooden planks, and in boats.

2.14.s:
jitendriyaḥ syāt satataṃ vaśyātmākrodhanaḥ śuciḥ /
prayuñjīta sadā vācaṃ madhurāṃ hitabhāṣiṇīm //
2.14.d:
जितेन्द्रियः स्यात् सततं वश्यात्माक्रोधनः शुचिः ।
प्रयुञ्जीत सदा वाचं मधुरां हितभाषिणीम् ॥
2.14.m: He should always keep his senses conquered, his mind controlled, free from anger, and pure; / he should always use gentle words that speak what is beneficial.

2.14.s:
gandhamālyaṃ rasaṃ kalyāṃ śuktaṃ prāṇivihiṃsanam /
abhyaṅgaṃ cāñcanopānacchatradhāraṇameva ca //
2.14.d:
गन्धमाल्यं रसं कल्यां शुक्तं प्राणिविहिंसनम् ।
अभ्यङ्गं चाञ्चनोपानच्छत्रधारणमेव च ॥
2.14.m: Perfumes, garlands, spices, wine, sour gruel, harming living beings, / anointing the body, applying collyrium, wearing shoes, and holding an umbrella,

2.14.s:
kāmaṃ lobhaṃ bhayaṃ nidrāṃ gītavāditranartanam /
ātarjanaṃ parīvādaṃ strīprekṣālambhanaṃ tathā /
paropaghātaṃ paiśunyaṃ prayatnena vivarjayet //
2.14.d:
कामं लोभं भयं निद्रां गीतवादित्रनर्तनम् ।
आतर्जनं परीवादं स्त्रीप्रेक्षालम्भनं तथा ।
परोपघातं पैशुन्यं प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.14.m: desire, greed, fear, sleep, singing, instrumental music, dancing, / threatening, slander, gazing at and touching women, / harming others, and backbiting—these he should scrupulously avoid.

2.14.s:
udakumbhaṃ sumanaso gośakṛnmṛttikāṃ kuśān /
āhared yāvadarthāni bhaikṣyaṃ cāharahaścaret //
2.14.d:
उदकुम्भं सुमनसो गोशकृन्मृत्तिकां कुशान् ।
आहरेद् यावदर्थानि भैक्ष्यं चाहरहश्चरेत् ॥
2.14.m: A water-jar, flowers, cow dung, earth, and kuśa grass / he should bring as needed, and he should go begging for alms day after day.

2.14.s:
kṛtaṃ ca lavaṇaṃ sarvaṃ varjyaṃ paryuṣitaṃ ca yat /
anṛtyadarśo satataṃ bhaved gītādiniḥ spṛhaḥ //
2.14.d:
कृतं च लवणं सर्वं वर्ज्यं पर्युषितं च यत् ।
अनृत्यदर्शो सततं भवेद् गीतादिनिः स्पृहः ॥
2.14.m: All prepared salt should be avoided, as well as food that is stale; / he should never watch dancing, and be free of desire for singing and similar things.

2.14.s:
nādityaṃ vai samīkṣeta na cared dantadhāvanam /
ekāntamaśucistrībhiḥ śūdrāntyairabhibhāṣaṇam //
2.14.d:
नादित्यं वै समीक्षेत न चरेद् दन्तधावनम् ।
एकान्तमशुचिस्त्रीभिः शूद्रान्त्यैरभिभाषणम् ॥
2.14.m: He should not gaze at the sun, nor clean his teeth [with twigs on prohibited occasions]; / he should never converse in private with impure women, Śūdras, or outcastes.

2.14.s:
gurūcchiṣṭaṃ bheṣajārthaṃ prayuñjīta na kāmataḥ /
kalāpakarṣaṇasnānaṃ nācareddhi kadācana //
2.14.d:
गुरूच्छिष्टं भेषजार्थं प्रयुञ्जीत न कामतः ।
कलापकर्षणस्नानं नाचरेद्धि कदाचन ॥
2.14.m: He should consume the guru's leftovers only for the purpose of medicine, not at will; / he should never take a bath that involves scrubbing the limbs for pleasure.

2.14.s:
na kuryānmānasaṃ vipro gurostyāge kadācana /
mohādvā yadi vā lobhāt tyaktena patito bhavet //
2.14.d:
न कुर्यान्मानसं विप्रो गुरोस्त्यागे कदाचन ।
मोहाद्वा यदि वा लोभात् त्यक्तेन पतितो भवेत् ॥
2.14.m: A brahmin should never set his mind on abandoning his guru; / if he is abandoned out of delusion or greed, he becomes fallen.

2.14.s:
laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ cāpi tathādhyātmikameva ca /
ādadīta yato jñānaṃ na taṃ druhyet kadācana //
2.14.d:
लौकिकं वैदिकं चापि तथाध्यात्मिकमेव च ।
आददीत यतो ज्ञानं न तं द्रुह्येत् कदाचन ॥
2.14.m: The one from whom he receives knowledge—secular, Vedic, / or spiritual—he must never wrong.

2.14.s:
gurorapyavaliptasya kāryākāryamajānataḥ /
utpathapratipannasya manustyāgaṃ samabravīt //
2.14.d:
गुरोरप्यवलिप्तस्य कार्याकार्यमजानतः ।
उत्पथप्रतिपन्नस्य मनुस्त्यागं समब्रवीत् ॥
2.14.m: Even of a guru who is arrogant, ignorant of what ought and ought not to be done, / and who has embarked on a deviant path, Manu declared abandonment [to be proper].

2.14.s:
gurorgurau sannihite guruvad bhaktimācaret /
na cātisṛṣṭo guruṇā svān gurūnabivādayet //
2.14.d:
गुरोर्गुरौ सन्निहिते गुरुवद् भक्तिमाचरेत् ।
न चातिसृष्टो गुरुणा स्वान् गुरूनबिवादयेत् ॥
2.14.m: When the guru's guru is present, he should show devotion as toward his own guru; / and without permission from his guru, he should not greet his own elders.

2.14.s:
vidyāguruṣvetadeva nityā vṛttiḥ svayoniṣu /
pratiṣedhatsu cādharmāddhitaṃ copadiśatsvapi //
2.14.d:
विद्यागुरुष्वेतदेव नित्या वृत्तिः स्वयोनिषु ।
प्रतिषेधत्सु चाधर्माद्धितं चोपदिशत्स्वपि ॥
2.14.m: This very conduct [applies] always toward teachers of knowledge and toward one's own kinsmen / who restrain him from unrighteousness and instruct him in what is beneficial.

2.14.s:
śreyaḥsu guruvad vṛttiṃ nityameva samācaret /
guruputreṣu dāreṣu guroścaiva svabandhuṣu //
2.14.d:
श्रेयःसु गुरुवद् वृत्तिं नित्यमेव समाचरेत् ।
गुरुपुत्रेषु दारेषु गुरोश्चैव स्वबन्धुषु ॥
2.14.m: He should always behave as toward his guru toward those who are superior, / toward the guru's sons, wives, and the guru's own relatives.

2.14.s:
bālaḥ samānajanmā vā śiṣyo vā yajñakarmaṇi /
adhyāpayan gurusuto guruvanmānamarhati //
2.14.d:
बालः समानजन्मा वा शिष्यो वा यज्ञकर्मणि ।
अध्यापयन् गुरुसुतो गुरुवन्मानमर्हति ॥
2.14.m: A guru's son who is younger, of equal age, or a fellow student in sacrificial rites, / who teaches him, deserves respect like the guru.

2.14.s:
utsādanaṃ vai gātrāṇāṃ snāpanocchiṣṭabhojane /
na kuryād guruputrasya pādayoḥ śaucameva ca //
2.14.d:
उत्सादनं वै गात्राणां स्नापनोच्छिष्टभोजने ।
न कुर्याद् गुरुपुत्रस्य पादयोः शौचमेव च ॥
2.14.m: He should not perform the rubbing down of limbs, bathing, eating of leftovers, / or the washing of feet for a guru's son.

2.14.s:
guruvat paripūjyāstu savarṇā guruyoṣitaḥ /
asavarṇāstu saṃpūjyāḥ pratyutthānābhivādanaiḥ //
2.14.d:
गुरुवत् परिपूज्यास्तु सवर्णा गुरुयोषितः ।
असवर्णास्तु संपूज्याः प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादनैः ॥
2.14.m: The guru's wives of the same caste are to be honored like the guru; / but those of a different caste are to be honored by rising up and greeting.

2.14.s:
abhyañjanaṃ snāpanaṃ ca gātrotsādanameva ca /
gurupatnyā na kāryāṇi keśānāṃ ca prasādhanam //
2.14.d:
अभ्यञ्जनं स्नापनं च गात्रोत्सादनमेव च ।
गुरुपत्न्या न कार्याणि केशानां च प्रसाधनम् ॥
2.14.m: Anointing, bathing, massaging the limbs, / and dressing the hair are not to be done for a guru's wife.

2.14.s:
gurupatnī tu yuvatī nābhivādyeha pādayoḥ /
kurvota vandanaṃ bhūmyāmasāvahamiti bruvan //
2.14.d:
गुरुपत्नी तु युवती नाभिवाद्येह पादयोः ।
कुर्वोत वन्दनं भूम्यामसावहमिति ब्रुवन् ॥
2.14.m: A young wife of the guru should not be greeted by touching her feet here; / he should make obeisance on the ground, saying, 'I am so-and-so.'

2.14.s:
viproṣya pādagrahaṇamanvahaṃ cābhivādanam /
gurudāreṣu kurvota satāṃ dharmamanusmaran //
2.14.d:
विप्रोष्य पादग्रहणमन्वहं चाभिवादनम् ।
गुरुदारेषु कुर्वोत सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन् ॥
2.14.m: Returning from a journey, he should clasp the feet [of the guru's wife] and make daily obeisance / toward the guru's wives, remembering the duty of the virtuous.

2.14.s:
mātṛṣvasā mātulānī śvaśrūścātha pitṛṣvasā /
saṃpūjyā gurupatnīva samāstā gurubhāryayā //
2.14.d:
मातृष्वसा मातुलानी श्वश्रूश्चाथ पितृष्वसा ।
संपूज्या गुरुपत्नीव समास्ता गुरुभार्यया ॥
2.14.m: A maternal aunt, a maternal uncle's wife, a mother-in-law, and a paternal aunt / are to be revered like a guru's wife; they are equal to a guru's wife.

2.14.s:
bhrāturbhāryopasaṃgrāhyā savarṇāhanyahanyapi /
viproṣya tūpasaṃgrāhyā jñātisaṃbandhiyoṣitaḥ //
2.14.d:
भ्रातुर्भार्योपसंग्राह्या सवर्णाहन्यहन्यपि ।
विप्रोष्य तूपसंग्राह्या ज्ञातिसंबन्धियोषितः ॥
2.14.m: A brother's wife of the same caste should be greeted by clasping her feet day after day; / but the women among one's kinsmen and relatives are to be greeted thus only upon returning from a journey.

2.14.s:
piturbhaginyāṃ mātuśca jyāyasyāṃ ca svasaryapi /
mātṛvad vṛttimātiṣṭhenmāt tābhyo garīyasī //
2.14.d:
पितुर्भगिन्यां मातुश्च ज्यायस्यां च स्वसर्यपि ।
मातृवद् वृत्तिमातिष्ठेन्मात् ताभ्यो गरीयसी ॥
2.14.m: Toward a father's sister, a mother's [sister], and an elder sister, / he should behave as toward a mother; yet a mother is more venerable than them.

2.14.s:
evamācārasaṃpannamātmavantamadāmbhikam /
vedamadhyāpayed dharmaṃ purāṇāṅgāni nityaśaḥ //
2.14.d:
एवमाचारसंपन्नमात्मवन्तमदाम्भिकम् ।
वेदमध्यापयेद् धर्मं पुराणाङ्गानि नित्यशः ॥
2.14.m: To [a student] endowed with such conduct, self-controlled, and free from deceit, / he should continuously teach the Veda, righteousness, the Purāṇas, and the auxiliary sciences.

2.14.s:
saṃvatsaroṣite śiṣye gururjñānamanirdiśan /
harate duṣkṛtaṃ tasya śiṣyasya vasato guruḥ //
2.14.d:
संवत्सरोषिते शिष्ये गुरुर्ज्ञानमनिर्दिशन् ।
हरते दुष्कृतं तस्य शिष्यस्य वसतो गुरुः ॥
2.14.m: If a guru does not impart knowledge to a disciple who has dwelt [with him] for a year, / the guru takes on the misdeeds of that dwelling disciple.

2.14.s:
ācāryaputraḥ śuśrūṣurjñānado dhārmikaḥ śuciḥ /
śakto 'nnador'tho svaḥsādhuradhyāpyā daśa dharmataḥ //
2.14.d:
आचार्यपुत्रः शुश्रूषुर्ज्ञानदो धार्मिकः शुचिः ।
शक्तो ऽन्नदोर्ऽथो स्वःसाधुरध्याप्या दश धर्मतः ॥
2.14.m: A teacher's son, one who is obedient, an imparter of knowledge, a righteous person, one who is pure, / one who is capable, a provider of food, one who offers wealth, one's own kinsman, and a virtuous person—these ten are fit to be taught according to dharma.

2.14.s:
kṛtajñaśca tathādrohī medhāvī śubhakṛnnaraḥ /
āptaḥ priyo 'tha vidhivat ṣaḍadhyāpyā dvijātayaḥ /
eteṣu brahmaṇo dānamanyatra tu yathoditān //
2.14.d:
कृतज्ञश्च तथाद्रोही मेधावी शुभकृन्नरः ।
आप्तः प्रियो ऽथ विधिवत् षडध्याप्या द्विजातयः ।
एतेषु ब्रह्मणो दानमन्यत्र तु यथोदितान् ॥
2.14.m: Grateful, free from malice, intelligent, doing good, / trustworthy, and affectionate—these six types of twice-born are to be taught according to rule. / To these the gift of the Veda [is given], and to others as stated.

2.14.s:
ācamya saṃyato nityamadhīyīta udaṅmukhaḥ /
upasaṃgṛhya tatpādau vīkṣamāṇo gurormukham /
adhīṣva bho iti brūyād virāmo 'stviti cāramet //
2.14.d:
आचम्य संयतो नित्यमधीयीत उदङ्मुखः ।
उपसंगृह्य तत्पादौ वीक्षमाणो गुरोर्मुखम् ।
अधीष्व भो इति ब्रूयाद् विरामो ऽस्त्विति चारमेत् ॥
2.14.m: Having sipped water, self-controlled, facing north, he should constantly study. / Having grasped both [the teacher's] feet and gazing at the teacher's face, / [the teacher] should say, 'Recite, sir!' and [the student] should cease when he says, 'Let there be a pause.'

2.14.s:
prākkūlān paryupāsīnaḥ pavitraiścaiva pāvitaḥ /
prāṇāyāmaistribhiḥ pūtastata oṅkāramarhati //
2.14.d:
प्राक्कूलान् पर्युपासीनः पवित्रैश्चैव पावितः ।
प्राणायामैस्त्रिभिः पूतस्तत ओङ्कारमर्हति ॥
2.14.m: Sitting near [kusa-blades] whose tips point east, purified by blades of kusa grass, / cleansed by three breath-controls, he is then worthy of the syllable Oṃ.

2.14.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ praṇavaṃ kuryādante ca vidhivad dvijaḥ /
kuryādadhyayanaṃ nityaṃ sa brahmāñjalipūrvataḥ //
2.14.d:
ब्राह्मणः प्रणवं कुर्यादन्ते च विधिवद् द्विजः ।
कुर्यादध्ययनं नित्यं स ब्रह्माञ्जलिपूर्वतः ॥
2.14.m: The twice-born brāhmaṇa should utter the syllable oṃ at the beginning and the end according to rule; / he should always study after first making the respectful posture with folded hands for Brahman.

2.14.s:
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ vedaścakṣuḥ sanātanam /
adhīyītāpyayaṃ nityaṃ brāhmaṇyāccyavate 'nyathā //
2.14.d:
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां वेदश्चक्षुः सनातनम् ।
अधीयीताप्ययं नित्यं ब्राह्मण्याच्च्यवते ऽन्यथा ॥
2.14.m: The Veda is the eternal eye of all beings; / he should study it daily, otherwise he falls from his status as a brāhmaṇa.

2.14.s:
yo 'dhīyīta ṛco nityaṃ kṣīrāhutyā sa devatāḥ /
prīṇāti tarpayantyenaṃ kāmaistṛptāḥ sadaiva hi //
2.14.d:
यो ऽधीयीत ऋचो नित्यं क्षीराहुत्या स देवताः ।
प्रीणाति तर्पयन्त्येनं कामैस्तृप्ताः सदैव हि ॥
2.14.m: He who studies the ṛc-verses daily pleases the deities with an oblation of milk; / satisfied, they always delight him with desired objects.

2.14.s:
yajūṃṣyadhīte niyataṃ dadhnā prīṇāti devatāḥ /
sāmānyadhīte prīṇāti ghṛtāhutibhiranvaham //
2.14.d:
यजूंष्यधीते नियतं दध्ना प्रीणाति देवताः ।
सामान्यधीते प्रीणाति घृताहुतिभिरन्वहम् ॥
2.14.m: He who regularly studies the yajus-formulas pleases the deities with curd; / he who studies the sāman-chants pleases them daily with oblations of clarified butter.

2.14.s:
atharvāṅgiraso nityaṃ madhvā prīṇāti devatāḥ /
dharmāṅgāni purāṇāni māṃsaistarpayate surān //
2.14.d:
अथर्वाङ्गिरसो नित्यं मध्वा प्रीणाति देवताः ।
धर्माङ्गानि पुराणानि मांसैस्तर्पयते सुरान् ॥
2.14.m: He pleases the deities daily with honey through the Atharvan and Aṅgiras hymns; / he satisfies the gods with flesh through the limbs of dharma and the Purāṇas.

2.14.s:
apāṃ samīpe niyato naityakaṃ vidhimāśritaḥ /
gāyatrīmapyadhīyīta gatvāraṇyaṃ samāhitaḥ //
2.14.d:
अपां समीपे नियतो नैत्यकं विधिमाश्रितः ।
गायत्रीमप्यधीयीत गत्वारण्यं समाहितः ॥
2.14.m: Restrained near the waters, relying on the obligatory daily ritual, / and going to the forest, he should recite the Gāyatrī with a focused mind.

2.14.s:
sahasraparamāṃ devīṃ śatamadhyāṃ daśāvarām /
gāyatrīṃ vai japennityaṃ japayajñaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
2.14.d:
सहस्रपरमां देवीं शतमध्यां दशावराम् ।
गायत्रीं वै जपेन्नित्यं जपयज्ञः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
2.14.m: A thousand times at best, a hundred times as the middle, ten times at least— / one should indeed repeat the divine Gāyatrī daily; this is proclaimed as the sacrifice of recitation.

2.14.s:
gāyatrīṃ caiva vedāṃśca tulayātolayat prabhuḥ /
ekataścaturo vedān gāyatrīṃ ca tathaikataḥ //
2.14.d:
गायत्रीं चैव वेदांश्च तुलयातोलयत् प्रभुः ।
एकतश्चतुरो वेदान् गायत्रीं च तथैकतः ॥
2.14.m: The Lord weighed on a scale both the Gāyatrī and the Vedas: / the four Vedas on one side, and the Gāyatrī likewise on the other.

2.14.s:
oṅkāramāditaḥ kṛtvā vyāhṛtīstadanantaram /
tato 'dhīyīta sāvitrīmekāgraḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ //
2.14.d:
ओङ्कारमादितः कृत्वा व्याहृतीस्तदनन्तरम् ।
ततो ऽधीयीत सावित्रीमेकाग्रः श्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
2.14.m: Placing the syllable oṃ at the beginning, immediately followed by the mystical utterances, / he should then recite the Sāvitrī, one-pointed and endowed with faith.

2.14.s:
purākalpe samutpannā bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥ sanātanāḥ /
mahāvyāhṛtayastistraḥ sarvāśubhanibarhaṇāḥ //
2.14.d:
पुराकल्पे समुत्पन्ना भूर्भुवःस्वः सनातनाः ।
महाव्याहृतयस्तिस्त्रः सर्वाशुभनिबर्हणाः ॥
2.14.m: Bhuḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ arose in an ancient era as eternal; / they are the three great mystical utterances that destroy all misfortune.

2.14.s:
pradhānaṃ puruṣaḥ kālo viṣṇurbrahmā maheśvaraḥ /
sattvaṃ rajastamastistraḥ kramād vyāhṛtayaḥ smṛtāḥ //
2.14.d:
प्रधानं पुरुषः कालो विष्णुर्ब्रह्मा महेश्वरः ।
सत्त्वं रजस्तमस्तिस्त्रः क्रमाद् व्याहृतयः स्मृताः ॥
2.14.m: Primordial matter, spirit, time; Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Maheśvara; / goodness, passion, darkness: these are taught as the three mystical utterances in order.

2.14.s:
oṅkārastat paraṃ brahma sāvitrī syāt tadakṣaram /
eṣa mantro mahāyogaḥ sārāt sāra udāhṛtaḥ //
2.14.d:
ओङ्कारस्तत् परं ब्रह्म सावित्री स्यात् तदक्षरम् ।
एष मन्त्रो महायोगः सारात् सार उदाहृतः ॥
2.14.m: The syllable oṃ is that supreme Brahman; the Sāvitrī is that imperishable syllable; / this mantra is the great yoga, declared to be the essence of essence.

2.14.s:
yo 'dhīte 'hanyahanyetāṃ gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram /
vijñāyārthaṃ brahmacārī sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
2.14.d:
यो ऽधीते ऽहन्यहन्येतां गायत्रीं वेदमातरम् ।
विज्ञायार्थं ब्रह्मचारी स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.14.m: The celibate student who, knowing its meaning, recites day after day this Gāyatrī, / the mother of the Vedas, goes to the supreme state.

2.14.s:
gāyatrī vedajananī gāyatrī lokapāvanī /
na gāyatryāḥ paraṃ japyametad vijñāya mucyate //
2.14.d:
गायत्री वेदजननी गायत्री लोकपावनी ।
न गायत्र्याः परं जप्यमेतद् विज्ञाय मुच्यते ॥
2.14.m: The Gāyatrī is the mother of the Vedas; the Gāyatrī purifies the worlds; / there is nothing to be repeated that is higher than the Gāyatrī; knowing this, one is liberated.

2.14.s:
śrāvaṇasya tu māsasya paurṇamāsyāṃ dvijottamāḥ /
āṣāḍhyāṃ proṣṭhapadyāṃ vā vedopākaraṇaṃ smṛtam //
2.14.d:
श्रावणस्य तु मासस्य पौर्णमास्यां द्विजोत्तमाः ।
आषाढ्यां प्रोष्ठपद्यां वा वेदोपाकरणं स्मृतम् ॥
2.14.m: On the full moon of the month of Śrāvaṇa, O best of the twice-born, / or on that of Āṣāḍha or of Prauṣṭhapada, the commencement of Vedic study is prescribed.

2.14.s:
utsṛjya grāmanagaraṃ māsān vipror'ddhapañcamān /
adhīyīta śucau deśe brahmacārī samāhitaḥ //
2.14.d:
उत्सृज्य ग्रामनगरं मासान् विप्रोर्ऽद्धपञ्चमान् ।
अधीयीत शुचौ देशे ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः ॥
2.14.m: Leaving the village and the city, the celibate student, focused in a pure place, / should study for four and a half months.

2.14.s:
puṣye tu chandasāṃ kuryād bahirutsarjanaṃ dvijaḥ /
māghaśuklasya vā prāpte pūrvāhne prathame 'hani //
2.14.d:
पुष्ये तु छन्दसां कुर्याद् बहिरुत्सर्जनं द्विजः ।
माघशुक्लस्य वा प्राप्ते पूर्वाह्ने प्रथमे ऽहनि ॥
2.14.m: In the Puṣya asterism, the twice-born should perform the suspension of Vedic meters outside, / or when the first day of the light fortnight of Māgha has arrived in the forenoon.

2.14.s:
chandāṃsyūrdhvamathobhyasyecchuklapakṣeṣu vai dvijaḥ /
vedāṅgāni purāṇāni kṛṣṇapakṣe ca mānavam //
2.14.d:
छन्दांस्यूर्ध्वमथोभ्यस्येच्छुक्लपक्षेषु वै द्विजः ।
वेदाङ्गानि पुराणानि कृष्णपक्षे च मानवम् ॥
2.14.m: Thereafter, the twice-born should repeat the meters during the light fortnights, / and the Vedic auxiliary sciences, the Purāṇas, and the Manu-code during the dark fortnights.

2.14.s:
imān nityamanadhyāyānadīyāno vivarjayet /
adhyāpanaṃ ca kurvāṇo hyabhyasyannapi yatnataḥ //
2.14.d:
इमान् नित्यमनध्यायानदीयानो विवर्जयेत् ।
अध्यापनं च कुर्वाणो ह्यभ्यस्यन्नपि यत्नतः ॥
2.14.m: A student should constantly avoid these times unfit for study while reciting, / while teaching, and while diligently practicing.

2.14.s:
karṇaśrave 'nile rātrau divā pāṃśusamūhane /
vidyutstanitavarṣeṣu maholkānāṃ ca saṃplave /
ākālikamanadhyāyameteṣvāha prajāpatiḥ //
2.14.d:
कर्णश्रवे ऽनिले रात्रौ दिवा पांशुसमूहने ।
विद्युत्स्तनितवर्षेषु महोल्कानां च संप्लवे ।
आकालिकमनध्यायमेतेष्वाह प्रजापतिः ॥
2.14.m: When wind is audible to the ear, during the night, when dust swirls during the day, / in lightning, thunder, and rain, and during a fall of large meteors, / Prajāpati has declared an intermission of study for that duration.

2.14.s:
etānabhyuditān vidyād yadā prāduṣkṛtāgniṣu /
tadā vidyādanadhyāyamanṛtau cābhradarśane //
2.14.d:
एतानभ्युदितान् विद्याद् यदा प्रादुष्कृताग्निषु ।
तदा विद्यादनध्यायमनृतौ चाभ्रदर्शने ॥
2.14.m: One should know that when these occur while the sacred fires have been brought forth, / and when clouds appear out of season, that is a time unfit for study.

2.14.s:
nirghāte bhūmicalane jyotiṣāṃ copasarjane /
etānākālikān vidyādanadhyāyānṛtāvapi //
2.14.d:
निर्घाते भूमिचलने ज्योतिषां चोपसर्जने ।
एतानाकालिकान् विद्यादनध्यायानृतावपि ॥
2.14.m: During a thunderstroke, an earthquake, and an eclipse of the luminaries, / one should know that these are intermissions of study for that duration, even in the proper season.

2.14.s:
prāduṣkṛteṣvagniṣu tu vidyutstanitanisvane /
sajyotiḥ syādanadhyāyaḥ śeṣarātrau yathā divā //
2.14.d:
प्रादुष्कृतेष्वग्निषु तु विद्युत्स्तनितनिस्वने ।
सज्योतिः स्यादनध्यायः शेषरात्रौ यथा दिवा ॥
2.14.m: When the sacred fires have been brought forth, during the sound of lightning and thunder, / the cessation of study lasts as long as the light continues, in the remainder of the night as during the day.

2.14.s:
nityānadhyāya eva syād grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca /
dharmanaipuṇyakāmānāṃ pūtigandhe ca nityaśaḥ //
2.14.d:
नित्यानध्याय एव स्याद् ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च ।
धर्मनैपुण्यकामानां पूतिगन्धे च नित्यशः ॥
2.14.m: In villages and cities, there should constantly be an intermission of study / for those who desire perfection in dharma, and always when there is a foul odor.

2.14.s:
antaḥ śavagate grāme vṛṣalasya ca sannidhau /
anadhyāyo rudyamāne samavāye janasya ca //
2.14.d:
अन्तः शवगते ग्रामे वृषलस्य च सन्निधौ ।
अनध्यायो रुद्यमाने समवाये जनस्य च ॥
2.14.m: When a corpse is inside the village, and in the presence of a śūdra, / while weeping is heard, and in an assembly of people, there is an intermission of study.

2.14.s:
udake madhyarātre ca viṇmūtre ca visarjane /
ucchiṣṭaḥ śrāddhabuk caiva manasāpi na cintayet //
2.14.d:
उदके मध्यरात्रे च विण्मूत्रे च विसर्जने ।
उच्छिष्टः श्राद्धबुक् चैव मनसापि न चिन्तयेत् ॥
2.14.m: In water, at midnight, and while evacuating feces and urine, / one who is impure and one who has eaten at an ancestral offering rite should not recite even in thought.

2.14.s:
pratigṛhya dvijo vidvānekodiṣṭasya ketanam /
tryahaṃ na kīrtayed brahma rājño rāhośca sūtake //
2.14.d:
प्रतिगृह्य द्विजो विद्वानेकोदिष्टस्य केतनम् ।
त्र्यहं न कीर्तयेद् ब्रह्म राज्ञो राहोश्च सूतके ॥
2.14.m: Having accepted an invitation to a rite for a single ancestor, the learned twice-born / should not recite the sacred text for three days, nor during the ritual impurity of a king or of Rāhu.

2.14.s:
yāvadeko 'nudiṣṭasya sneho gandhaśca tiṣṭhati /
viprasya viduṣo dehe tāvad brahma na kīrtayet //
2.14.d:
यावदेको ऽनुदिष्टस्य स्नेहो गन्धश्च तिष्ठति ।
विप्रस्य विदुषो देहे तावद् ब्रह्म न कीर्तयेत् ॥
2.14.m: As long as the oil and scent of a rite for a single deceased remain / on the body of the learned brāhmaṇa, so long he should not recite the sacred text.

2.14.s:
śayānaḥ prauḍhapādaśca kṛtvā caivāvasakthikām /
nādhīyītāmiṣaṃ jagdhvā sūtakānnādyameva ca //
2.14.d:
शयानः प्रौढपादश्च कृत्वा चैवावसक्थिकाम् ।
नाधीयीतामिषं जग्ध्वा सूतकान्नाद्यमेव च ॥
2.14.m: Lying down, with feet raised, or with a band tied around the knees, / having eaten meat, or food of birth-impurity, he should not study.

2.14.s:
nīhāre bāṇaśabde ca saṃdhyayorubhayorapi /
amāvāsyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ paurṇamāsyaṣṭamīṣu ca //
2.14.d:
नीहारे बाणशब्दे च संध्ययोरुभयोरपि ।
अमावास्यां चतुर्दश्यां पौर्णमास्यष्टमीषु च ॥
2.14.m: In fog, at the sound of an arrow, at both twilights, / on the new moon, on the fourteenth day, on the full moon, and on the eighth days;

2.14.s:
upākarmaṇi cotsarge trirātraṃ kṣapaṇaṃ smṛtam /
aṣṭakāsu tvahorātraṃ ṛtvantyāsu ca rātriṣu //
2.14.d:
उपाकर्मणि चोत्सर्गे त्रिरात्रं क्षपणं स्मृतम् ।
अष्टकासु त्वहोरात्रं ऋत्वन्त्यासु च रात्रिषु ॥
2.14.m: At the commencement of study and at its suspension, an interruption of three nights is prescribed; / but on the Aṣṭakā days, for a day and a night, and on the nights that end a season.

2.14.s:
mārgaśīrṣe tathā pauṣe māghamāse tathaiva ca /
tistro 'ṣṭakāḥ samākhyātā kṛṣṇapakṣetu sūribhiḥ //
2.14.d:
मार्गशीर्षे तथा पौषे माघमासे तथैव च ।
तिस्त्रो ऽष्टकाः समाख्याता कृष्णपक्षेतु सूरिभिः ॥
2.14.m: In Mārgaśīrṣa, in Pauṣa, and likewise in the month of Māgha, / three Aṣṭakā days in the dark fortnight are declared by the wise.

2.14.s:
śleṣmātakasya chāyāyāṃ śālmalermadhukasya ca /
kadācidapi nādhyeyaṃ kovidārakapitthayoḥ //
2.14.d:
श्लेष्मातकस्य छायायां शाल्मलेर्मधुकस्य च ।
कदाचिदपि नाध्येयं कोविदारकपित्थयोः ॥
2.14.m: In the shade of a śleṣmātaka, of a silk-cotton tree, and of a madhuka, / one must never study, nor under a kovidāra and a wood-apple tree.

2.14.s:
samānavidye ca mṛte tathā sabrahmacāriṇi /
ācārye saṃsthite vāpi trirātraṃ kṣapaṇaṃ smṛtam //
2.14.d:
समानविद्ये च मृते तथा सब्रह्मचारिणि ।
आचार्ये संस्थिते वापि त्रिरात्रं क्षपणं स्मृतम् ॥
2.14.m: When a scholar of equal learning has died, and likewise a fellow-student, / or when the teacher has passed away, an interruption of three nights is prescribed.

2.14.s:
chidrāṇyetāni viprāṇāṃye 'nadhyāyaḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
hiṃsanti rākṣasāsteṣu tasmādetān vivarjayet //
2.14.d:
छिद्राण्येतानि विप्राणांये ऽनध्यायः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
हिंसन्ति राक्षसास्तेषु तस्मादेतान् विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.14.m: These occasions declared unfit for study are vulnerabilities of brāhmaṇas; / rākṣasas harm them during these times; therefore, one should avoid them.

2.14.s:
naityake nāstyanadhyāyaḥ saṃdhyopāsana eva ca /
upākarmaṇi karmānte homamantreṣu caiva hi //
2.14.d:
नैत्यके नास्त्यनध्यायः संध्योपासन एव च ।
उपाकर्मणि कर्मान्ते होममन्त्रेषु चैव हि ॥
2.14.m: There is no intermission of study in obligatory daily recitation, nor in the twilight worship, / nor at the commencement of study, nor at the end of a rite, nor in the formulas for fire offerings.

2.14.s:
ekāmṛcamathaikaṃ vā yajuḥ sāmāthavā punaḥ /
aṣṭakādyāsvadhīyīta mārute cātivāyati //
2.14.d:
एकामृचमथैकं वा यजुः सामाथवा पुनः ।
अष्टकाद्यास्वधीयीत मारुते चातिवायति ॥
2.14.m: One may recite a single ṛc-verse, or a single yajus-formula, or again a sāman-chant / on the Aṣṭakā and other days, and when the wind blows excessively.

2.14.s:
anadhyāyastu nāṅgeṣu netihāsapurāṇayoḥ /
na dharmaśāstreṣvanyeṣu parvaṇyetāni varjayet //
2.14.d:
अनध्यायस्तु नाङ्गेषु नेतिहासपुराणयोः ।
न धर्मशास्त्रेष्वन्येषु पर्वण्येतानि वर्जयेत् ॥
2.14.m: There is no intermission of study in the auxiliary sciences, nor in the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, / nor in the other treatises on dharma; one should avoid these only on the joint-days.

2.14.s:
eṣa dharmaḥ samāsena kīrtito brahmacāriṇām /
brahmaṇābhihitaḥ pūrvamṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām //
2.14.d:
एष धर्मः समासेन कीर्तितो ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ।
ब्रह्मणाभिहितः पूर्वमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम् ॥
2.14.m: This duty of celibate students has been proclaimed in brief, / as declared of old by Brahmā to the sages of purified minds.

2.14.s:
yo 'nyatra kurute yatnamanadhītya śrutiṃ dvijaḥ /
sa saṃmūḍho na saṃbhāṣyo vedabāhyo dvijātibhiḥ //
2.14.d:
यो ऽन्यत्र कुरुते यत्नमनधीत्य श्रुतिं द्विजः ।
स संमूढो न संभाष्यो वेदबाह्यो द्विजातिभिः ॥
2.14.m: The twice-born who strives elsewhere without studying the revealed scripture / is completely deluded; excluded from the Veda, he should not be spoken to by twice-born persons.

2.14.s:
na vedapāṭhamātreṇa saṃtuṣṭo vai bhaved dvijaḥ /
pāṭhamātrāvasannastu paṅke gauriva sīdati //
2.14.d:
न वेदपाठमात्रेण संतुष्टो वै भवेद् द्विजः ।
पाठमात्रावसन्नस्तु पङ्के गौरिव सीदति ॥
2.14.m: A twice-born person should not be satisfied merely with reciting the Veda; / one who sinks merely into recitation sinks down like a cow in the mud.

2.14.s:
yo 'dhītya vidhivad vedaṃ vedārthaṃ na vicārayet /
sasānvayaḥ śūdrakalpaḥ pātratāṃ na prapadyate //
2.14.d:
यो ऽधीत्य विधिवद् वेदं वेदार्थं न विचारयेत् ।
ससान्वयः शूद्रकल्पः पात्रतां न प्रपद्यते ॥
2.14.m: He who, having studied the Veda according to rule, does not reflect upon its meaning, / is, along with his family, like a śūdra; he does not attain the status of a worthy recipient.

2.14.s:
yadi tvātyantikaṃ vāsaṃ kartumicchati vai gurau /
yuktaḥ paricaredenamāśarīravimokṣaṇāt //
2.14.d:
यदि त्वात्यन्तिकं वासं कर्तुमिच्छति वै गुरौ ।
युक्तः परिचरेदेनमाशरीरविमोक्षणात् ॥
2.14.m: If, however, he desires to dwell permanently with the guru, / he should serve him with devotion until the release from his body.

2.14.s:
gatvā vanaṃ vā vidhivajjuhuyājjātavedasam /
adhīyīta sadā nityaṃ brahmaniṣṭhaḥ samāhitaḥ //
2.14.d:
गत्वा वनं वा विधिवज्जुहुयाज्जातवेदसम् ।
अधीयीत सदा नित्यं ब्रह्मनिष्ठः समाहितः ॥
2.14.m: Or, having gone to the forest, he should offer oblations to the fire according to rule; / he should always study continually, intent on Brahman, with a focused mind.

2.14.s:
sāvitrīṃ śatarudrīyaṃ vedāntāṃśca viśeṣataḥ /
abhyaset satataṃ yukte bhasmasnānaparāyaṇaḥ //
2.14.d:
सावित्रीं शतरुद्रीयं वेदान्तांश्च विशेषतः ।
अभ्यसेत् सततं युक्ते भस्मस्नानपरायणः ॥
2.14.m: Endowed with discipline and devoted to bathing in ashes, / he should constantly repeat the Sāvitrī, the Śatarudrīya, and especially the Upaniṣads.

2.14.s:
etad vidhānaṃ paramaṃ purāṇaṃ
vedāgame samyagiheritaṃ vaḥ /
purā maharṣipravarābhipṛṣṭaḥ
svāyaṃbhuvo yanmanurāha devaḥ //
2.14.d:
एतद् विधानं परमं पुराणं
वेदागमे सम्यगिहेरितं वः ।
पुरा महर्षिप्रवराभिपृष्टः
स्वायंभुवो यन्मनुराह देवः ॥
2.14.m: This supreme, ancient ordinance taught in the Vedic tradition / has been fully related here to you, which the divine Manu Svāyambhuva declared / of old when questioned by the foremost great sages.

2.14.s:
evamīśvarasamarpitāntaro
yo 'nutiṣṭhati vidhiṃ vidhānavit /
mohajālamapahāya so 'mṛto
yāti tat padamanāmayaṃ śivam //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.14.d:
एवमीश्वरसमर्पितान्तरो
यो ऽनुतिष्ठति विधिं विधानवित् ।
मोहजालमपहाय सो ऽमृतो
याति तत् पदमनामयं शिवम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे चतुर्दशो ऽध्यायः
2.14.m:
The knower of ordinances who, having surrendered his inner self to the Lord, / performs the ordinance in this manner, casting off the snare of delusion, / becomes immortal and goes to that auspicious state free from disease.

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the holy Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.15.s:
vyāsa uvāca
vedaṃ vedau tathā vedān vedān vā caturo dvijāḥ /
adhītya cādhigamyārthaṃ tataḥ snāyād dvijottamaḥ //
2.15.d:
व्यास उवाच
वेदं वेदौ तथा वेदान् वेदान् वा चतुरो द्विजाः ।
अधीत्य चाधिगम्यार्थं ततः स्नायाद् द्विजोत्तमः ॥
2.15.m: Vyāsa said: / Having studied one Veda, two Vedas, [three] Vedas, or all four Vedas, O twice-born ones, / and having comprehended their meaning, the best of the twice-born should then take the bath.

2.15.s:
gurave tu varaṃ dattvā snāyīta tadanujñayā /
cīrṇavrato 'tha yuktātmā saśaktaḥ snātumarhati //
2.15.d:
गुरवे तु वरं दत्त्वा स्नायीत तदनुज्ञया ।
चीर्णव्रतो ऽथ युक्तात्मा सशक्तः स्नातुमर्हति ॥
2.15.m: Having given a gift of choice to the teacher, he should bathe with his permission. / Having completed his vows, disciplined in self, capable, he is fit to bathe.

2.15.s:
vaiṇavīṃ dhārayed yaṣṭimantarvāsastathottaram /
yajñopavītadvitayaṃ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum //
2.15.d:
वैणवीं धारयेद् यष्टिमन्तर्वासस्तथोत्तरम् ।
यज्ञोपवीतद्वितयं सोदकं च कमण्डलुम् ॥
2.15.m: He should carry a bamboo staff, an undergarment, an upper garment, / two sacred threads, and a water-pot with water.

2.15.s:
chatraṃ coṣṇīṣamamalaṃ pāduke cāpyupānahau /
raukme ca kuṇḍale vedaṃ kṛttakeśanakhaḥ śuciḥ //
2.15.d:
छत्रं चोष्णीषममलं पादुके चाप्युपानहौ ।
रौक्मे च कुण्डले वेदं कृत्तकेशनखः शुचिः ॥
2.15.m: An umbrella, a clean turban, wooden sandals, and shoes, / two gold earrings, and the Veda; his hair and nails clipped, pure.

2.15.s:
svādhyāye nityayuktaḥ syād bahirmālyaṃ na dhārayet /
anyatrakāñcanād vipronaraktāṃ bibhṛyāt strajam //
2.15.d:
स्वाध्याये नित्ययुक्तः स्याद् बहिर्माल्यं न धारयेत् ।
अन्यत्रकाञ्चनाद् विप्रोनरक्तां बिभृयात् स्त्रजम् ॥
2.15.m: He should always be engaged in personal study; he should not wear a garland on the outside; / except for a gold one, a twice-born should not wear a red wreath.

2.15.s:
śuklāmbaradharo nityaṃ sugandhaḥ priyadarśanaḥ /
na jīrṇamalavadvāsā bhaved vai vibhave sati //
2.15.d:
शुक्लाम्बरधरो नित्यं सुगन्धः प्रियदर्शनः ।
न जीर्णमलवद्वासा भवेद् वै विभवे सति ॥
2.15.m: Always wearing white garments, sweet-smelling, pleasing in appearance; / he should not wear worn-out or dirty clothes if he possesses the means.

2.15.s:
na raktamulbaṇaṃ cānyadhṛtaṃ vāso na kuṇḍikām /
nopānahau strajaṃ cātha pāduke ca prayojayet //
2.15.d:
न रक्तमुल्बणं चान्यधृतं वासो न कुण्डिकाम् ।
नोपानहौ स्त्रजं चाथ पादुके च प्रयोजयेत् ॥
2.15.m: He should not wear a red or gaudy garment, nor one worn by another, nor [use another's] water-jar; / nor should he use another's shoes, garland, or sandals.

2.15.s:
upavītamalaṅkāraṃ darbhān kṛṣṇājināni ca /
nāpasavyaṃ parīdadhyād vāso na vikṛtaṃ vaset //
2.15.d:
उपवीतमलङ्कारं दर्भान् कृष्णाजिनानि च ।
नापसव्यं परीदध्याद् वासो न विकृतं वसेत् ॥
2.15.m: The sacred thread, ornamentation, kuśa grass, and black-antelope skins / he should not put on in the reverse way; nor should he wear a disfigured garment.

2.15.s:
āhared vidhivad dārān sadṛśānātmanaḥ śubhān /
rūpalakṣaṇasaṃyuktān yonidoṣavivarjitān //
2.15.d:
आहरेद् विधिवद् दारान् सदृशानात्मनः शुभान् ।
रूपलक्षणसंयुक्तान् योनिदोषविवर्जितान् ॥
2.15.m: He should take a wife according to rule, equal [in caste] to himself, auspicious, / endowed with beauty and good bodily marks, and free from faults of maternal descent.

2.15.s:
amātṛgotraprabhavāmasamānarṣigotrajām /
āhared brāhmaṇo bhāryāṃ śīlaśaucasamanvitām //
2.15.d:
अमातृगोत्रप्रभवामसमानर्षिगोत्रजाम् ।
आहरेद् ब्राह्मणो भार्यां शीलशौचसमन्विताम् ॥
2.15.m: Born outside of his mother's lineage, not born of the lineage of the same sage— / such a wife a Brahmin should take, one endowed with good conduct and purity.

2.15.s:
ṛtukālābhigāmī syād yāvat putro 'bhijāyate /
varjayet pratiṣiddhāni prayatnena dināni tu //
2.15.d:
ऋतुकालाभिगामी स्याद् यावत् पुत्रो ऽभिजायते ।
वर्जयेत् प्रतिषिद्धानि प्रयत्नेन दिनानि तु ॥
2.15.m: He should approach her during the fertile season until a son is born; / but he should carefully avoid the forbidden days.

2.15.s:
ṣaṣṭhyaṣṭamīṃ pañcadaśīṃ dvādaśīṃ ca caturdaśīm /
brahmacārī bhavennityaṃ tadvajjanmatrayāhani //
2.15.d:
षष्ठ्यष्टमीं पञ्चदशीं द्वादशीं च चतुर्दशीम् ।
ब्रह्मचारी भवेन्नित्यं तद्वज्जन्मत्रयाहनि ॥
2.15.m: On the sixth, eighth, fifteenth, twelfth, and fourteenth [lunar days], / he should always remain celibate, and likewise on the three days of his birth-star.

2.15.s:
ādadhītāvasathyāgniṃ juhuyājjātavedasam /
vratāni snātako nityaṃ pāvanāni ca pālayet //
2.15.d:
आदधीतावसथ्याग्निं जुहुयाज्जातवेदसम् ।
व्रतानि स्नातको नित्यं पावनानि च पालयेत् ॥
2.15.m: He should establish the domestic fire and offer oblations to Jātavedas; / as a snātaka, he should always observe purifying vows.

2.15.s:
vedoditaṃ svakaṃ karma nityaṃ kuryādatandritaḥ /
akurvāṇaḥ patatyāśu narakānatibhīṣaṇān //
2.15.d:
वेदोदितं स्वकं कर्म नित्यं कुर्यादतन्द्रितः ।
अकुर्वाणः पतत्याशु नरकानतिभीषणान् ॥
2.15.m: He should constantly and unweariedly perform his own duty prescribed by the Veda; / not performing it, he falls quickly into terrifying hells.

2.15.s:
abyaset prayato vedaṃ mahāyajñān na hāpayet /
kuryād gṛhyāṇi karmāṇi saṃdhyopāsanameva ca //
2.15.d:
अब्यसेत् प्रयतो वेदं महायज्ञान् न हापयेत् ।
कुर्याद् गृह्याणि कर्माणि संध्योपासनमेव च ॥
2.15.m: He should recite the Veda with devotion, and not neglect the great sacrifices; / he should perform the domestic rituals and the twilight worship.

2.15.s:
sakhyaṃ samādhaikaiḥ kuryādupeyādīśvaraṃ sadā /
daivatānyapi gaccheta kuryād bhāryābhipoṣaṇam //
2.15.d:
सख्यं समाधैकैः कुर्यादुपेयादीश्वरं सदा ।
दैवतान्यपि गच्छेत कुर्याद् भार्याभिपोषणम् ॥
2.15.m: He should form friendships with equals or superiors, and always revere God; / he should also visit deities and maintain his wife.

2.15.s:
na dharmaṃ khyāpayed vidvān na pāpaṃ gūhayedapi /
kurvotātmahitaṃ nityaṃ sarvabhūtānikampakaḥ //
2.15.d:
न धर्मं ख्यापयेद् विद्वान् न पापं गूहयेदपि ।
कुर्वोतात्महितं नित्यं सर्वभूतानिकम्पकः ॥
2.15.m: The wise man should not proclaim his righteousness, nor should he conceal sin; / he should constantly act for his own spiritual welfare, showing compassion to all beings.

2.15.s:
vayasaḥ karmaṇor'thasya śrutasyābhijanasya ca /
veṣavāgbuddhisārūpyamācaran vicaret sadā //
2.15.d:
वयसः कर्मणोर्ऽथस्य श्रुतस्याभिजनस्य च ।
वेषवाग्बुद्धिसारूप्यमाचरन् विचरेत् सदा ॥
2.15.m: In accordance with his age, actions, wealth, sacred learning, and family lineage, / he should always conduct himself, conforming his dress, speech, and intellect to them.

2.15.s:
śrutismṛtyuditaḥ samyak sādhubhiryaśca sevitaḥ /
tamācāraṃ niṣeveta nehetānyatra karhicit //
2.15.d:
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितः सम्यक् साधुभिर्यश्च सेवितः ।
तमाचारं निषेवेत नेहेतान्यत्र कर्हिचित् ॥
2.15.m: Conduct that is properly set forth in revelation and tradition, and practiced by the virtuous— / he should follow that conduct and never pursue anything else.

2.15.s:
yenāsya pitaro yātā yena yātāḥ pitāmahāḥ /
tena yāyāt satāṃ mārgaṃ tena gacchan na riṣyati //
2.15.d:
येनास्य पितरो याता येन याताः पितामहाः ।
तेन यायात् सतां मार्गं तेन गच्छन् न रिष्यति ॥
2.15.m: By the path along which his fathers have gone, and by which his grandfathers have gone, / along that path of the good he should proceed; proceeding by it, he does not come to harm.

2.15.s:
nityaṃ svādhyāyaśīlaḥ syānnityaṃ yajñopavītavān /
satyavādī jitakrodho brahmabhūyāya kalpate //
2.15.d:
नित्यं स्वाध्यायशीलः स्यान्नित्यं यज्ञोपवीतवान् ।
सत्यवादी जितक्रोधो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
2.15.m: He should always be devoted to personal study and always wear the sacred thread; / speaking truth and having conquered anger, he is fit to attain the state of Brahman.

2.15.s:
saṃdhyāsnānaparo nityaṃ brahmayajñuparāyaṇaḥ /
anasūyī mṛdurdānto gṛhasthaḥ pretya vardhate //
2.15.d:
संध्यास्नानपरो नित्यं ब्रह्मयज्ञुपरायणः ।
अनसूयी मृदुर्दान्तो गृहस्थः प्रेत्य वर्धते ॥
2.15.m: Always devoted to bathing at twilight and dedicated to the sacrifice of reciting the Veda, / free from malice, gentle, and self-controlled, a householder prospers in the next world.

2.15.s:
vītarāgabhayakrodho lobhamohavivarjitaḥ /
sāvitrījāpyanirataḥ śrāddhakṛnmucyate gṛhī //
2.15.d:
वीतरागभयक्रोधो लोभमोहविवर्जितः ।
सावित्रीजाप्यनिरतः श्राद्धकृन्मुच्यते गृही ॥
2.15.m: Free from attachment, fear, and anger, and devoid of greed and delusion, / devoted to murmuring the Sāvitrī, performing the ancestral offering rite, the householder is liberated.

2.15.s:
mātāpitrorhite yukto gobrāhmaṇahite rataḥ /
dānto yajvā devabhakto brahmaloke mahīyate //
2.15.d:
मातापित्रोर्हिते युक्तो गोब्राह्मणहिते रतः ।
दान्तो यज्वा देवभक्तो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
2.15.m: Engaged in the welfare of mother and father, devoted to the welfare of cows and Brahmins, / self-controlled, a performer of sacrifices, devoted to the gods, he is honored in the world of Brahmā.

2.15.s:
trivargasevī satataṃ devatānāṃ ca pūjanam /
kuryādaharaharnityaṃ namasyet prayataḥ surān //
2.15.d:
त्रिवर्गसेवी सततं देवतानां च पूजनम् ।
कुर्यादहरहर्नित्यं नमस्येत् प्रयतः सुरान् ॥
2.15.m: Pursuing the three aims of life constantly, and worshiping the deities, / he should daily and continuously bow down with devotion to the gods.

2.15.s:
vibhāgaśīlaḥ satataṃ kṣamāyukto dayālukaḥ /
gṛhasthastu samākhyāto na gṛheṇa gṛhī bhavet //
2.15.d:
विभागशीलः सततं क्षमायुक्तो दयालुकः ।
गृहस्थस्तु समाख्यातो न गृहेण गृही भवेत् ॥
2.15.m: Always disposed to sharing, endowed with patience, and compassionate— / such a one is called a householder; one does not become a householder merely by [having] a house.

2.15.s:
kṣamā dayā ca vijñānaṃ satyaṃ caiva damaḥ śamaḥ /
adhyātmanirataṃ jñānametad brāhmaṇalakṣaṇam //
2.15.d:
क्षमा दया च विज्ञानं सत्यं चैव दमः शमः ।
अध्यात्मनिरतं ज्ञानमेतद् ब्राह्मणलक्षणम् ॥
2.15.m: Patience, compassion, discernment, truth, self-restraint, tranquility, / and knowledge devoted to the supreme self—this is the characteristic of a Brahmin.

2.15.s:
etasmānna pramādyeta viśeṣeṇa dvijottamaḥ /
yathāśaktiṃ caran karma ninditāni vivarjayet //
2.15.d:
एतस्मान्न प्रमाद्येत विशेषेण द्विजोत्तमः ।
यथाशक्तिं चरन् कर्म निन्दितानि विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.15.m: From this the best of the twice-born should especially not deviate; / performing rites according to his ability, he should avoid blameworthy deeds.

2.15.s:
vidhūya mohakalilaṃ labdhvā yogamanuttamam /
gṛhastho mucyate bandhāt nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
2.15.d:
विधूय मोहकलिलं लब्ध्वा योगमनुत्तमम् ।
गृहस्थो मुच्यते बन्धात् नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
2.15.m: Having shaken off the impurity of delusion and attained unsurpassable yoga, / the householder is freed from bondage; herein there should be no doubt.

2.15.s:
vigarhātikramākṣepahiṃsābandhavadhātmanām /
anyamanyusamutthānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ marṣaṇaṃ kṣamā //
2.15.d:
विगर्हातिक्रमाक्षेपहिंसाबन्धवधात्मनाम् ।
अन्यमन्युसमुत्थानां दोषाणां मर्षणं क्षमा ॥
2.15.m: Enduring offenses arising reciprocally among people, / such as reproach, transgression, insults, violence, imprisonment, and murder, is patience.

2.15.s:
svaduḥ kheṣviva kāruṇyaṃ paraduḥ kheṣu sauhṛdāt /
dayeti munayaḥ prāhuḥ sākṣād dharmasya sādhanam //
2.15.d:
स्वदुः खेष्विव कारुण्यं परदुः खेषु सौहृदात् ।
दयेति मुनयः प्राहुः साक्षाद् धर्मस्य साधनम् ॥
2.15.m: Compassion toward the sufferings of others out of friendship, as if they were one's own sufferings— / this the sages call mercy, the direct means of righteousness.

2.15.s:
caturdaśānāṃ vidyānāṃ dhāraṇaṃ hi yatārthataḥ /
vijñānamiti tad vidyād yena dharmo vivardhate //
2.15.d:
चतुर्दशानां विद्यानां धारणं हि यतार्थतः ।
विज्ञानमिति तद् विद्याद् येन धर्मो विवर्धते ॥
2.15.m: Retaining in truth the fourteen branches of learning— / one should know that to be discernment, by which righteousness increases.

2.15.s:
adhītya vidhivad vidyāmarthaṃ caivopalabhya tu /
dharmakāryānnivṛttaścenna tad vijñānamiṣyate //
2.15.d:
अधीत्य विधिवद् विद्यामर्थं चैवोपलभ्य तु ।
धर्मकार्यान्निवृत्तश्चेन्न तद् विज्ञानमिष्यते ॥
2.15.m: Even having studied sacred learning according to rule and comprehended its meaning, / if one turns away from acts of righteousness, that is not recognized as discernment.

2.15.s:
satyena lokāñjayati satyaṃ tatparamaṃ padam /
yathābhūtapravād tu satyamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
2.15.d:
सत्येन लोकाञ्जयति सत्यं तत्परमं पदम् ।
यथाभूतप्रवाद् तु सत्यमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
2.15.m: Through truth one conquers the worlds; truth is that supreme state; / wise men call truth the stating of things as they truly are.

2.15.s:
damaḥ śarīroparamaḥ śamaḥ prajñāprisādajaḥ /
adhyātmamakṣaraṃ vidyād yatra gatvā na śocati //
2.15.d:
दमः शरीरोपरमः शमः प्रज्ञाप्रिसादजः ।
अध्यात्ममक्षरं विद्याद् यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ॥
2.15.m: Restraint is the cessation of the bodily senses; tranquility arises from the clarity of intellect; / one should know the supreme self as the imperishable, having gone to which one does not grieve.

2.15.s:
yayā sa devo bhagavān vidyayā vedyate paraḥ /
sākṣād devo mahādevastajjñānamiti kīrtitam //
2.15.d:
यया स देवो भगवान् विद्यया वेद्यते परः ।
साक्षाद् देवो महादेवस्तज्ज्ञानमिति कीर्तितम् ॥
2.15.m: The knowledge by which that supreme, blessed God, / Mahādeva directly, is known—that is proclaimed as wisdom.

2.15.s:
tanniṣṭhastatparo vidvānnityamakrodhanaḥ śuciḥ /
mahāyajñaparo vipro labhate tadanuttamam //
2.15.d:
तन्निष्ठस्तत्परो विद्वान्नित्यमक्रोधनः शुचिः ।
महायज्ञपरो विप्रो लभते तदनुत्तमम् ॥
2.15.m: Dedicated to that, intent on that, wise, constantly free from anger, pure, / and devoted to the great sacrifices, the Brahmin attains that unsurpassable state.

2.15.s:
dharmasyāyatanaṃ yatnāccharīraṃ paripālayet /
na hi dehaṃ vinā rudraḥ puruṣairvidyate paraḥ //
2.15.d:
धर्मस्यायतनं यत्नाच्छरीरं परिपालयेत् ।
न हि देहं विना रुद्रः पुरुषैर्विद्यते परः ॥
2.15.m: One should diligently protect the body, which is the abode of righteousness; / for without a body, the supreme Rudra is not known by men.

2.15.s:
nityadharmārthakāmeṣu yujyeta niyato dvijaḥ /
na dharmavarjitaṃ kāmamarthaṃ vā manasā smaret //
2.15.d:
नित्यधर्मार्थकामेषु युज्येत नियतो द्विजः ।
न धर्मवर्जितं काममर्थं वा मनसा स्मरेत् ॥
2.15.m: A restrained twice-born should be engaged in constant duty, wealth, and desire; / he should not even think in his mind of desire or wealth divorced from duty.

2.15.s:
sīdannapi hi dharmeṇa na tvadharmaṃ samācaret /
dharmo hi bhagavān devo gatiḥ sarveṣu jantuṣu //
2.15.d:
सीदन्नपि हि धर्मेण न त्वधर्मं समाचरेत् ।
धर्मो हि भगवान् देवो गतिः सर्वेषु जन्तुषु ॥
2.15.m: Even while suffering, he should not practice unrighteousness instead of duty; / for duty is the blessed God, the refuge among all living beings.

2.15.s:
bhūtānāṃ priyakārī syāt na paradrohakarmadhīḥ /
na vedadevatānindāṃ kuryāt taiśca na saṃvaset //
2.15.d:
भूतानां प्रियकारी स्यात् न परद्रोहकर्मधीः ।
न वेददेवतानिन्दां कुर्यात् तैश्च न संवसेत् ॥
2.15.m: He should do what is pleasing to living beings, not having a mind set on malice toward others; / he should not revile the Vedas or the deities, nor should he live with those who do.

2.15.s:
yastvimaṃ niyataṃ vipro dharmādhyāyaṃ paṭhecchuciḥ /
adhyāpayet śrāvayed vā brahmaloke mahīyate //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.15.d:
यस्त्विमं नियतं विप्रो धर्माध्यायं पठेच्छुचिः ।
अध्यापयेत् श्रावयेद् वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे पञ्चदशो ऽध्यायः
2.15.m:
The Brahmin who, self-controlled and pure, recites this chapter on duty, / or teaches it or causes it to be heard, is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the holy Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.16.s:
vyāsa uvāca
na hiṃsyāt sarvabhūtāninānṛtaṃ vāvadet kvacit /
nāhitaṃ nāpriyaṃ vākyaṃ na stenaḥ syād kadācana //
2.16.d:
व्यास उवाच
न हिंस्यात् सर्वभूतानिनानृतं वावदेत् क्वचित् ।
नाहितं नाप्रियं वाक्यं न स्तेनः स्याद् कदाचन ॥
2.16.m: Vyāsa said: / One should not harm any living beings, nor ever speak an untruth; / one should not speak words that are harmful or disagreeable, and one should never be a thief.

2.16.s:
tṛṇaṃ vā yadi vā śākaṃ mṛdaṃ vā jalameva vā /
parasyāpaharañjanturnarakaṃ pratipadyate //
2.16.d:
तृणं वा यदि वा शाकं मृदं वा जलमेव वा ।
परस्यापहरञ्जन्तुर्नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
2.16.m: Whether grass or vegetable, earth or even water, / taking what belongs to another, a creature falls into hell.

2.16.s:
na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna śūdrapatitādapi /
na cānyasmādaśaktaśca ninditān varjayed budhaḥ //
2.16.d:
न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न शूद्रपतितादपि ।
न चान्यस्मादशक्तश्च निन्दितान् वर्जयेद् बुधः ॥
2.16.m: A wise man should not accept gifts from a king, nor from a Śūdra or a fallen man; / and unable [to sustain himself], he should not accept from any other censured person; he should avoid them.

2.16.s:
nityaṃ yācanako na syāt punastaṃ naiva yācayet /
prāṇānapaharatyevaṃ yācakastasya durmatiḥ //
2.16.d:
नित्यं याचनको न स्यात् पुनस्तं नैव याचयेत् ।
प्राणानपहरत्येवं याचकस्तस्य दुर्मतिः ॥
2.16.m: One should not be a perpetual beggar; one must not beg from that same person again. / A beggar of evil intent takes away his vital breaths in this way.

2.16.s:
na devadravyahārī syād viśeṣeṇa dvijottamaḥ /
brahmasvaṃ vā nāpaharedāpadyapi kadācana //
2.16.d:
न देवद्रव्यहारी स्याद् विशेषेण द्विजोत्तमः ।
ब्रह्मस्वं वा नापहरेदापद्यपि कदाचन ॥
2.16.m: One should not take the property of a deity, especially an excellent twice-born; / nor should one ever seize the property of a Brahmin, even in distress.

2.16.s:
na viṣaṃ viṣamityāhurbrahmasvaṃ viṣamucyate /
devasvaṃ cāpi yatnena sadā pariharet tataḥ //
2.16.d:
न विषं विषमित्याहुर्ब्रह्मस्वं विषमुच्यते ।
देवस्वं चापि यत्नेन सदा परिहरेत् ततः ॥
2.16.m: They say that poison is not poison; the property of a Brahmin is called poison. / Therefore, one should also diligently avoid the property of a deity.

2.16.s:
puṣpe śākrodake kāṣṭhe tathā mūle phale tṛṇe /
adattādānamasteyaṃ manuḥ prāha prajāpatiḥ //
2.16.d:
पुष्पे शाक्रोदके काष्ठे तथा मूले फले तृणे ।
अदत्तादानमस्तेयं मनुः प्राह प्रजापतिः ॥
2.16.m: Taking without it being given is not theft in the case of flowers, vegetables, water, wood, / as well as roots, fruits, and grass—so said the lord of creatures, Manu.

2.16.s:
grahītavyāni puṣpāṇi devārcanavidhau dvijāḥ /
naikasmādeva niyatamananujñāya kevalam //
2.16.d:
ग्रहीतव्यानि पुष्पाणि देवार्चनविधौ द्विजाः ।
नैकस्मादेव नियतमननुज्ञाय केवलम् ॥
2.16.m: Flowers should be gathered for the rite of worshipping a deity, O twice-born; / but certainly not constantly from a single person without permission.

2.16.s:
tṛṇaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ prakāśaṃ vai hared budhaḥ /
dharmārthaṃ kevalaṃ viprā hyanyathā patito bhavet //
2.16.d:
तृणं काष्ठं फलं पुष्पं प्रकाशं वै हरेद् बुधः ।
धर्मार्थं केवलं विप्रा ह्यन्यथा पतितो भवेत् ॥
2.16.m: A wise man may openly take grass, wood, fruit, and flower / solely for the sake of religious duty, O Brahmins; otherwise, he becomes fallen.

2.16.s:
tilamudgayavādīnāṃ muṣṭirgrāhyā pathi sthitaiḥ /
kṣudhārtairnānyathā viprā dharmavidbhiriti sthitiḥ //
2.16.d:
तिलमुद्गयवादीनां मुष्टिर्ग्राह्या पथि स्थितैः ।
क्षुधार्तैर्नान्यथा विप्रा धर्मविद्भिरिति स्थितिः ॥
2.16.m: A handful of sesame, beans, barley, and the like may be taken by those on a journey / who are afflicted by hunger, but not otherwise, O Brahmins; such is the rule of those who know duty.

2.16.s:
na dharmasyāpadeśena pāpaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caret /
vratena pāpaṃ pracchādya kurvan strīśūdradambhanam //
2.16.d:
न धर्मस्यापदेशेन पापं कृत्वा व्रतं चरेत् ।
व्रतेन पापं प्रच्छाद्य कुर्वन् स्त्रीशूद्रदम्भनम् ॥
2.16.m: One should not perform a vow having committed a sin under the pretext of religious duty, / concealing sin through a vow and practicing deceit on women and Śūdras.

2.16.s:
pretyeha cedṛśo vipro garhyate brahmavādibhiḥ /
chadmanācaritaṃ yacca vrataṃ rakṣāṃsi gacchati //
2.16.d:
प्रेत्येह चेदृशो विप्रो गर्ह्यते ब्रह्मवादिभिः ।
छद्मनाचरितं यच्च व्रतं रक्षांसि गच्छति ॥
2.16.m: Such a Brahmin is censured here and in the hereafter by knowers of Brahman; / and a vow performed with hypocrisy goes to the demons.

2.16.s:
aliṅgī liṅgiveṣeṇa yo vṛttimupajīvati /
sa liṅgināṃ haredenastiryagyonau ca jāyate //
2.16.d:
अलिङ्गी लिङ्गिवेषेण यो वृत्तिमुपजीवति ।
स लिङ्गिनां हरेदेनस्तिर्यग्योनौ च जायते ॥
2.16.m: One without religious marks who earns his livelihood disguised in the garb of an ascetic / takes on the sin of the genuine ascetics and is born in an animal womb.

2.16.s:
baiḍālavratinaḥ pāpā loke dharmavināśakāḥ /
sadyaḥ patanti pāpeṣu karmaṇastasya tat phalam //
2.16.d:
बैडालव्रतिनः पापा लोके धर्मविनाशकाः ।
सद्यः पतन्ति पापेषु कर्मणस्तस्य तत् फलम् ॥
2.16.m: Those who follow the hypocritical cat-vow are wicked, destroyers of religious duty in the world; / they immediately fall into sins; that is the fruit of their action.

2.16.s:
pāṣaṇḍino vikarmasthān vāmācārāṃstathaiva ca /
pañcarātrān pāśupatān vāṅmātreṇāpi nārcayet //
2.16.d:
पाषण्डिनो विकर्मस्थान् वामाचारांस्तथैव च ।
पञ्चरात्रान् पाशुपतान् वाङ्मात्रेणापि नार्चयेत् ॥
2.16.m: One should not honour, even with a mere word, heretics, those engaged in improper conduct, / and likewise followers of the left-handed path, Pāñcarātras, and Pāśupatas.

2.16.s:
vedanindāratān martyān devanindāratāṃstathā /
dvijanindāratāṃścaiva manasāpi na cintayet //
2.16.d:
वेदनिन्दारतान् मर्त्यान् देवनिन्दारतांस्तथा ।
द्विजनिन्दारतांश्चैव मनसापि न चिन्तयेत् ॥
2.16.m: Those mortals devoted to reviling the Vedas, and likewise those devoted to reviling deities, / and those devoted to reviling the twice-born, one should not contemplate even with one’s mind.

2.16.s:
yājanaṃ yonisaṃbandhaṃ sahavāsaṃ ca bhāṣaṇam /
kurvāṇaḥ patate jantustasmād yatnena varjayet //
2.16.d:
याजनं योनिसंबन्धं सहवासं च भाषणम् ।
कुर्वाणः पतते जन्तुस्तस्माद् यत्नेन वर्जयेत् ॥
2.16.m: Performing sacrifices for them, marital alliance, dwelling together, and conversation— / engaging in these, a creature falls; therefore, one should diligently avoid them.

2.16.s:
devadrohād gurudrohaḥ koṭikoṭiguṇādhikaḥ /
jñānāpavādo nāstikyaṃ tasmāt koṭiguṇādhikam //
2.16.d:
देवद्रोहाद् गुरुद्रोहः कोटिकोटिगुणाधिकः ।
ज्ञानापवादो नास्तिक्यं तस्मात् कोटिगुणाधिकम् ॥
2.16.m: Hostility toward a guru is millions upon millions of times greater than hostility toward a deity; / censure of knowledge and atheism are ten million times greater than that.

2.16.s:
gobhiśca daivatairvipraiḥ kṛṣyā rājopasevayā /
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti yāni hīnāni dharmataḥ //
2.16.d:
गोभिश्च दैवतैर्विप्रैः कृष्या राजोपसेवया ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति यानि हीनानि धर्मतः ॥
2.16.m: Through cows, deities, Brahmins, agriculture, and attendance upon a king, / families that are deficient in religious duty become non-noble families.

2.16.s:
kuvivāhaiḥ kriyālopairvedānadhyayanena ca /
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca //
2.16.d:
कुविवाहैः क्रियालोपैर्वेदानध्ययनेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥
2.16.m: Through bad marriages, omission of rites, non-study of the Vedas, / and disrespect toward Brahmins, families become non-noble families.

2.16.s:
anṛtāt pāradāryācca tathābhakṣyasya bhakṣaṇāt /
aśrautadharmācaraṇāt kṣipraṃ naśyati vai kulam //
2.16.d:
अनृतात् पारदार्याच्च तथाभक्ष्यस्य भक्षणात् ।
अश्रौतधर्माचरणात् क्षिप्रं नश्यति वै कुलम् ॥
2.16.m: Through falsehood, adultery, and eating what is inedible, / and practicing non-Vedic religion, a family quickly perishes.

2.16.s:
aśrotriyeṣu vai dānād vṛṣaleṣu tathaiva ca /
vihitācārahīneṣu kṣipraṃ naśyati vai kulam //
2.16.d:
अश्रोत्रियेषु वै दानाद् वृषलेषु तथैव च ।
विहिताचारहीनेषु क्षिप्रं नश्यति वै कुलम् ॥
2.16.m: Through giving gifts to those not learned in the Vedas, and likewise to Śūdras, / and to those devoid of prescribed conduct, a family quickly perishes.

2.16.s:
nādhārmikairvṛte grāme na vyādhibahule bhṛśam /
na śūdrarājye nivasenna pāṣaṇḍajanairvṛte //
2.16.d:
नाधार्मिकैर्वृते ग्रामे न व्याधिबहुले भृशम् ।
न शूद्रराज्ये निवसेन्न पाषण्डजनैर्वृते ॥
2.16.m: One should not dwell in a village surrounded by unrighteous people, nor one that is exceedingly diseased, / nor should one dwell in a kingdom ruled by a Śūdra, nor one surrounded by heretics.

2.16.s:
himavadvindhyayormadhye pūrvapaścimayoḥ śubham /
muktvā samudrayordeśaṃ nānyatra nivased dvijaḥ //
2.16.d:
हिमवद्विन्ध्ययोर्मध्ये पूर्वपश्चिमयोः शुभम् ।
मुक्त्वा समुद्रयोर्देशं नान्यत्र निवसेद् द्विजः ॥
2.16.m: Apart from the auspicious land between the Himavat and Vindhya mountains, / and between the eastern and western seas, a twice-born should not dwell elsewhere.

2.16.s:
kṛṣṇo vā yatra carati mṛgo nityaṃ svabhāvataḥ /
puṇyāśca viśrutā nadyastatra vā nivased dvijaḥ //
2.16.d:
कृष्णो वा यत्र चरति मृगो नित्यं स्वभावतः ।
पुण्याश्च विश्रुता नद्यस्तत्र वा निवसेद् द्विजः ॥
2.16.m: Or where the black antelope roams naturally at all times, / and where there are sacred, renowned rivers, there a twice-born should dwell.

2.16.s:
ardhakrośānnadīkūlaṃ varjayitvā dvijottamaḥ /
nānyatra nivaset puṇyaṃ nāntyajagrāmasannidhau //
2.16.d:
अर्धक्रोशान्नदीकूलं वर्जयित्वा द्विजोत्तमः ।
नान्यत्र निवसेत् पुण्यं नान्त्यजग्रामसन्निधौ ॥
2.16.m: Leaving half a krośa from the riverbank, the best of the twice-born / should not dwell anywhere else that is sacred, nor near a settlement of outcasts.

2.16.s:
na saṃvasecca patitairna caṇḍālairna pukkasaiḥ /
na mūrkhairnāvaliptaiśca nāntyairnāntyāvasāyibhiḥ //
2.16.d:
न संवसेच्च पतितैर्न चण्डालैर्न पुक्कसैः ।
न मूर्खैर्नावलिप्तैश्च नान्त्यैर्नान्त्यावसायिभिः ॥
2.16.m: One should not dwell together with fallen men, nor with Caṇḍālas, nor with Pukkasas, / nor with fools, nor with the conceited, nor with outcasts, nor with the lowest outcasts.

2.16.s:
ekaśayyāsanaṃ paṅktirbhāṇḍapakvānnamiśraṇam /
yājanādhyāpane yonistathaiva sahabhojanam //
2.16.d:
एकशय्यासनं पङ्क्तिर्भाण्डपक्वान्नमिश्रणम् ।
याजनाध्यापने योनिस्तथैव सहभोजनम् ॥
2.16.m: Sharing a single bed or seat, dining in a row, mixing vessels or cooked food, / officiating at sacrifices, teaching, marital relation, and dining together;

2.16.s:
sahādhyāyastu daśamaḥ sahayājanameva ca /
ekādaśa samuddiṣṭā doṣāḥ sāṅkaryasaṃjñitāḥ //
2.16.d:
सहाध्यायस्तु दशमः सहयाजनमेव च ।
एकादश समुद्दिष्टा दोषाः साङ्कर्यसंज्ञिताः ॥
2.16.m: studying together as the tenth, and officiating at sacrifices together: / these are proclaimed as the eleven faults designated as defiling intermixture.

2.16.s:
samīpe vā vyavasthānāt pāpaṃ saṃkramate nṛṇām /
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena sāṅkaryaṃ parivarjayet //
2.16.d:
समीपे वा व्यवस्थानात् पापं संक्रमते नृणाम् ।
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन साङ्कर्यं परिवर्जयेत् ॥
2.16.m: Sin is transmitted to human beings even by remaining in proximity; / therefore, with all effort, one should completely avoid defiling intermixture.

2.16.s:
ekapaṅktyupaviṣṭā ye na spṛśanti parasparam /
bhasmanā kṛtamaryādā na teṣāṃ saṃkaro bhavet //
2.16.d:
एकपङ्क्त्युपविष्टा ये न स्पृशन्ति परस्परम् ।
भस्मना कृतमर्यादा न तेषां संकरो भवेत् ॥
2.16.m: For those who are seated in the same row but do not touch one another, / having a boundary made with ashes, there is no defiling intermixture.

2.16.s:
agninā bhasmanā caiva salilenāvasekataḥ /
dvāreṇa stambhamārgeṇa ṣaḍbhiḥ paṅktirvibhidyate //
2.16.d:
अग्निना भस्मना चैव सलिलेनावसेकतः ।
द्वारेण स्तम्भमार्गेण षड्भिः पङ्क्तिर्विभिद्यते ॥
2.16.m: By fire, by ashes, by sprinkling with water, / by a doorway, and by a pathway between pillars: by these six, a row is divided.

2.16.s:
na kuryācchuṣkavairāṇi vivādaṃ ca na paiśunam /
parakṣetre gāṃ dhayantīṃ na cācakṣīta kasyacit /
na saṃvadet sūtake ca na kañcinmarmaṇi spṛśet //
2.16.d:
न कुर्याच्छुष्कवैराणि विवादं च न पैशुनम् ।
परक्षेत्रे गां धयन्तीं न चाचक्षीत कस्यचित् ।
न संवदेत् सूतके च न कञ्चिन्मर्मणि स्पृशेत् ॥
2.16.m: One should not maintain baseless enmities, dispute, or slander; / one should not report to anyone a cow suckling its calf in another’s field; / one should not converse during ritual impurity, and one should not strike anyone in a vulnerable spot.

2.16.s:
na sūryapariveṣaṃ vā nendracāpaṃ śavāgnikam /
parasmai kathayed vidvān śaśinaṃ vā kadācana //
2.16.d:
न सूर्यपरिवेषं वा नेन्द्रचापं शवाग्निकम् ।
परस्मै कथयेद् विद्वान् शशिनं वा कदाचन ॥
2.16.m: The wise person should never describe to another a halo around the sun, / or a rainbow, or fire from a corpse, or the moon.

2.16.s:
na kuryād bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ virodhaṃ bandhubhistathā /
ātmanaḥ pratikūlāni pareṣāṃ na samācaret //
2.16.d:
न कुर्याद् बहुभिः सार्धं विरोधं बन्धुभिस्तथा ।
आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत् ॥
2.16.m: One should not make enmity with many, nor with kinsmen; / one should not do to others what is disagreeable to oneself.

2.16.s:
tithiṃ pakṣasya na brūyāt na nakṣatrāṇi nirdiśet /
nodakyāmabhibhāṣeta nāśuciṃ vā dvijottamaḥ //
2.16.d:
तिथिं पक्षस्य न ब्रूयात् न नक्षत्राणि निर्दिशेत् ।
नोदक्यामभिभाषेत नाशुचिं वा द्विजोत्तमः ॥
2.16.m: One should not predict the lunar day of a fortnight, nor indicate the lunar mansions; / the best of the twice-born should not converse with a menstruating woman, nor with an impure person.

2.16.s:
na devaguruviprāṇāṃ dīyamānaṃ tu vārayet /
na cātmānaṃ praśaṃsed vā paranindāṃ ca varjayet /
vedanindāṃ devanindāṃ prayatnena vivarjayet //
2.16.d:
न देवगुरुविप्राणां दीयमानं तु वारयेत् ।
न चात्मानं प्रशंसेद् वा परनिन्दां च वर्जयेत् ।
वेदनिन्दां देवनिन्दां प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.16.m: One should not hinder what is being given to deities, gurus, and Brahmins; / one should not praise oneself, and one should avoid censuring others; / one should diligently avoid censuring the Vedas and censuring deities.

2.16.s:
yastu devānṛṣīn viprānvedān vā nindati dvijaḥ /
na tasya niṣkṛtirdṛṣṭā śāstreṣviha munīśvarāḥ //
2.16.d:
यस्तु देवानृषीन् विप्रान्वेदान् वा निन्दति द्विजः ।
न तस्य निष्कृतिर्दृष्टा शास्त्रेष्विह मुनीश्वराः ॥
2.16.m: A twice-born who reviles deities, sages, Brahmins, or the Vedas— / no expiation is seen for him in the scriptures here, O chiefs of sages.

2.16.s:
nindayed vai guruṃ devaṃ vedaṃ vā sopabṛṃhaṇam /
kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ raurave pacyate naraḥ //
2.16.d:
निन्दयेद् वै गुरुं देवं वेदं वा सोपबृंहणम् ।
कल्पकोटिशतं साग्रं रौरवे पच्यते नरः ॥
2.16.m: A man who reviles a guru, a deity, or the Veda along with its auxiliary texts / is cooked in Raurava hell for more than a hundred times ten million kalpas.

2.16.s:
tūṣṇīmāsīta nindāyāṃ na brūyāt kiñciduttaram /
karṇau pidhāya gantavyaṃ na caitānavalokayet //
2.16.d:
तूष्णीमासीत निन्दायां न ब्रूयात् किञ्चिदुत्तरम् ।
कर्णौ पिधाय गन्तव्यं न चैतानवलोकयेत् ॥
2.16.m: During reviling, one should remain silent and not speak any reply; / covering one's ears, one should depart, and one should not look at those [revilers].

2.16.s:
varjayed vai rahasyāni pareṣāṃ gūhayed budhaḥ /
vivādaṃ svajanaiḥ sārdhaṃ na kuryād vai kadācana //
2.16.d:
वर्जयेद् वै रहस्यानि परेषां गूहयेद् बुधः ।
विवादं स्वजनैः सार्धं न कुर्याद् वै कदाचन ॥
2.16.m: A wise man should avoid secrets, and conceal those of others; / he should never enter into a dispute with his own relatives.

2.16.s:
na pāpaṃ pāpināṃ brūyādapāpaṃ vā dvijāttamāḥ /
satenatulyadoṣaḥ syānmithyā dvirdeṣavān bhavet //
2.16.d:
न पापं पापिनां ब्रूयादपापं वा द्विजात्तमाः ।
सतेनतुल्यदोषः स्यान्मिथ्या द्विर्देषवान् भवेत् ॥
2.16.m: One should not speak of sin among the sinful, nor of sin among the innocent, O best of the twice-born; / [in the former case] one acquires equal fault with him, and in the case of falsehood, double the fault.

2.16.s:
yāni mithyābhiśastānāṃ patantyaśrūṇi rodanāt /
tāniputrān paśūnghninti teṣāṃ mithyābhiśaṃsinām //
2.16.d:
यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि रोदनात् ।
तानिपुत्रान् पशून्घ्निन्ति तेषां मिथ्याभिशंसिनाम् ॥
2.16.m: The tears that fall from the weeping of those who are falsely accused / destroy the sons and livestock of those false accusers.

2.16.s:
brihmahatyāsurāpāne steyagurvaṅganāgame /
dṛṣṭaṃ viśodhanaṃ vṛddhairnāsti mithyābhiśaṃsane //
2.16.d:
ब्रिह्महत्यासुरापाने स्तेयगुर्वङ्गनागमे ।
दृष्टं विशोधनं वृद्धैर्नास्ति मिथ्याभिशंसने ॥
2.16.m: For killing a Brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, and union with the guru's wife, / purification is seen by the elders; there is none for false accusation.

2.16.s:
nekṣetodyantamādityaṃ śaśinaṃ cānimittataḥ /
nāstaṃ yāntaṃ na vāristhaṃ nopasṛṣṭaṃ na maghyagam /
tirohitaṃ vāsasā vā nādarśāntaragāminam //
2.16.d:
नेक्षेतोद्यन्तमादित्यं शशिनं चानिमित्ततः ।
नास्तं यान्तं न वारिस्थं नोपसृष्टं न मघ्यगम् ।
तिरोहितं वाससा वा नादर्शान्तरगामिनम् ॥
2.16.m: One should not gaze unnecessarily at the rising sun or the moon, / nor when setting, nor in water, nor when eclipsed, nor when in the middle of the sky, / nor covered by a cloth, nor reflected in a mirror.

2.16.s:
na nagnāṃ striyamīkṣeta puruṣaṃ vā kadācana /
na ca mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā na ca saṃspṛṣṭamaithunam /
nāśuciḥ sūryasomādīn grahānālokayed budhaḥ //
2.16.d:
न नग्नां स्त्रियमीक्षेत पुरुषं वा कदाचन ।
न च मूत्रं पुरीषं वा न च संस्पृष्टमैथुनम् ।
नाशुचिः सूर्यसोमादीन् ग्रहानालोकयेद् बुधः ॥
2.16.m: One should never look upon a naked woman, or a naked man; / nor upon urine or feces, nor at copulation taking place; / being impure, a wise person should not look upon planets such as the sun and the moon.

2.16.s:
patitavyaṅgacaṇḍālānucchiṣṭān nāvalokayet /
nābhibhāṣeta ca paramucchiṣṭo vāvaguṇṭhitaḥ //
2.16.d:
पतितव्यङ्गचण्डालानुच्छिष्टान् नावलोकयेत् ।
नाभिभाषेत च परमुच्छिष्टो वावगुण्ठितः ॥
2.16.m: One should not look upon outcasts, the mutilated, Caṇḍālas, or impure persons; / nor, being impure oneself or having one's head covered, should one converse with another.

2.16.s:
na paśyet pretasaṃsparśaṃ na kruddhasya gurormukham /
na tailodakayośchāyāṃ na patnīṃ bhojane sati /
nāmuktabandhanāṅgāṃ vā nonmattaṃ mattameva vā //
2.16.d:
न पश्येत् प्रेतसंस्पर्शं न क्रुद्धस्य गुरोर्मुखम् ।
न तैलोदकयोश्छायां न पत्नीं भोजने सति ।
नामुक्तबन्धनाङ्गां वा नोन्मत्तं मत्तमेव वा ॥
2.16.m: One should not look at contact with a corpse, nor at the face of an angry guru; / nor at one's shadow in oil or water; nor at one's wife while she is eating, / nor when her clothing is unfastened, nor when she is insane or intoxicated.

2.16.s:
nāśnīyāt bhāryayā sārdhaṃnaināmīkṣeta cāśnatīm /
kṣuvantīṃ jṛmbhamāṇāṃ vā nāsanasthāṃ yathāsukham //
2.16.d:
नाश्नीयात् भार्यया सार्धंनैनामीक्षेत चाश्नतीम् ।
क्षुवन्तीं जृम्भमाणां वा नासनस्थां यथासुखम् ॥
2.16.m: One should not eat together with one's wife, nor watch her eating, / sneezing, yawning, or sitting at her ease.

2.16.s:
nodake cātmano rūpaṃ na kūlaṃ śvabhrameva vā /
na laṅghayecca mūtraṃ vā nādhitiṣṭhet kadācana //
2.16.d:
नोदके चात्मनो रूपं न कूलं श्वभ्रमेव वा ।
न लङ्घयेच्च मूत्रं वा नाधितिष्ठेत् कदाचन ॥
2.16.m:
